answers.question: If we double the length and width of a MOSFET, what happens to its intrinsic gain?

answer.text:
With fixed bias the {\it Early voltage}
is $\propto L$ so to first order

$$A_{0}\equiv g_{m}r_{o}= {g_{m}\over g_{ds}}=
{g_{m}\over I_{D}}V_{A}\approx {2\over V_{ov}}{1\over \lambda}$$

$$V_{A}=1/\lambda = V_{A}^{\prime}L\;\;,\;\;g_{m}/I_{D}=2/V_{ov}$$

for the long channel square law in saturation

$$\eqalign{
I_{D} &= {1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}^{2} \cr
g_{m} &= \mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}= \sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}
      ={2I_{D}\over V_{ov}}\cr
g_{ds}&= \lambda I_{D}\approx {\lambda^{\prime}\over L}I_{D}\cr
r_{o} &= {1\over g_{ds}}={L\over \lambda^{\prime}I_{D}}={V_{A}\over I_{D}}}$$

so that

$$A_{0}=g_{m}r_{o}= {2V_{A}\over V_{ov}}={2\over \lambda V_{ov}}
      \propto {L\over V_{ov}} \tag{1}$$

$$\left|A_{0}\right| = {\sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}WLI_{D}}\over \lambda^{\prime}I_{D}}
      \propto \sqrt{{WL\over I_{D}}} \tag{2}$$

* $A_{0}\propto L$ for fixed $V_{ov}$ or fixed $g_{m}/I_{D}$.
  $W$ drops out to first order. $W/L=$ const $\rightarrow g_{m}=$ const,
  $r_{o}\propto L$.

* $A_{0}\propto \sqrt{WL}$ for fixed $I_{D}$.

In either normal analog biasing:

* fixed $I_{D}$: $W/L\to W/L$ so $V_{ov}=$ const, $g_{m}=$ const,
  $r_{o}\to 2r_{o}$
* fixed $V_{ov}$: $I_{D}\propto W/L=$ const, same.

$$\;A_{0}\to 2A_{0}\approx +6{\rm dB}\;$$

in the ideal long channel case. E.G. $20\to 40$, $26{\rm dB}\to 32{\rm dB}$.

In words: doubling $W$ alone at fixed $I_{D}$ and $L$,
$V_{ov}\propto 1/\sqrt{W}$, $g_{m}/I_{D}\propto \sqrt{W}$,
$A_{0}\propto \sqrt{W}$, $+3{\rm dB}$. Doubling $L$ alone
at fixed $I_{D}$ and $W$, $A_{0}\propto \sqrt{L}$, $+3{\rm dB}$.
Doubling both $\propto \sqrt{WL}\to 2$.

> {\it Remark:} That is for the same bias current or the same
> $V_{ov}$. If you re-bias to keep current {\it density} constant,
> $I_{D}\propto WL$, Eq.2 gives $A_{0}=$ const. In the usual
> textbook language {\it ``scale the device at constant power
> density''} the intrinsic gain is unchanged. If you scale
> $I_{D}\propto W$ at constant $V_{ov}$, $g_{m}\propto W\to 2g_{m}$,
> $V_{A}\to 2V_{A}$, $r_{o}=V_{A}/I_{D}=$ const, $A_{0}\to 2A_{0}$
> again.

In a modern velocity saturated short channel
$g_{m}\approx WC_{ox}v_{sat}$, $r_{o}\propto L/I_{D}$,
$A_{0}\propto L$ still, but $\lambda\ne \lambda^{\prime}/L$
because of DIBL, CLM, mobility degradation etc. so you get
typically $1.3-1.8\times$, not the full $2\times$, for $2L$.
Paid for with $\approx 4\times$ in $C_{gs}\propto WL$ and
$f_{T}\approx g_{m}/2\pi C_{gg}\propto 1/L^{2}$ to $1/L$.

answers.question: Student A says the transconductance of a MOSFET goes up as the overdrive voltage increases. Student B says it goes down. Who is correct?

answer.text:
With a square law in saturation

$${I_{D}={1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}^{2}\;\;,\;\;
V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{T}}$$

$${g_{m}\equiv {\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}\Biggr|_{Q}
 =\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}
 =\sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}={2I_{D}\over V_{ov}} \tag{*}}$$

so that the {\it absolute} $g_{m}$ of a {\it given}
geometry $W/L$ is $\propto V_{ov}$.

> {\it In that sense {\rm A} is right and {\rm B} is confusing
> $g_{m}$ with $g_{m}/I_{D}$.}

$$g_{m}/I_{D} = {2\over V_{ov}}\propto 1/V_{ov}$$

decreases $\propto 1/V_{ov}$ and is the normal figure of
merit in analogue design.

Put in design language: $(*)$ can be read two ways

* {\it $W/L ={\rm const}$:}  Increasing $V_{ov}$ means
increasing $V_{GS}$ and $I_{D}\propto V_{ov}^{2}$.
Then $g_{m}\propto V_{ov}$ increases linearly with $V_{ov}$.
In velocity saturation $g_{m}\to WC_{ox}v_{sat}={\rm const.}$
With vertical field mobility degradation
$\mu =\mu_{0}/(1+\theta V_{ov})$ it goes through a maximum
and can even fall at very large $V_{ov}$.

* {\it $I_{D}={\rm const}$:}  Increasing $V_{ov}$ means
decreasing $W/L\propto 1/V_{ov}^{2}$ at constant current,
the normal low power analogue constraint. Then from $(*)$

$$g_{m}= {2I_{D}\over V_{ov}}\propto {1\over V_{ov}}$$

decreases with $V_{ov}$. In that, conventional,
constant current reading {\rm B} is right.  That is normally
quoted as ``$g_{m}$ goes down with overdrive''.

In the sub threshold $g_{m}=I_{D}/nV_{T}$ so $g_{m}\propto I_{D}$
$\propto \exp \left(V_{ov}/nV_{T}\right)$ still monotonic
increasing with $V_{ov}$ at $W/L={\rm const}$ and
$g_{m}/I_{D}=1/nV_{T}={\rm const}$ maximum.

{\it Remark:}  If the question is taken literally with no
qualification about $I_{D}={\rm const}$, {\rm A} is the
text book square law answer.  Most analogue courses quote
the second form $g_{m}=2I_{D}/V_{ov}$ at $I_{D}={\rm const}$
and call {\rm B} correct.

answers.question: Is the small-signal model of a PMOS device identical to that of an NMOS device?

answer.text:
Yes, topologically and mathematically identical
up to reference polarity.

In large signal they are complementary:

$$I_{D,n} = \frac12 \mu_n C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_n V_{DS})$$

$$I_{D,p} = \frac12 \mu_p C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda_p V_{SD})$$

with $I_{D,n}$ defined $D\to S$ and $I_{D,p}$ defined $S\to D$,
$V_{GS}>0$, $V_{DS}>0$ for NMOS in saturation and $V_{SG}>0$, $V_{SD}>0$ for PMOS in saturation.

Linearize about the $Q$-point $I_D = f(V_{GS},V_{DS},V_{BS})$:

$$i_d = g_m v_{gs} + g_{mb} v_{bs} + g_{ds} v_{ds}$$

$$g_m = \left.\frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{GS}}\right|_Q >0 \;\;,\;\;
g_{mb}= \left.\frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{BS}}\right|_Q \;\;,\;\;
g_{ds}= \left.\frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{DS}}\right|_Q = 1/r_o$$

For PMOS if you keep the *same* terminal voltage definitions $v_{gs}=v_g-v_s$, $v_{ds}=v_d-v_s$ you get

$$i_d = -g_m v_{sg} -g_{mb} v_{sb} -g_{ds} v_{sd} = g_m v_{gs}+g_{mb} v_{bs}+g_{ds} v_{ds}$$

with

$$g_m = \left.\frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{SG}}\right|_Q >0 \;\;,\;\;
g_{mb}= \left.\frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{SB}}\right|_Q \;\;,\;\;
r_o = 1/g_{ds}$$

defined as positive magnitudes. I.e. if you define for PMOS

$$v_{sg} = -v_{gs} \;\;,\;\; v_{sd} = -v_{ds} \;\;,\;\; v_{sb} = -v_{bs}$$

and define $i_{sd} = -i_{ds}$ as the conventional forward current $S\to D$, you get *exactly* the same equation:

$$i_{sd} = g_m v_{sg} + g_{mb} v_{sb} + g_{ds} v_{sd}$$

So the incremental equivalent circuit is indistinguishable.

Low frequency `hybrid-pi`:

```
NMOS:                  PMOS with i_sd, v_sg reference:
 G o---||---o S         G o---||---o S
       |                    |
       vgs                  vsg
       |                    |
       +--[gmb*vbs]--+      +--[gmb*vsb]--+
       |             |      |             |
       +--[gm*vgs]---+      +--[gm*vsg]---+
       |             |      |             |
 D o---+----[ro]-----+ S  D o---+----[ro]-----+ S
       i_d D->S             i_sd S->D
```

Gate open, current source $g_m v_{gs}$ [$g_m v_{sg}$] from drain to source [source to drain], $r_o$ drain-source, $g_{mb}v_{bs}$ [$g_{mb}v_{sb}$] in parallel. With body tied to source $v_{bs}=0$ it disappears in both cases.

High frequency: $C_{gs},C_{gd},C_{gb},C_{sb},C_{db}$ same topology.

> In other words: If you flip the PMOS small signal circuit upside down so $S$ is on top at AC ground $V_{DD}$ and $D$ is on bottom, it overlays exactly on the NMOS circuit with $D$ on top and $S$ on bottom at AC ground $GND$. You cannot tell from the small signal circuit alone whether the device is N or P.

Pedantically: If you insist on keeping $v_{gs},v_{ds}$ and $i_d$ entering the drain as the reference for *both* devices, the PMOS dependent source points the other way and appears as $-g_m v_{gs}$. That is just a sign convention. In magnitude and topology it is identical.

Values of course differ: $g_m = \mu C_{ox}W/L\,|V_{GS}-V_T| = \sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}W/L\,I_D}$, $r_o = 1/\lambda I_D$, so for same $W/L$ and $I_D$, $g_{m,n} \approx 2-3\, g_{m,p}$ because $\mu_n \approx 2-3\mu_p$, but the *model* is the same.

This is why you can analyze CMOS analog circuits with one hybrid-pi / T model for both transistors.

answers.question: Sketch IX versus VX in the circuit in Figure 1.

answer.text:
With the usual sign convention the 2 terminal
device is

$$V_{GS}=V_{DS}=V_{X}\qquad V_{SB}=0$$

so that, apart from the $n^{+}p$ drain diode,

$${\rm cut\;off}\;\;V_{X}<V_{T}\tag{1}$$
$${\rm on}\;\;V_{X}>V_{T}\tag{2}$$

and when it is on

$$V_{DS}=V_{GS}>V_{GS}-V_{T}\tag{3}$$

it is saturated {\it a fortiori}.

$$\eqalign{
I_{D}&=0\;\;{\rm for}\;\;V_{GS}<V_{T}\cr
I_{D}&={{k_{n}}\over {2}}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS}\right]\;\;{\rm for}\;\;V_{GS}>V_{T}\cr
k_{n}&=\mu _{n}C_{ox}W/L\cr} \tag{4}$$

In the conventional long channel square law
with $\lambda \rightarrow 0$

$$I_{D}= \cases{0 & $V_{X}<V_{T}$\cr
{{k_{n}}\over {2}}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2} & $V_{X}>V_{T}$} \tag{5}$$

$$I_{D}={{k_{n}}\over {2}}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{X}\right]\qquad V_{X}>V_{T}\tag{5a}$$

with $V_{T}=V_{T0}$ because $V_{SB}=0$.
$g_{m}=k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)$,
$r_{d}=1/g_{m}\parallel r_{o}\approx 1/g_{m}$.

With the reference polarity drawn in Fig.1

$$I_{X}=+I_{D}\tag{6}$$

so that $I_{X}\approx 0$ for $V_{X}<V_{T}$ and
$I_{X}\propto \left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}$ for
$V_{X}>V_{T}$, a diode like characteristic but
parabolic in the forward direction.  With the
opposite reference polarity $I_{X}=-I_{D}$ the
parabola is in $I_{X}<0$.

> {\it Remark on the sign:}  Many texts draw $I_{X}$
> going {\it into} the $V_{X}$ source, {\it i. e.} to
> the right in Fig.1.  In that case $I_{X}=-I_{D}$ and
> the parabola for $V_{X}>V_{T}$ is in the 4th.
> quadrant, $I_{X}=-k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}/2<0$.

Ideal MOS, $\lambda =0$:

```
IX
 ^                     IX = +ID
 |                    /
 |                   /
 |                  /
 |                 /
 |                /
 |               /
 |              /
 |             /
 |            /
 |-----------o----------------> VX
 0          VT
 IX =0  cut off      IX = kn/2(VX-VT)**2
                     saturation
```

With $r_{o}<\infty $ the parabola is multiplied by
$1+\lambda V_{X}$.

In the ideal MOS picture $I_{X}=0$ is normally
continued for $V_{X}<0$ to $V_{X}\to -\infty $.
In silicon the $n^{+}$ drain $p$ substrate diode
is in parallel with the MOS channel, Fig.2.

```
IX
 ^                     IX = +ID
 |                    /
 |                   /
 |                  /
 |                 /
 |                /
 |               /
 |              /
 |-------------o----------------> VX
 |            VT
 |            0
 |           /
 |          / drain diode forward
 |         / IX = -Is exp(-VX/Vt)
 |        /
 |_______/
        -0.6V
```

For $V_{X}>-0.5{\rm V}$ the diode is off and (5)
holds.  For

$$V_{X}< -V_{F}\approx -0.6{\rm to}-0.7{\rm V}$$

the $p$ substrate - $n^{+}$ drain diode goes
forward and

$$I_{X}\approx -I_{S}\left[{\rm exp}\left(-V_{X}/V_{t}\right)-1\right] <0\tag{7}$$

becomes large and negative, the normal
diode clamp, for $I_{X}=+I_{D}$ to the left.
With the opposite sign convention for $I_{X}$ the
large diode current is $>0$ for $V_{X}< -V_{F}$.
If the parasitic diode is neglected the $I_{X}=0$
plateau is normally drawn to $V_{X}\to -\infty $.

For $V_{X}>V_{T}$ the incremental resistance is

$$R_{X}={{dV_{X}}\over {dI_{X}}}={1\over {g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{o}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m}}}={1\over {k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)}}
\tag{8}$$

decreasing $\propto \left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{-1}$.
At very large $V_{X}$ velocity saturation makes
(5) quasi linear, $I_{X}\propto V_{X}-V_{T}$.

The sketches show zero current until threshold and then a parabolic rise. answers.question: Sketch IX versus VX in the circuit of Figure 2.

answer.text:
With $V_{D}=1{\rm V}$ fixed

$$V_{GS}=V_{X}\qquad V_{DS}=1{\rm V}\qquad V_{BS}=0$$

$$I_{D}=I_{X}{\rm \;in\; magnitude}$$

for the conventional long channel square law
with $I_{X}$ taken as flowing {\it into} the drain.
If you take the reference direction as drawn from
drain to $V_{DD}$ $I_{X}=-I_{D}$.

* $V_{X}<V_{T}$ : cut off

$$I_{X}\approx 0\;\;{\rm exp.\;subthreshold\;if\;you\;want\;to\;be\;fussy}$$

* $V_{T}<V_{X}<V_{DS}+V_{T}$ : $V_{DS}>V_{GS}-V_{T}$ saturation

$$I_{X}= {1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS}\right]\approx {k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\tag{1}$$

$$k_{n}=k_{n}^{\prime}W/L=\mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

parabolic, $g_{m}=dI_{X}/dV_{X}=k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)$.

* $V_{X}>V_{DS}+V_{T}$ : $V_{DS}<V_{GS}-V_{T}$ triode - linear

$$I_{X}=k_{n}\left[\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)V_{DS}-{1\over 2}V_{DS}^{2}\right]
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS}\right]$$

for $V_{DS}=1{\rm V}$ and $\lambda \approx 0$

$$I_{X}=k_{n}\left[V_{X}-V_{T}-{1\over 2}\right]=k_{n}V_{DS}
\left[V_{X}-V_{T}-V_{DS}/2\right]\tag{2}$$

linear in $V_{X}$ with slope

$$g_{m}=k_{n}V_{DS}={\rm const}$$

At the boundary $V_{X}=V_{T}+V_{DS}$

$$(1)=(2)= {k_{n}\over 2}V_{DS}^{2}$$

so $I_{X}$ and $dI_{X}/dV_{X}=k_{n}V_{DS}$ are continuous,
$d^{2}I_{X}/dV_{X}^{2}$ goes from $k_{n}$ to $0$.

In normal $1{\rm V}$ CMOS $V_{T}\approx 0.3-0.5{\rm V}$ so
with $V_{DS}=1{\rm V}$ the boundary is at

$$V_{X,tr}=1+V_{T}\approx 1.3-1.5{\rm V}$$

Up to $\approx 1{\rm V}$ on the gate you stay in saturation
and you see only the parabola.

> {\it If $I_{X}$ is taken as flowing out of the drain
> toward the battery as the arrow is sometimes drawn,
> $I_{X}=-I_{D}$ and the whole picture is inverted below
> the $V_{X}$ axis. The magnitude is the same.}

```
IX  ^
    |                     /  triode : IX = kn[(VX-VT)-1/2]
    |                    /
    |                   /
    |                  / saturation : IX = kn/2 (VX-VT)^2
    |                 /.
    |                / .
    |               /  .
    |              /   .
    |             /    .
    |            /     .
    |           /      .
    |----------/-------.----------------> VX
    0         VT      VT+1V
             cutoff  |<--->|
                     saturation
```

Ideal $\lambda =0$ : flat $I_{D}(V_{DS})$ in saturation.
With $\lambda >0$ the parabola is multiplied by $1+\lambda$ and
has a small positive slope $\propto \lambda$.

For illustration $V_{T}=0.5{\rm V}$, $k_{n}=1{\rm mA/V^{2}}$,
$\lambda =0$:

* $V_{X}<0.5$ : $0$
* $0.5<V_{X}<1.5$ : $0.5(V_{X}-0.5)^{2}{\rm mA}$
* $V_{X}>1.5$ : $(V_{X}-1.0){\rm mA}$

e. {\rm g.} $I_{X}(1.5)=0.5{\rm mA}$, $I_{X}(2.0)=1.0{\rm mA}$,
$I_{X}(2.5)=1.5{\rm mA}$.

Any $V_{T}$ and any $k_{n}$ just scales the $V$ and $I$
axes. Short channel/velocity saturation rounds the
parabola to quasi linear in saturation, but the
cut-off $\to$ quadratic $\to$ linear sequence remains.

answers.question: Can the device shown in Figure 3 act as a current source?

answer.text:
With the conventional 3 terminal symbol the arrow is
the source cum body.  In the figure

$${\rm S}\equiv {\rm B}=X\qquad {\rm D}=0\qquad {\rm G}=0$$

so that for the normal {\it e} -mode device the
transistor is normally {\it off} and in any case the
2 terminal $I_{X}(V_{X})$ is not flat and the
incremental impedance at $X$ is low.  Put $V_{X}$ for
the voltage at the $X$ terminal.

For an $n$ channel {\it e} -mode device, Fig.3 is

$${\rm D}=X\qquad {\rm S}=0\qquad {\rm G}=0\qquad 
V_{GS}=0<V_{T}\tag*{NMOS}$$

so that

$$I_{D}=0\qquad {\rm cut\;off}$$

to first order.  There is no normal ${\rm SAT}$
current to source.  If you call the arrow the source,
Fig.3 is a $p$ channel device

$${\rm S}=X\qquad {\rm D}=0\qquad {\rm G}=0\tag*{PMOS}$$

$$V_{SG}=V_{X}\qquad V_{SD}=V_{X}\tag{1}$$

so that if $V_{X}>|V_{Tp}|$ the device can be turned
on and, with the usual

$$V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}\;\;,\;\;V_{Tp}<0\tag{2}$$

$$V_{X}\ge V_{X}-|V_{Tp}|\tag{3}$$

it is {\it always} {\rm SAT} when it is on.  In the
square law first order large signal

$$I_{X}=I_{S}= {k_{p}\over 2}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD}\right]\tag{4}$$

$$I_{X}={k_{p}\over 2}\left(V_{X}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda _{p}V_{X}\right]\qquad V_{X}>|V_{Tp}|\tag{5}$$

is a strong function of $V_{X}$.  It is the ordinary
diode connected load, ${\rm G}$ tied to ${\rm D}$
through ac ground.  Small signal at $X$, Fig.3 is the
common gate stage with ${\rm G}$ and ${\rm D}$ ac
ground,

$$R_{X}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}
\approx {1\over g_{m}}\ll r_{o}={1\over g_{ds}} \tag{6}$$

so that the impedance presented at $X$ is $O(g_{m}^{-1})$,
the impedance of a forward diode, not the $r_{o}$ of a
current source.  The high impedance is looking into the
{\it drain}, not into the source as drawn.

In the conventional sense of a high $r_{o}\approx
1/g_{ds}$ constant current source the circuit is not a
current source at all; for the normal $n{\rm MOS}$
{\it e} -mode technology it is simply cut off,
$I_{X}\approx 0$.  With a $p{\rm MOS}$ or a depletion
$n{\rm MOS}$ $\left(V_{T}<0\right)$ it will conduct for
$V_{X}>|V_{T}|$ but as a low impedance diode with
$I_{X}\propto \left(V_{X}-|V_{T}|\right)^{2}$.  Apart
from that conventional abuse of language it is often
referred to as a very poor current source.  Interchanging
${\rm S}$ and ${\rm D}$ it is cut off, $V_{GS}=0$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 4.

answer.text:
With ${\rm V}_{DD}$ an $a.c.$ earth the
circuit is the $p$ channel dual of the $n$ channel
${\rm CS}+{R_{S}}$ stage, Fig.1.

> {\it Common source with (unbypassed) source
> degeneration and resistive load ${R_{D}}$ to earth.}
> In $a.c.$ ${R_{S}}$ goes from source to earth and
> ${R_{D}}$ goes from drain to earth.

\begin{center}
{\it Small signal}
\end{center}

Put ${V_{DD}}=0$ for $a.c.$

$${v_{sg}}=v_{s}-v_{g}=v_{s}-v_{in}\qquad 
  v_{sd}=v_{s}-v_{d}=v_{s}-v_{o}$$

for the $p{\rm MOS}$ in saturation

$$i_{sd}=g_{m}v_{sg}+g_{mb}v_{sb}+{v_{sd}\over r_{o}}$$

In the figure the bulk is strapped to the source,
Fig.1, $v_{sb}=0$, $g_{mb}=0$.  If the $n$ well is
strapped to ${V_{DD}}$ put $v_{sb}=v_{s}$ and
$g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in what follows.

$$i_{s}=i_{d}=g_{m}(v_{s}-v_{in})+{v_{s}-v_{o}\over r_{o}}
\tag{1}$$

$$KCL_{S}:\;\;{v_{s}\over {R_{S}}}+i_{s}=0\tag{2a}$$
the current in ${R_{S}}$ is $({V_{DD}}-V_{S})/{R_{S}}$
d.c. from ${V_{DD}}$ into the source.  In $a.c.$
$-v_{s}/{R_{S}}=i_{s}$.

$$KCL_{D}:\;\;i_{s}={v_{o}\over {R_{D}}}\tag{2b}$$
apart from $r_{o}$ the same current flows in
${R_{D}}$ to earth, $V_{o}=I_{D}{R_{D}}$ d.c.

From (2) $v_{s}=-i_{s}{R_{S}}=-v_{o}{R_{S}}/{R_{D}}$ and
with (1)

$${v_{o}\over {R_{D}}}=g_{m}\left(-v_{o}{{R_{S}}\over {R_{D}}}
-v_{in}\right)+{1\over r_{o}}\left(-v_{o}{{R_{S}}\over {R_{D}}}
-v_{o}\right)$$

$${v_{o}\over {R_{D}}}+g_{m}{R_{S}\over {R_{D}}}v_{o}
+{{R_{S}}+{R_{D}}\over r_{o}{R_{D}}}v_{o}=-g_{m}v_{in}$$

$${A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{in}}=
-{{g_{m}{R_{D}}}\over {1+g_{m}{R_{S}}+{{R_{S}}+{R_{D}}\over r_{o}}}}
=-{{g_{m}r_{o}{R_{D}}}\over {r_{o}+{R_{D}}+{R_{S}}+g_{m}r_{o}{R_{S}}}}
\tag{3}}$$

For the $n$ well to ${V_{DD}}$

$$A_{v}=-{{g_{m}{R_{D}}}\over 
{1+(g_{m}+g_{mb}){R_{S}}+{{R_{S}}+{R_{D}}\over r_{o}}}} \tag{3b}$$

In particular for $r_{o}\to \infty $, $r_{o}\gg {R_{S}},{R_{D}}$,

$$A_{v}\approx -{{g_{m}{R_{D}}}\over {1+g_{m}{R_{S}}}}
\approx -{{{R_{D}}}\over {R_{S}}}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;g_{m}{R_{S}}\gg 1
\tag{4}$$

the conventional series feedback result.  Without
degeneration, ${R_{S}}\to 0$, $C_{S}$ bypassed,

$$A_{v0}=-g_{m}{R_{D}}\parallel r_{o}\approx -g_{m}{R_{D}}$$

so ${R_{S}}$ trades gain for linearity, bias
stability and bandwidth.  The sign is inverting:
$v_{in}\uparrow \;\Rightarrow v_{sg}\downarrow \;\Rightarrow
i_{sd}\downarrow \;\Rightarrow v_{o}=i_{sd}{R_{D}}\downarrow $.

With ${R_{L}}$ external, ${R_{D}}\to {R_{D}}\parallel {R_{L}}$.

$$g_{m}= \mu_{p}C_{ox}{W\over L}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)
 =\sqrt{2\mu_{p}C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}\;(1+\lambda V_{SD})$$

$$r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}\approx 1/g_{ds}$$

* Input impedance: gate, $R_{in}=\infty $ at low
frequency.

* Output impedance: with $v_{in}=0$ look into the
drain.  Put $v_{x}$ on the drain, $v_{g}=0$,

$$-v_{s}/{R_{S}}=g_{m}v_{s}+(v_{s}-v_{x})/r_{o}$$

$$v_{s}=v_{x}/\left[1+g_{m}r_{o}+r_{o}/{R_{S}}\right]$$

$$i_{x}=v_{x}/{R_{D}}-i_{s}=v_{x}/{R_{D}}+v_{s}/{R_{S}}$$

$$i_{x}=v_{x}\left[{1\over {R_{D}}}+{1\over r_{o}+{R_{S}}
+g_{m}r_{o}{R_{S}}}\right]$$

$$R_{o}=v_{x}/i_{x}={R_{D}}\parallel \left[r_{o}+{R_{S}}
+g_{m}r_{o}{R_{S}}\right]={R_{D}}\parallel \left[r_{o}
+(1+g_{m}r_{o}){R_{S}}\right] \tag{5}$$

$$\approx {R_{D}}\parallel (1+g_{m}r_{o}){R_{S}}\approx {R_{D}}
\qquad r_{o}\gg {R_{S}}$$

and $R_{o}\approx {R_{D}}$ for $r_{o}\to \infty $.
With $g_{mb}\ne 0$, $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in (5).

D.C. large signal, saturation, $\lambda =0$:

$$I_{D}={k_{p}\over 2}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
={k_{p}\over 2}\left({V_{DD}}-I_{D}{R_{S}}-V_{IN}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}$$

$$V_{O}=I_{D}{R_{D}}\tag{6}$$

$$V_{S}={V_{DD}}-I_{D}{R_{S}}\qquad V_{SD}=V_{S}-V_{O}
={V_{DD}}-I_{D}({R_{S}}+{R_{D}})$$

Saturation $V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$ i. e.

$$V_{IN}\ge I_{D}{R_{D}}-|V_{Tp}|\qquad 
  V_{IN}<{V_{DD}}-I_{D}{R_{S}}-|V_{Tp}|$$

for $V_{SG}>|V_{Tp}|$.  Eq.(6) is quadratic for
$I_{D}(V_{IN})$ and $V_{O}(V_{IN})$ is the usual
parabolic, linearised by $1+g_{m}{R_{S}}$ feedback.

In words: voltage series feedback via ${R_{S}}$.
${R_{S}}$ senses $I_{D}$, feeds back a voltage
$I_{D}{R_{S}}$ in series with $V_{IN}$ to reduce the
effective $V_{SG}$.  Bias stabilisation:
$I_{D}\uparrow \;\Rightarrow V_{S}\downarrow \;\Rightarrow
V_{SG}\downarrow \;\Rightarrow I_{D}\downarrow $.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 5.

answer.text:
This is the $n$ channel {\it common drain}
or {\it source follower} or {\it voltage follower}.
Drain is $ac$ ground, input to gate, output from
source. $100\%$ voltage series feedback.

> In the figure body is strapped to source so
> $V_{SB}=0$. In a $p$ sub discrete process body
> is to the lowest supply, $V_{B}=0$, $V_{SB}=V_{o}$
> and the back gate $g_{mb}$ must be retained.

### 1. Large signal

$$V_{D}=V_{DD}\;\;{\rm ac}\;0\qquad V_{G}=V_{in}\qquad 
V_{S}=V_{out}=I_{D}R_{S}$$

$$V_{GS}=V_{in}-V_{out}\qquad V_{DS}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$$

For $V_{GS}<V_{T}$ $M_{1}$ off, $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=0$.

For $V_{GS}>V_{T}$ in saturation, $\lambda =0$ for
illustration,

$$I_{D}= \frac{1}{2}k_{n}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
      =\frac{1}{2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}\left(V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
      =\frac{V_{out}}{R_{S}} \tag{1}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{T}-\sqrt{\frac{2V_{out}}{k_{n}R_{S}}}$$

i. e. $V_{out}$ follows $V_{in}$ with a $dc$ level
shift $\approx V_{GS0}=V_{T}+\sqrt{2I_{D0}/k_{n}}$.

Saturation condition:

$$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$$
$$V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{T}$$
$$V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{T}$$

normally satisfied. Cut off to saturation transition
at $V_{in}=V_{T}$ for $V_{out}=0$. For $V_{in}$ very
large $M_{1}$ can go triode but normally outside
normal supply range. Load line $V_{out}=I_{D}R_{S}$
intersected with $I_{D}(V_{GS})$ gives $Q$ point
$I_{D0},V_{GS0},V_{out0}$.

With channel length modulation

$$I_{D}= \frac{1}{2}k_{n}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)$$

$$g_{m}= \left.\frac{\partial I_{D}}{\partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
      =k_{n}\left(V_{GS0}-V_{T}\right)\left(1+\lambda V_{DS0}\right)
      \approx \sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D0}}=\frac{2I_{D0}}{V_{GS0}-V_{T}}$$

$$g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}= \lambda I_{D0}\qquad 
  g_{mb}= \frac{\gamma g_{m}}{2\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB0}}}= \eta g_{m}$$

$$V_{SB0}=V_{out0}\;\;{\rm if}\;B\to GND,\;\;0\;{\rm if}\;B\to S$$

### 2. Small signal $ac$ model

Gate $v_{in}$, drain $ac$ $0$, source $v_{out}$.

$$v_{gs}=v_{in}-v_{out}\qquad v_{bs}=v_{b}-v_{out}$$

$$v_{b}=0\;{\rm body\;to\;GND}\;:\;v_{bs}=-v_{out}\qquad 
  v_{b}=v_{out}\;{\rm body\;to\;S}\;:\;v_{bs}=0$$

KCL at source node, currents leaving node:

$$\frac{v_{out}}{R_{S}}+\frac{v_{out}}{r_{o}} = g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}$$

$$g_{m}\left(v_{in}-v_{out}\right)+g_{mb}v_{bs}=v_{out}\left(G_{S}+g_{ds}\right)
\qquad G_{S}=1/R_{S}$$

* Body to source, $g_{mb}=0$:

$$g_{m}\left(v_{in}-v_{out}\right)=v_{out}\left(G_{S}+g_{ds}\right)$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}}=
\frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+G_{S}+g_{ds}}=
\frac{g_{m}\left(r_{o}\parallel R_{S}\right)}
     {1+g_{m}\left(r_{o}\parallel R_{S}\right)} \tag{2}$$

For $r_{o}\gg R_{S}$,

$$A_{v}\approx \frac{g_{m}R_{S}}{1+g_{m}R_{S}}<1$$

$$A_{v}\to 1\;\;{\rm for}\;\;g_{m}R_{S}\gg 1$$

Non inverting, no phase shift. Typically $0.8-0.95$.

* Body to GND:

$$g_{m}\left(v_{in}-v_{out}\right)-g_{mb}v_{out}=v_{out}\left(G_{S}+g_{ds}\right)$$

$$A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+G_{S}+g_{ds}}
      =\frac{g_{m}\left(r_{o}\parallel R_{S}\right)}
            {1+\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)\left(r_{o}\parallel R_{S}\right)} \tag{3}$$

$$\approx \frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}\frac{1}{1+1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}}< \frac{1}{1+\eta}<1$$

With ideal current source load $R_{S}\to r_{oCS}\to\infty$,
$A_{v}\to g_{m}/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\approx 0.7-0.9$.

This is $1/(1+1/T)$ with loop gain $T=(g_{m}+g_{mb})(r_{o}\parallel R_{S})$,
feedback factor $f=1$.

### 3. Terminal impedances

Gate draws $dc$ current $\approx 0$.

$$Z_{in}= \frac{v_{in}}{i_{g}}\approx \frac{1}{s\left(C_{gs}+C_{gd}\right)}\to \infty\;{\rm at\;low\;frequency}$$

$R_{in}=R_{G}$ if a gate bias resistor is added.

Output impedance: set $v_{in}=0$, apply $v_{x}$ at source,
measure $i_{x}$.

$$i_{x}= \frac{v_{x}}{R_{S}}+\frac{v_{x}}{r_{o}}+g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}$$

$$v_{gs}=-v_{x}\;\;,\;\;v_{bs}=-v_{x}\;(B\to GND),\;0\;(B\to S)$$

$$i_{x}=v_{x}\left(G_{S}+g_{ds}+g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)$$

Impedance seen looking into source alone:

$$R_{o}^{\prime}= \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}$$

Including the external $R_{S}$:

$$R_{out}=R_{o}^{\prime}\parallel R_{S}= \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+G_{S}} \tag{4}$$

$$R_{out}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m}}\parallel R_{S}\;\;{\rm no\;body\;effect}$$

$\sim 1/g_{m}= 50-500\,\Omega$ for typical $g_{m}=2-20\,{\rm mS}$,
much lower than $R_{S}$. High $Z_{in}$, low $Z_{out}$:
impedance transformer.

Current gain $A_{i}=R_{in}/R_{out}\gg 1$, power gain
$\approx A_{v}A_{i}\gg 1$ although $A_{v}<1$.

At high frequency $C_{gs},C_{gd},C_{sb},C_{db}$ and load
$C_{L}$ create pole

$$\omega_{p,out}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}}\approx \frac{g_{m}+g_{mb}}{C_{L}}$$

wide band, inherently stable. Input pole $\omega_{p,in}\approx
1/R_{sig}C_{in}$ with $C_{in}\approx C_{gd}+C_{gs}(1-A_{v})$ small
due to bootstrapping.

### 4. Properties

* Voltage buffer: $A_{v}\approx 1$, $R_{in}\to\infty$,
$R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m}$ low, can drive resistive/capacitive load.
* $dc$ level shifter $V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{GS0}$.
* No voltage amplification, large current/power amplification.
* Very linear due to $100\%$ feedback, low distortion for
$g_{m}R_{S}\gg 1$.
* Can source large current $\approx k_{n}(V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{T})^{2}/2$
but can sink only $V_{out}/R_{S}$. Class A. Push-pull complementary
follower needed for symmetric drive.
* Output swing: $0\le V_{out}\le V_{DD}-V_{DS,sat}$,
$V_{DS,sat}=V_{GS}-V_{T}$, limited at bottom by cut off.
Replacing $R_{S}$ by $n$MOS/pMOS current source gives higher
$r_{o}$, higher $A_{v}$, larger swing and better $PSRR$.

In BJT terminology this is the common-collector / emitter-follower.
With $g_{m}R_{S}\gg 1$ it is an almost ideal voltage follower used
as input stage for high $Z_{in}$ and as output stage for low $Z_{out}$
of op-amps, regulators, etc.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 6.

answer.text:
This is the grounded gate, {\it common gate}
stage. $V_{DD}$ is $ac$ ground if
properly bypassed.

$$V_{G}=V_{DD}= {\rm const}\;\;v_{g}=0\;\;V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$$

$$V_{DS}=V_{D}-V_{S}=V_{out}-V_{in}$$

NMOS, ${\cal S}$ at bottom, ${\cal D}$ at top,
body tied to ${\cal S}$ in the symbol so $V_{BS}=0$,
no back gate effect. With body to $GND$ put
$g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

Large signal in saturation, long channel:

$$I_{D}= {k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)$$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}{k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\;\;{\rm sat.}$$

$$V_{GS}>V_{T}\;\;V_{in}<V_{DD}-V_{T}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;I_{D}>0$$

Saturation:

$$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$$

$$V_{out}-V_{in}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T}$$

$$V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{T}\tag*{$V_{T}>0$}$$

$$I_{D}R_{D}\le V_{T}$$

i. e. only for $V_{out}$ high, $I_{D}$ small, is
the device saturated. For $V_{in}$ low $V_{GS}$
large $I_{D}$ large $V_{out}$ falls and the device
goes triode. In triode

$$I_{D}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{T})V_{DS}-{1\over 2}V_{DS}^{2}\right]$$

Small signal $v_{dd}=0$:

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{in}\qquad v_{bs}=0\;\;{\rm body\;to\;}{\cal S}$$
$$v_{ds}=v_{d}-v_{s}=v_{out}-v_{in}$$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}= -g_{m}v_{in}+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{in})$$

$$v_{out}=-i_{d}R_{D}\;\;{\rm at\;}{\cal D}$$

$$-{v_{out}\over R_{D}}=-g_{m}v_{in}+g_{ds}v_{out}-g_{ds}v_{in}$$

$$\left(g_{ds}+{1\over R_{D}}\right)v_{out}=(g_{m}+g_{ds})v_{in}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}={g_{m}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+1/R_{D}}
=(g_{m}+g_{ds})\,R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\tag*{1}$$

$$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}$$

$$A_{v}= {g_{m}r_{o}+1\over r_{o}+R_{D}}R_{D}
=g_{m}R_{D}{1+1/g_{m}r_{o}\over 1+R_{D}/r_{o}}$$

For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$ and $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$

$$A_{v}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}\approx g_{m}\,R_{D}\parallel r_{o}>0$$

non inverting. With body to $GND$, $v_{bs}=-v_{in}$,

$$A_{v}={g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+1/R_{D}}
\approx (g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$$

Current gain $\approx 1$. It is a current buffer,
voltage amplifier.

Input resistance at the source. Put $v_{x}$ at
${\cal S}$, $v_{g}=0$, $v_{d}=v_{x}R_{D}/{\rm etc.}$

$$i_{x}=-i_{d}= -g_{m}v_{gs}-g_{ds}v_{ds}
=(g_{m}+g_{ds})v_{x}-g_{ds}v_{d}$$

$$v_{d}=i_{x}R_{D}$$

$$i_{x}=(g_{m}+g_{ds})v_{x}-g_{ds}R_{D}i_{x}$$

$$R_{in}\equiv {v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1+R_{D}/r_{o}\over g_{m}+g_{ds}}
={r_{o}+R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}r_{o}}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\parallel r_{o}
\tag*{2}$$

Low, $\sim 1/g_{m}$ $50-500\,{\rm \Omega}$ typical.
With $g_{mb}$:

$$R_{in}\approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}\approx {1\over g_{m}}{1\over 1+\eta}$$

With source generator resistance $R_{sig}$ in series
with $v_{in}$ the available gain is divided:

$$A_{v,tot}={v_{out}\over v_{sig}}=A_{v}{R_{in}\over R_{in}+R_{sig}}
\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{sig}}$$

For $R_{sig}=R_{in}=1/g_{m}$, $A_{v,tot}\approx g_{m}R_{D}/2$.

Output resistance at the drain. With $R_{sig}$ from
source to $GND$:

$$R_{o,d}=r_{o}+(1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o})R_{sig}$$

For $R_{sig}=0$, ideal $v_{in}$ source,

$$R_{o,d}=r_{o}$$

At the $V_{out}$ node

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o,d}\approx R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}
\tag*{3}$$

High.

In words: Common gate is the dual of common drain.
Low $R_{in}$, high $R_{out}$, $A_{i}\approx 1$,
$A_{v}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}$ in phase, no Miller
multiplication of $C_{gd}$, wide band, good reverse
isolation. Used as $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ matched
wide band input stage with $g_{m}=1/50\,{\rm S}$,
as current buffer, as cascode device on top of a
common source device to increase $R_{out}\approx
g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$ and bandwidth.

With $R_{D}$ replaced by $p$MOS current source
$R_{D}\rightarrow r_{op}\parallel r_{on}$,
$A_{v}\approx g_{m}r_{o}$.

Poles approx. $p_{in}\approx 1/R_{in}C_{in}$,
$C_{in}\approx C_{gs}+C_{sb}$, $p_{out}\approx
1/R_{out}C_{out}$, $C_{out}\approx C_{gd}+C_{db}+C_{L}$.
Normally $p_{out}$ dominant.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 7.

answer.text:
With ${\cal O}(1)$ the circuit is {\it no}
circuit at all. It is the conventional $CG$ with
the $i/p$ shorted out. Put $V_{b}=V_{B}+v_{b}$,
$V_{in}=v_{in}$ for $sC_{1}>>1$.

$$V_{B}={\rm const}\;\;v_{b}=0\;{\rm for\;ideal\;bias}$$

> {\it DC:}

$$V_{GS0}=V_{B}-0=V_{B}$$
$$I_{D0}= {1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{B}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda \left(V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}\right)\right] \tag{1}$$
in saturation

$$V_{out0}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D} \tag{2}$$

$$V_{DS0}=V_{out0}>V_{GS0}-V_{T}\;\;{\rm for\;sat.}$$

$$V_{out0}\ge V_{B}-V_{T}$$

$C_{1}$ blocks $V_{in,DC}$ from the bias.

> {\it AC: $sC_{1}\to \infty $ mid band:}

$$v_{g}=0\;\;{\rm ideal}\;V_{b}$$
$$v_{s}=v_{in}{Z_{s}\over Z_{s}+1/sC_{1}}\tag{3}$$

but

$$Z_{s}=0\tag{4}$$

by the hard ${\rm GND}$ on the source. So for any
finite source impedance $R_{sig}$ of $V_{in}$

$$v_{s}=0\tag{5}$$

for $sC_{1}\ne 0$. $C_{1}$ is shorted on the right.

Small signal model, $B\equiv S$ so $v_{bs}=0$:

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=0$$
$$v_{bs}=0$$
$$g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}+{v_{d}\over R_{D}}=0$$

$$v_{d}=v_{out}\;\;v_{ds}=v_{d}-v_{s}=v_{d}$$

$$\left(g_{ds}+{1\over R_{D}}\right)v_{out}=0$$

$$\;v_{out}=0\; \tag{6}$$

for any $v_{in}$ to first order. Capacitive
feed through $C_{gd},C_{gs}$ neglected.

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=0\; \tag{7}$$

in mid band and

$$A_{v}(s)=0\;\;{\rm for\;all\;}s\tag{8}$$

to the $1^{st}$ order. Formally with $R_{sig}$

$$A_{v}(s)={1\over sC_{1}R_{sig}+1}{Z_{s}\over R_{sig}+Z_{s}}g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}=0$$

$$R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\;\;r_{o}=1/g_{ds}$$

The $i/p$ source is shorted to ${\rm GND}$ through
$C_{1}$ in the signal band. The current delivered
by $V_{in}$ is

$$i_{in}=sC_{1}\left(v_{in}-v_{s}\right)\approx sC_{1}v_{in}\to
{v_{in}\over R_{sig}}\;\;{\rm for\;}sC_{1}R_{sig}>>1\tag{9}$$

limited only by $R_{sig}$.

$$R_{in}\equiv {v_{s}\over i_{s}}=0\tag{10}$$

seen from $C_{1}$ to ${\rm GND}$. Looked into the
source itself with the ${\rm GND}$ removed

$$R_{in,s}= {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\tag{11}$$

but it is shorted out.

Looked into the drain with $v_{in}=0$

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}\tag{12}$$

$$r_{o}={1\over \lambda I_{D0}}$$

in saturation. With $R_{sig}\ne 0$ on the source

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel \left\{r_{o}\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{sig}^{\prime}\right]+R_{sig}^{\prime}\right\}$$

$$R_{sig}^{\prime}=R_{sig}\parallel 1/sC_{1}\to 0$$

so (12).

In other words the stage is normally a $CG$ stage

$$A_{v,CG}=+{g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\over 1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}} \to +g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}$$

$$R_{in,CG}\approx 1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\;\;R_{out,CG}\approx
\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}\right]r_{o}$$

with $R_{S}$ the bias impedance in the source,
and a $CS$ stage from the gate

$$A_{v,CS}=-g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\;\;{\rm for\;}v_{b}\ne 0$$

but the $CG$ $i/p$ $v_{s}=v_{in}$ has been killed
by $Z_{s}=0$.

> {\it Remedy:} Remove the hard ${\rm GND}$ from
$M_{1}S$. Bias the source with a high $AC$ impedance
$I_{SS}$ - ideal current source, $R_{S}$ to $-V_{SS}$,
etc. - so that $Z_{s}\ne 0$ in $AC$ and $v_{s}=v_{in}$
can develop. $C_{1}$ then is the normal $DC$ block.
With $I_{SS}$ to ${\rm GND}$ the $DC$ value $V_{S0}=0$
is retained but $v_{s}\ne 0$.

answers.question: How many poles does the circuit of Figure 8 have?

answer.text:
With the source {\it a. c.} shorted the small
signal model is a two node model, Fig.1, so that
with ideal supplies

$${\rm det}\left[ {\bf Y}(s)\right] =0\tag{*}$$

is of the second degree in $s$.
In the notation of the figure, with $R_{D}^{\prime
-1}=R_{D}^{-1}+r_{o}^{-1}$,

$${\bf Y}(s)=\left[ \matrix{
R_{S}^{-1}+s(C_{GS}+C_{GD})&-sC_{GD}\cr
g_{m}-sC_{GD}&R_{D}^{\prime -1}+s(C_{GD}+C_{DB})\cr}\right] $$

so that, e. {\it g.} with $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $,

$${\rm det}{\bf Y}= {1\over {R_{S}R_{D}}}+s\left[
{{C_{GD}+C_{DB}}\over {R_{S}}}+{{C_{GS}+C_{GD}}\over {R_{D}}}
+g_{m}C_{GD}\right]+s^{2}\left[ C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{DB}
\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right)\right]=0\tag{**}$$

is the conventional second order Miller denominator.
The $s^{2}$ coefficient is

$${\rm det}{\bf C}= \left|\matrix{C_{GS}+C_{GD}&-C_{GD}\cr
-C_{GD}&C_{GD}+C_{DB}\cr}\right|
 =C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}C_{DB}\ne 0$$

so that the two roots of (**) are finite.
They are normally quoted as the {\it input\/} pole

$$\omega _{1}\approx {1\over {R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+
C_{GD}\left(1+g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime }\right)\right]}}$$

and the {\it output\/} pole

$$\omega _{2}\approx {1\over {R_{D}^{\prime }\left[C_{DB}+
C_{GD}{{1+g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime }C_{GS}/C_{GD}}\over
{1+g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime }}}\right]}}\approx {1\over {R_{D}^{\prime }
\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)}}\qquad g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime }\gg 1$$

the $g_{m}C_{GD}$ term in (**) being the Miller
multiplication.  Formally the network contains the three
capacitances $C_{GS},C_{GD},C_{DB}$ which form the
capacitive loop

$$C_{GS}-C_{GD}-C_{DB}-{\rm gnd}-C_{GS}=0\tag{***}$$

so that

$$V_{C_{GD}}=V_{C_{GS}}-V_{C_{DB}}$$

and only two of the three voltages are independent.
If you want to count the loop (***) as a degeneracy the
network is normally quoted as a three pole network, the
third pole being the degeneracy (***).  With the
capacitance $C_{SB}$ drawn in the figure the network is
formally of order four, order three with the degeneracy
(***).  As drawn $C_{SB}$ is shorted by the ideal
a. c. ground on the source, Fig.1, so that its pole is
pushed to $|s|\rightarrow \infty $,

$$Y_{SB}=sC_{SB}\;\;{\rm in\;parallel\;with}\;\;R_{S}=0\tag{****}$$

and it does not appear in the finite transfer function
$V_{o}(s)/V_{i}(s)$.  With a finite source impedance
$R_{S}^{\prime }$ to ground (****) becomes the third
finite pole

$$\omega _{3}\approx {1\over {R_{S}^{\prime }C_{SB}}}$$

and the circuit becomes formally third order, fourth
order counting $C_{SB}$, second order modulo the
capacitive loop (***).  Loosely the circuit is often
referred to as the three pole, four capacitance, Miller
rolled common source stage.

> {\it Remark:}  Naively counting capacitances the stage
> is often quoted as a {\it three pole\/} stage,
> {\it four pole\/} if $C_{SB}$ is counted, the $C_{GS}-
> C_{GD}-C_{DB}$ loop reducing the order by one and the
> $C_{SB}$ pole being at $s=\infty $ for the ideal
> circuit as drawn leaving the familiar two pole Miller
> denominator (**).

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 9.

answer.text:
With ${\rm M}_{1}$ in saturation put

$${\rm M}_{1}:g_{m},g_{mb},g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}\qquad 
V_{gs}=V_{g}-V_{s}\;\;V_{bs}=-V_{s}\;\;V_{ds}=V_{d}-V_{s}$$

$$I_{d}=g_{m}V_{gs}+g_{mb}V_{bs}+g_{ds}V_{ds}\tag{1}$$

$V_{DD}$ is $ac$ ground.

> {\it Fig. 9 is the conventional $R_{D}$ loaded common gate
> stage with its gate bias taken from the output by the
> potential divider $R_{1},R_{2}$.}  $V_{in}$ is in series
> with the gate voltage $V_{F}$ in the $V_{gs}$ loop and the
> divider is in shunt with the output node.  I. e. voltage
> sampling, series mixing.

In the usual ${\rm mixing/sampling}$ language

* sampling : $R_{1}+R_{2}$ in parallel with $V_{out}$ -
  voltage - shunt - sampling
* mixing : $V_{F}$ in series with $V_{in}$ in the
  $V_{gs}=V_{F}-V_{in}$ loop - series - voltage mixing

so called {\it series - shunt} or {\it voltage - series}
feedback.  With the normal sign convention it is negative:

$$V_{in}\uparrow \rightarrow V_{gs}\downarrow \rightarrow
I_{d}\downarrow \rightarrow V_{R_{D}}\downarrow \rightarrow
V_{out}\uparrow \rightarrow V_{F}\uparrow \rightarrow V_{gs}
\uparrow $$

which opposes the initial $\Delta V_{gs}$.
For $g_{m}R_{D}\gg 1$ the loop gain is $>1$ and the
closed loop properties are essentially set by the passive
divider.

Put for $ac$

$$V_{F}=kV_{out}\qquad k\equiv \beta \equiv {V_{F}\over V_{out}}
\Bigl|_{I_{g}=0}={R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{2}$$

$$1-k={R_{1}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\qquad {1-k\over R_{1}}={1\over
R_{1}+R_{2}} \tag{3}$$

The divider loads the output with

$$R_{L}=R_{1}+R_{2}\tag{4}$$

to ground.  The gate presents no load at the mixing port.

The $a$ - circuit, i. e. the forward amplifier loaded by the
feedback network but with the feedback nulled, is the common
gate stage with $V_{g}=0$, source driven, load

$$R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel R_{L}\parallel r_{o}\tag{5}$$

$$A_{0}\equiv {V_{out}\over V_{\epsilon}}\Bigl|_{\beta =0}
={g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}}
\approx g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\tag{6}$$

$$V_{\epsilon}=V_{in}-V_{F}=V_{in}-\beta V_{out}\tag{7}$$

is the series error voltage, $V_{gs}=V_{\epsilon}$ for
$g_{mb}=0$.  In the ideal $r_{o}\to \infty $

$$A_{0}\approx g_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel R_{L}\right) \tag{6a}$$

and with $g_{mb}\ne 0$

$$A_{0}={g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}}
\qquad R_{i0}={1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}
\tag{8}$$

$$R_{o0}=R_{D}\parallel R_{L}\parallel r_{o}\tag{9}$$

is the output resistance with $V_{in}=0$ and no feedback.

The ideal feedback factor is (2)

$$\beta =k={R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{10}$$

so that the return ratio - loop gain - is

$$T\equiv -\,{\cal R}=A_{0}\beta
={g_{m}k\over g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}}
\approx g_{m}k\,R_{D}^{\prime}
=g_{m}{R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\,R_{D}\parallel \left(R_{1}+R_{2}\right)
\tag{11}$$

$$T\approx g_{m}R_{D}{R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;
R_{L}\gg R_{D}\tag{11a}$$

$T>0$ for negative feedback.

Direct nodal analysis gives the same result without
invoking the two port approximation.  With (1) KCL at the
output node, $V_{DD}=0$ $ac$,

$${V_{out}\over R_{D}}+{V_{out}-V_{F}\over R_{1}}+I_{d}=0\tag{12}$$

$$I_{d}=g_{m}(V_{F}-V_{in})+g_{mb}(-V_{in})+g_{ds}(V_{out}-V_{in})
=g_{m}V_{F}+g_{ds}V_{out}-(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})V_{in}\tag{13}$$

With (2)

$${V_{out}\over R_{D}}+{1-k\over R_{1}}V_{out}+g_{m}kV_{out}
+g_{ds}V_{out}-(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})V_{in}=0\tag{14}$$

i. e. with (3)

$$V_{out}\left[{1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{L}}+g_{ds}+g_{m}k\right]
=(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})V_{in}\tag{15}$$

Hence the exact small signal closed loop voltage gain

$${\cal A}_{f}\equiv {V_{out}\over V_{in}}
={g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{m}k}
={A_{0}\over 1+A_{0}\beta}\tag{16}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty ,\;g_{mb}\to 0$

$${\cal A}_{f}={g_{m}\over R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{m}k}
={g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\over 1+g_{m}kR_{D}^{\prime}}
={A_{0}\over 1+T}\tag{16a}$$

$${\cal A}_{f}= {g_{m}R_{D}R_{L}\over R_{D}+R_{L}+g_{m}R_{D}R_{2}}
={g_{m}R_{D}(R_{1}+R_{2})\over R_{D}+R_{1}+R_{2}+g_{m}R_{D}R_{2}}\tag{16b}$$

In the high loop gain limit $T=g_{m}kR_{D}^{\prime}\gg 1$,

$${\cal A}_{f}\to {1\over \beta}={1\over k}=1+{R_{1}\over R_{2}}>0
\tag{17}$$

the familiar non inverting resistive gain, desensitised to
$g_{m},R_{D}$.  The condition is

$$g_{m}R_{D}{R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\gg 1\qquad {\rm or}\qquad
g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\gg 1/k\tag{18}$$

For finite $T$

$${\cal A}_{f}={1\over \beta}{T\over 1+T}\tag{19}$$

Input resistance.  Let $I_{in}$ be the current forced into
the source terminal.  $I_{s}=I_{d}$,

$$I_{in}=-I_{s}=-I_{d}
=(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})V_{in}-g_{m}V_{F}-g_{ds}V_{out}\tag{20}$$

With $V_{out}={\cal A}_{f}V_{in}$ and $V_{F}=kV_{out}$,

$$I_{in}=V_{in}\left[(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})-{\cal A}_{f}(g_{m}k+g_{ds})\right]
=V_{in}(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}){R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}\over
R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}k}\tag{21}$$

so that

$$R_{if}\equiv {V_{in}\over I_{in}}
={R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}k\over
(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})(R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1})}
={1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\left[1+{g_{m}k+g_{ds}\over
R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}}\right]\tag{22}$$

$$R_{if}=R_{i0}\,(1+T^{\prime})\qquad 
R_{i0}\approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}\tag{23}$$

with $T^{\prime}=g_{m}k/(R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds})$.
For $r_{o}\to\infty ,g_{mb}\to 0$,

$$R_{if}={1\over g_{m}}+k\,R_{D}^{\prime}
={1\over g_{m}}+{R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\,R_{D}\parallel R_{L}
\tag{22a}$$

$$R_{if}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+R_{2}\parallel {R_{D}R_{2}\over R_{1}}
\approx {1\over g_{m}}+R_{2}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{D}\gg R_{L}\tag{22b}$$

$$R_{if}=R_{i0}(1+T)\tag{23a}$$

i. e. series mixing raises the low $1/g_{m}$ input resistance
of the common gate stage by $1+T$.  This is used to obtain
e. g. $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ wide band matching with

$$R_{if}=50\,{\rm \Omega}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+kR_{D}^{\prime}\tag{24}$$

without an inductor.

Output resistance.  Put $V_{in}=0$, apply $V_{x}$ at the
output, measure $I_{x}$.

$$V_{F}=kV_{x}\tag{25}$$
$$I_{d}=g_{m}kV_{x}+g_{ds}V_{x}\tag{26}$$
$$I_{x}={V_{x}\over R_{D}}+{V_{x}-V_{F}\over R_{1}}+I_{d}
=V_{x}\left[{1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{L}}+g_{ds}+g_{m}k\right]\tag{27}$$

Hence the resistance seen at the output node, $R_{D}$ and
$R_{L}$ included,

$$R_{of}\equiv {V_{x}\over I_{x}}
={1\over R_{D}^{-1}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}k}
={R_{o0}\over 1+T}\tag{28}$$

$$R_{o0}=R_{D}\parallel R_{L}\parallel r_{o}\tag{29}$$

The resistance seen looking into the drain alone is

$$R_{od}={1\over R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}k}\approx {1\over g_{m}k}
={R_{1}+R_{2}\over g_{m}R_{2}}\;\;{\rm for\;large\;}T\tag{30}$$

so that $R_{of}=R_{D}\parallel R_{od}$.  Voltage sampling
lowers the output resistance by $1+T$, improves drive
capability and extends bandwidth by the same factor,
$BW_{f}\approx BW_{0}(1+T)$.

In Blackman form $R_{of}=R_{o0}(1+T_{sc})/(1+T_{oc})$ with
$T_{oc}=T$, $T_{sc}=0$ for the $R_{D}$ inclusive port.

Remarks:

* $DC$ the divider provides self bias: $V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$,
  $V_{F}=V_{out}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$, $V_{GS}=V_{F}-V_{S}$,
  $V_{S}=V_{in,DC}$.  Saturation requires
  $V_{out}\ge V_{F}-V_{T}$ and $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$.

* For $T\gg 1$ the circuit is essentially an ideal
  non inverting voltage amplifier of gain $1+R_{1}/R_{2}$,
  input impedance $\approx (1+R_{1}/R_{2})/g_{m}$ and output
  impedance $\approx 0$, with all the usual feedback
  advantages: desensitivity, linearity, $BW$ extension,
  $R_{if}$ up, $R_{of}$ down.  With a single dominant pole
  at the output the resistive loop is unconditionally stable.

Any of (16), (22), (28) with $g_{mb}=0,\;r_{o}\to\infty$
is normally quoted as the ``resistive feedback common gate''
result, e. g.

$${\cal A}_{v}\approx {1+R_{1}/R_{2}\over 1+(1+R_{1}/R_{2})/g_{m}R_{D}}
\;\;,\;\;R_{in}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\left(1+g_{m}R_{D}{R_{2}\over
R_{1}+R_{2}}\right)\;\;,\;\;R_{out}\approx {R_{D}\over
1+g_{m}R_{D}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})}$$

which $\to 1+R_{1}/R_{2},\;R_{2}+1/g_{m},\; (R_{1}+R_{2})/g_{m}R_{2}$
for $g_{m}R_{D}\gg 1+R_{1}/R_{2}$.

minimax_m3.rationale: The answer correctly identifies the circuit as a feedback amplifier with source input, gate driven by the R1-R2 divider, and derives the closed-loop voltage gain in exact form as well as the large-loop-gain approximation 1/β = 1 + R1/R2. It correctly identifies series-shunt (voltage-series) feedback, vgs = vF - vin, and includes body effect refinement without contradicting the essential result. All key elements of the golden solution are present.

It also provides exact expressions with body effect and finite ro, which are acceptable refinements. The feedback interpretation (series-shunt, voltage sampling, series mixing) is correct. Input/output resistance discussions are extra but not required, and they do not contradict the essential result.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 10.

answer.text:
This is the $n-$ channel {\it common drain}
with $n-$ channel active load, Fig.1.

\begin{center}
{\it $M_{1}$ is the driver $M_{2}$ is the $W/L$,
$I_{DSS}$ current source.}
\end{center}

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{B}={\rm const}$$

$$I_{B}={1\over 2}k_{n2}\left( V_{b}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}
\left( 1+\lambda _{2}V_{out}\right) \approx {\rm const}$$

for $M_{2}$ saturated

$$V_{DS2}=V_{out}>V_{GS2}-V_{T}=V_{b}-V_{T}=V_{ov2}=V_{DSAT2}$$

$$I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{n1}\left( V_{GS1}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left( 1+\lambda _{1}V_{DS1}\right) $$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{out}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{T}-V_{ov1}$$

$$V_{ov1}=\sqrt{{2I_{B}\over k_{n1}}}$$

with $k_{n}= \mu _{n}C_{ox}W/L$.
In bulk ${\rm Si}$ the $p-$ substrate is at the
lowest potential, $M_{1}$ suffers body effect if its
$n-$ channel is not in its own $p-$ well strapped to
the source.  In Fig.1 $M_{1}$ is drawn as a 4 terminal
device with $V_{B1}=V_{DD}$ a.c. ground.  If it is
laid out in its own well $V_{B1}=V_{S1}=V_{out}$ and
$g_{mb1}=0$.  Normally

$$V_{BS1}=V_{B1}-V_{S1}=-V_{out}\;\;{\rm a.c.}$$

$$g_{m}={\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}=
\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D}}=k_{n}V_{ov}$$

$$g_{mb}= {\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{BS}}=
\chi g_{m}\qquad \chi \approx 0.1-0.3$$

$$g_{o}=g_{ds}= \lambda I_{D}=r_{o}^{-1}$$

$$r_{o1}={1\over \lambda _{1}I_{B}}\;\;r_{o2}={1\over 
\lambda _{2}I_{B}}$$

Small signal, $V_{DD}$ a.c. ground, $V_{b}$ a.c.
ground, Fig.2.

$M_{1}$ : $v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}$ , $v_{bs1}=-v_{out}$,
$v_{ds1}=-v_{out}$.

$M_{2}$ : $v_{gs2}=0$ , $v_{ds2}=v_{out}$.

$${\rm KCL}\;{\rm at}\;{\rm output:}$$

$$i_{d1}=i_{d2}$$

$$g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{o1}v_{ds1}=g_{o2}v_{ds2}$$

$$g_{m1}\left( v_{in}-v_{out}\right)-g_{mb1}v_{out}
-g_{o1}v_{out}=g_{o2}v_{out}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}} \tag{1}$$

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\over 
1+\left( g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}} \tag{1a}$$

For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$A_{v}\approx {1\over 1+{g_{mb1}\over g_{m1}}
+{g_{o1}+g_{o2}\over g_{m1}}}<1\tag{2}$$

and non inverting.  With the body strapped to the
source $g_{mb1}=0$

$$A_{v0}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}
={g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\over 1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}
\approx 1-{1\over g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}} \tag{3}$$

Normally $0.7<A_{v}<0.95$, $A_{v}\to 1$ for
$g_{m1}\to \infty $, i. e. large $W_{1}/L_{1}$ and/or
large $I_{B}$.  The stage is $100\%$ voltage series
feedback.  The loop gain is $\left( g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)
r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$.

In the conventional notation (1) is a voltage divider
between the impedance looking into the source of $M_{1}$
and the load $r_{o2}$.

$$R_{o1}= {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}}\approx 
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\parallel r_{o1}$$

is the impedance looking into the source of a common
gate device with gate grounded, drain grounded.

With $v_{in}=0$ and a test source $v_{x}$ at the output

$$i_{x}= \left( g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}\right)v_{x}+g_{o2}v_{x}$$

$$R_{out}\equiv {v_{x}\over i_{x}}=
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}
=R_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}
\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2} \tag{4}$$

$$\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}
\;\;{\rm for}\;g_{mb1}=0$$

Typically $50\Omega <R_{out}<1{\rm k}\Omega $ for
$m{\rm A}$ bias.  It can be made small by increasing
$g_{m1}$.

$$R_{in}= {v_{in}\over i_{g1}}=\infty \;\;{\rm d.c.}$$
$$Z_{in}=1/sC_{gs1}\parallel 1/sC_{gb1}\;\;{\rm a.c.}$$

i. e. essentially capacitive.  No Miller multiplication,
$C_{gd1}$ is between input and a.c. ground.

Large signal the circuit is a class $A$ follower.
$V_{out}$ follows $V_{in}$ with a d.c. level shift
$V_{GS1}$.

$$V_{out,max}\approx V_{in,max}-V_{T}-V_{ov1}$$

limited by $M_{1}$ going triode for

$$V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{out}<V_{GS1}-V_{T}=V_{ov1}$$

Normally $V_{DD}\gg V_{in}$ so not limiting.

$$V_{out,min}=V_{DSAT2}=V_{ov2}=V_{b}-V_{T}$$

for $M_{2}$ to stay saturated.  Below that $r_{o2}$
collapses and $A_{v}$ collapses.  The negative slew
rate is limited to $I_{B}/C_{L}$.

Small signal bandwidth is dominated by the output pole

$$\omega _{p,out}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}=

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 11(a).

answer.text:
With the usual square law, long channel
notation the circuit $a$ is the complementary
push pull stage.

> {\it Remark on the symbols:} In $a$ the $n$ channel
> device has its $p$ bulk to $GND$ and the $p$ channel
> device its $n$ bulk to $V_{DD}$ so that
> $V_{BS}=0$ and $V_{T}=V_{T0}$. In $b$ the upper
> device has its bulk to $V_{out}$. It is normally
> drawn as the $p$ device with $V_{SB}\ne 0$ and
> suffers body effect. If taken literally with the
> arrow as source the upper device is an $n$MOS
> source follower, the lower an $n$MOS common source.
> It is not a complementary inverter. It has a
> $V_{T}$ drop on the high level, static current and
> no restoration. In the following $a$ is analysed.
> $b$ is the same topology with $V_{Tp}=V_{Tp0}+
> \gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}-
> \sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]$.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&: n{\rm MOS}\;\;S=GND\;\;D=V_{out}\;\;G=V_{in}\cr
M_{2}&: p{\rm MOS}\;\;S=V_{DD}\;\;D=V_{out}\;\;G=V_{in}\cr
k_{n}&=k_{n}^{\prime}(W/L)_{n}=\mu _{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{n}\cr
k_{p}&=k_{p}^{\prime}(W/L)_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{p}\cr
\beta _{n,p}&=k_{n,p}\cr}$$

$$I_{Dn}= {k_{n}\over 2}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS})
\;\;{\rm sat.}$$
$$I_{Dn}= k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]
\;\;{\rm triode}$$
and complementary for the $p$ device with
$V_{SG}=-V_{GS}$, $V_{SD}=-V_{DS}$, $|V_{Tp}|=-V_{Tp}$.

Put $I_{Dn}=I_{Dp}=I_{D}$.

### 1. Static - switch - operation

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}(n)$ | $M_{2}(p)$ | $V_{out}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $0$ | $V_{GS}=0<V_{Tn}$ OFF | $V_{SG}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|$ ON triode | $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$ |
| $V_{DD}$ | $V_{GS}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}$ ON triode | $V_{SG}=0<|V_{Tp}|$ OFF | $V_{OL}=0$ |

No d.c. path $V_{DD}\to GND$. Static current $\approx 0$
apart from leakage. Rail to rail logic swing. High
$Z_{in}$, low $Z_{out}$ when ON. Ratioless.

For $0<V_{in}<V_{DD}$ both can conduct.

Five regions of the voltage transfer characteristic
$V_{out}(V_{in})$, $\lambda =0$ for first order:

* **I:** $0\le V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ : $n$ OFF, $p$ triode

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}$$

* **II:** $V_{Tn}<V_{in}<V_{IL}$ : $n$ saturation, $p$ triode

$$ {k_{n}\over 2}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
k_{p}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|)(V_{DD}-V_{out})
-{1\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{out})^{2}\right] $$

* **III:** $V_{IL}<V_{in}<V_{IH}$ : both saturation, high gain

$${k_{n}\over 2}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{out})=
{k_{p}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}
(V_{DD}-V_{out}))$$

* **IV:** $V_{IH}<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $n$ triode, $p$ saturation

$$k_{n}\left[(V_{in}-V_{Tn})V_{out}-V_{out}^{2}/2\right]=
{k_{p}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

* **V:** $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|<V_{in}\le V_{DD}$ : $p$ OFF, $n$ triode

$$V_{out}=0$$

The VTC is monotonic decreasing with very steep
transition in III. $dV_{out}/dV_{in}\ll -1$ there.

### 2. Logic threshold $V_{M}$ : $V_{in}=V_{out}$

Normally defined at the point both are in saturation,
$\lambda \approx 0$:

$$ {k_{n}\over 2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
{k_{p}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

$$V_{M}={V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+V_{Tn}\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}
\over 1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}
={V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+V_{Tn}\sqrt{\beta _{n}/\beta _{p}}
\over 1+\sqrt{\beta _{n}/\beta _{p}}} \tag{1}$$

For the matched case $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$,
$k_{n}=k_{p}$ :

$$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

In general $V_{M}$ can be set by transistor sizing.
For equal rise and fall times $R_{on,p}=R_{on,n}$ :

$${(W/L)_{p}\over (W/L)_{n}}\approx {\mu _{n}\over \mu _{p}}
\approx 2-3$$

including $\lambda $ :

$$V_{M}\approx {V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+V_{Tn}\sqrt{\beta _{n}/\beta _{p}}
\over 1+\sqrt{\beta _{n}/\beta _{p}}}
+{\rm small\;}\lambda {\rm \;correction}$$

### 3. Noise margins

$V_{IL},V_{IH}$ defined by $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$ on the
VTC.

$$\eqalign{
V_{IL}&\approx {2V_{out}-V_{DD}+|V_{Tp}|+ (k_{n}/k_{p})V_{Tn}
\over 1+k_{n}/k_{p}}\cr
V_{IH}&\approx {V_{DD}+V_{Tn}+ (k_{p}/k_{n})(2V_{out}+|V_{Tp}|)
\over 1+k_{p}/k_{n}}\cr}$$

First order for $k_{n}=k_{p}$, $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|$ :

$$V_{IL}\approx {3V_{DD}\over 8}+{V_{T}\over 4}\;\;,
\;\;V_{IH}\approx {5V_{DD}\over 8}-{V_{T}\over 4}$$

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\approx V_{IL}$$
$$NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{IH}$$

$\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ for $V_{DD}\gg V_{T}$, i.e. large,
almost optimum $V_{DD}/2$.

### 4. Small signal at $V_{M}$

Both in saturation:

$$A_{v}={dV_{out}\over dV_{in}}\Bigg|_{V_{M}}
=-{g_{m n}+g_{m p}\over g_{ds n}+g_{ds p}}
=-{g_{m n}+g_{m p}\over \lambda _{n}I_{Dn}+\lambda _{p}I_{Dp}}$$

$$g_{m n}=k_{n}(V_{M}-V_{Tn}),\;\;
g_{m p}=k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)$$

$$|A_{v}|\approx {1\over (\lambda _{n}+\lambda _{p})}
\sqrt{2k_{n,p}/I_{D}}\gg 1\;\;20-50\,{\rm dB}$$

So the inverter is a high gain push pull amplifier
when biased at $V_{M}$.

### 5. Dynamic and power

Input capacitance $C_{in}=C_{gsn}+C_{gsp}+C_{gdon}+C_{gdop}$.

Load $C_{L}=C_{dbn}+C_{dbp}+C_{wire}+C_{g,next}$.

Propagation delay, first order $RC$ :

$$t_{pHL}\approx 0.69\,R_{n}C_{L}\approx
{0.69\,C_{L}\over k_{n}(V_{DD}-V_{Tn})}$$
$$t_{pLH}\approx 0.69\,R_{p}C_{L}\approx
{0.69\,C_{L}\over k_{p}(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)}$$
$$t_{p}={t_{pHL}+t_{pLH}\over 2}$$

Short circuit current flows only during the
transition when both conduct, $V_{Tn}<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$.

Power:

$$P_{stat}\approx I_{leak}V_{DD}\approx 0$$
$$P_{dyn}= \alpha C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc,av}$$
$$\approx C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f\;\;{\rm for\;a\;0\to 1\to 0\;cycle}$$

No static power, the essential advantage of CMOS.

In $b$ with $V_{BS,p}=V_{out}-V_{DD}$,

$$|V_{Tp}|=|V_{Tp0}|+\gamma\left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}-V_{BS}}-
\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right)$$

$V_{M}$ is shifted to lower voltage, the $p$ device is
weaker in triode, $V_{OH}$ is still $V_{DD}$ but the
transition is degraded and the output resistance is
higher. Taken literally as $n$-only, $V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$
and the stage draws static current when $V_{in}=V_{DD}$,
i.e. not a restoring CMOS inverter.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 11(b).

answer.text:
In Fig.11a

$${\rm PUN}=M_{2}\;p{\rm MOS}\;\;S=V_{DD}\;\;B=V_{DD}\;\;
{\rm PDN}=M_{1}\;n{\rm MOS}\;\;S=0\;\;B=0\tag{*}$$

$$G_{1}=G_{2}=V_{in}\qquad D_{1}=D_{2}=V_{out}$$

is the conventional ratioless complementary
inverter. $B$ is the bulk. $S-B$ is reverse
biased for $0\le V_{out}\le V_{DD}$,
$V_{T}=V_{T0}$, no d.c. path $V_{DD}\to 0$ in
steady state, $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$, $V_{OL}=0$,
$V_{M}\approx \left[V_{DD}-|V_{Tp0}|
+V_{Tn0}\sqrt{\beta _{n}/\beta _{p}}\right]/
\left[1+\sqrt{\beta _{n}/\beta _{p}}\right]$,
$A_{v}\approx -(g_{m1}+g_{m2})/(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})$.

Fig.11b is the same topology with the $p$ device
turned upside down. With the conventional
designation $M_{1}=n$, $M_{2}=p$ it is $n$ on top
$p$ at the bottom. With the designation of the
figure it is $p$ on top with $S$ and $B$ on the
output side. In either notation the pull up is
no longer a common source device.

> {\it e. g.} $M_{1}$ $p$MOS $D=V_{DD}$ $S=B=V_{out}$
> $G=V_{in}$ - common drain - source follower -
> $M_{2}$ $n$MOS $D=V_{out}$ $S=B=0$ $G=V_{in}$ -
> common source. The dual description $M_{1}$ $n$MOS
> source follower $D=V_{DD}$ $S=B=V_{out}$,
> $M_{2}$ $n$MOS or $p$MOS reversed is completely
> analogous with $V_{Tn}\leftrightarrow |V_{Tp}|$.

Put $V_{Tn}>0$, $|V_{Tp}|>0$,
$\beta =k^{\prime}W/L$.

For the $p$ follower - $n$ common source version

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}:&V_{GS2}=V_{in}\;\;V_{DS2}=V_{out}\cr
M_{1}:&V_{SG1}=V_{S1}-V_{G1}=V_{out}-V_{in}\cr
&V_{SD1}=V_{S1}-V_{D1}=V_{out}-V_{DD}=-(V_{DD}-V_{out})\cr
&V_{SB1}=V_{S1}-V_{B1}=0\cr
&V_{SB2}=0}$$

so that $M_{1}$ has $V_{SB1}=0$, no body effect,
$|V_{Tp}|=|V_{Tp0}|$, but its $S-D$ voltage is
reversed. Normal $p$ operation requires
$V_{S}>V_{D}$, i. e. $V_{out}>V_{DD}$. For
$V_{out}<V_{DD}$ the $p^{+}$ drain - $n$ bulk
junction $D_{B1}$ is forward.

$$V_{D_{B1}}=V_{DD}-V_{B1}=V_{DD}-V_{out}>0.6{\rm V}
\;\;{\rm forward}$$

The $n$-well is at $V_{out}$, the $p^{+}$ drain at
$V_{DD}$. The circuit violates the rule
$B_{p}=V_{DD}$, $B_{n}=0$ for reverse $S-B$.

D.C. large signal, no load:

* $V_{in}=V_{DD}$: $V_{SG1}=V_{out}-V_{DD}<0$
$|V_{SG1}|<|V_{Tp}|$ $M_{1}$ OFF,
$V_{GS2}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}$ $M_{2}$ ON in triode,
$$V_{OL}\approx 0\tag{1}$$
pulled to $0$ through $M_{2}$. Correct low level,
$M_{1}$ is OFF, no static current except
junction leakage if $V_{out}\approx 0$ the
junction $D_{B1}$ is strongly forward and will
try to source current $V_{DD}\to V_{out}$ through
the forward diode. In practice $V_{OL}$ is held at
$0$ by the $n$ device sinking the diode current,
large static $I_{DD}$ and latch up hazard.

* $V_{in}=0$: $M_{2}$ OFF, $M_{1}$ $V_{SG1}=V_{out}$.
To have $M_{1}$ ON need $V_{out}>|V_{Tp}|$.
With $I_{D2}=0$, $I_{D1}=0$ in steady state the
saturation condition gives

$$V_{SG1}=|V_{Tp0}|+\sqrt{2I_{D1}/\beta _{p}}$$

so with $I_{D1}=0$

$$V_{OH}^{({\rm tr})}=|V_{Tp0}|\approx 0.3-0.7{\rm V}\tag{2}$$

i. e. the source follower can only follow the gate
by a threshold. $V_{OH}\ne V_{DD}$. With the
forward diode the node is clamped by the
$p^{+}-n$ diode

$$V_{OH}^{({\rm diode})}\approx V_{DD}-V_{D}\approx
V_{DD}-0.7{\rm V}\tag{3}$$

to $\sim 1.0-2.5{\rm V}$ for $V_{DD}=1.8-3.3{\rm V}$,
still $\ne V_{DD}$ and drawing d.c. current
$I_{F}=I_{S}\exp (V_{D}/V_{T})$. In either case
no rail to rail high.

If the top device is read as $n$MOS, $M_{1}$ $n$
follower $V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{out}$,
$V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$, $M_{2}$ $n$ common source,
the dual result is

$$V_{in}=0: M_{1}\;V_{GS1}=-V_{out}<0\;{\rm OFF},
\;M_{2}\;{\rm OFF}\;{\rm high\;impedance\;node}$$

$$V_{in}=V_{DD}: M_{1}\;{\rm ON},\;M_{2}\;{\rm ON}$$

voltage divider

$$I_{D1}= {\beta_{1}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-V_{Tn})^{2}
      =I_{D2}= {\beta_{2}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{Tn})^{2}
      \;{\rm sat/sat}$$

or triode, giving ratioed

$$V_{OL}=f(\beta_{1}/\beta_{2})>0\tag{4}$$

and

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{Tn0}\tag{5}$$

for $M_{2}$ OFF, $M_{1}$ as source follower.
Again $V_{OH}\ne V_{DD}$, $V_{OL}\ne 0$ in the
all $n$ version, static current
$I_{DD}=I_{D1}=I_{D2}\ne 0$ for $V_{in}=V_{DD}$,
ratioed pseudo $n$MOS logic, $P_{stat}=V_{DD}I_{DD}$.

In general for $0<V_{in}<V_{DD}$ both devices
conduct in the transition region, but the
switching point $V_{in}=V_{out}$ does not exist
in the normal sense. E.g. $V_{in}=V_{out}=V_{M}$
gives $V_{SG1}=0$ for the $p$ follower, so $M_{1}$
is OFF. The VTC is shifted, degraded and low
gain.

Small signal about the high gain region, $M_{1}$
common drain, $M_{2}$ common source,

$$A_{v}={v_{out}\over v_{in}}\approx
-{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}<1\tag{6}$$

for the follower load, versus
$-(g_{m1}+g_{m2})/(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})\gg 1$ for the
correct inverter. $R_{out}\approx
1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})$.

Sketch:

```
Vout
VDD |------\
    |       \  correct
    |        \
VD-Vt|--------\___  malformed VOH ~ VD-Vt or |Vtp|
    |         \  \      or VD-0.7
    |          \  \________
    |           \________\________ Vin
    0           Vtn  VM
```

Noise margins $NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}$ collapse to
$<0.5{\rm V}$, $NM_{L}$ degraded, the high level
will not turn the next $p$ device OFF, cascade
fails, rise time $\tau_{r}\approx C_{L}/g_{m1}$
slow, fall time set by $M_{2}$.

In short Fig.11b is not complementary CMOS.
It is a common drain pull up loaded by a common
source pull down, ratioed, non rail to rail,
with forward $S-B$ junction, body effect and
static power, latch up prone, low gain, poor
$V_{OH}$, $V_{OL}$ and noise margin. It can
invert in the sense $V_{in}=H\to V_{out}=L$ but
$V_{in}=L\to V_{out}=H^{\prime}\ne V_{DD}$ and
is unusable as digital gate.

Correction: interchange $S$ and $D$ of $M_{1}$,
tie $B_{p}=V_{DD}$, $B_{n}=0$, i.e. Fig.11a.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 12.

answer.text:
This is the $n$ channel common source with
$p$ channel saturated - enhancement - load inverter.
Put $K_{n}=k_{n}/2=W_{1}\mu _{n}C_{ox}/2L_{1}$,
$K_{p}=k_{p}/2=W_{2}\mu _{p}C_{ox}/2L_{2}$,
$V_{TN}=V_{thn}>0$, $V_{TP}=-|V_{TP}|<0$.

$$I_{D1}=K_{n}(V_{GS1}-V_{TN})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS1})\;\;V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{TN}$$
$$I_{D1}=K_{n}\left[2(V_{GS1}-V_{TN})V_{DS1}-V_{DS1}^{2}\right](1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS1})\;\;V_{DS1}<V_{GS1}-V_{TN}$$
$$I_{D2}=K_{p}(V_{SG2}-|V_{TP}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD2})\;\;V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{TP}|$$

For $M_{2}$ $G_{2}\equiv D_{2}$

$$V_{SG2}=V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$$

so that

$$V_{SD2}=V_{SG2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{TP}|$$

$M_{2}$ is always saturated when on. $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$.

Small signal $V_{DD}$ is $ac$ ground.

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}\;\;v_{sg2}=-v_{o}\;\;v_{bs1}=0\;\;v_{bs2}=0\;{\rm if}\;B_{2}\to V_{DD}$$

In general

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}$$
$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{mb2}v_{sb2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}$$

with $v_{sb2}=-v_{o}$ if $B_{2}=GND$ and $0$ if
$B_{2}=S_{2}=V_{DD}$.  For the usual $n$-well
$p$MOS $B_{2}=V_{DD}$, $S_{2}=V_{DD}$ $v_{sb2}=0$ $ac$,
$g_{mb2}$ does not appear.  In a $p$ substrate
with $B_{2}=GND$ keep $g_{mb2}$.

At the output node $i_{d1}+i_{d2}=0$:

$$g_{m1}v_{in}+g_{ds1}v_{o}+(-g_{m2}v_{o}-g_{mb2}v_{o}+g_{ds2}(-v_{o}))=0$$

$$v_{o}\left(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\right)=-g_{m1}v_{in}$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{o}}{v_{in}}= -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\; \tag{1}$$

$$R_{out}= \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\parallel \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}} \tag{2}$$

For $B_{2}=S_{2}$ $g_{mb2}=0$.

With $\lambda =0$, $g_{ds}=0$,

$$R_{out}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}$$

$$A_{v}\approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}\approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}} \tag{3}$$

The diode behaves $ac$ as a resistor $1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\parallel r_{o}$ to $ac$ ground.
The stage is inverting, $R_{in}=\infty $ at low frequency,
$C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1-A_{v})$ Miller.

With $g_{m}= \sqrt{2kI_{D}}=\;2I_{D}/V_{ov}$,
$V_{ov1}=V_{GS1}-V_{TN}$, $V_{ov2}=V_{SG2}-|V_{TP}|$,

$$|A_{v}|=\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}}=\frac{V_{ov2}}{V_{ov1}}
      =\sqrt{\frac{k_{n}}{k_{p}}}= \sqrt{\frac{\mu_{n}(W/L)_{1}}{\mu_{p}(W/L)_{2}}}$$

for the same $I_{D}$, independent to first order of $I_{D}$.
Typically $|A_{v}|\approx 5-15$ for reasonable ratio.
Increasing $(W/L)_{1}/(W/L)_{2}$ increases gain but
increases $V_{ov2}$ and limits swing.

Large signal, $\lambda =0$:

* $1.\;V_{in}<V_{TN}$ : $M_{1}$ off, $I_{D}=0$, $V_{SG2}=|V_{TP}|$

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|$$

ideal $V_{OH}<V_{DD}$. Enhancement load cannot pull to $V_{DD}$.

* $2.\;V_{in}>V_{TN}$, $V_{o}\ge V_{in}-V_{TN}$ both saturated:

$$K_{n}(V_{in}-V_{TN})^{2}=K_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{o}-|V_{TP}|)^{2}$$

$$V_{o}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}\,(V_{in}-V_{TN}) \tag{4}$$

linear with slope $dV_{o}/dV_{in}= -\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}=-g_{m1}/g_{m2}=A_{v}$.

Inverter threshold $V_{in}=V_{o}=V_{M}$:

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{TN}+\sqrt{K_{p}/K_{n}}\,(V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|)}{1+\sqrt{K_{p}/K_{n}}}$$

* $3.\;V_{o}<V_{in}-V_{TN}$ $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ saturated:

$$K_{n}\left[2(V_{in}-V_{TN})V_{o}-V_{o}^{2}\right]=K_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{o}-|V_{TP}|)^{2} \tag{5}$$

$$V_{OL}\approx \frac{K_{p}}{2K_{n}(V_{DD}-V_{TN})}(V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|)^{2}\;\;{\rm for}\;V_{in}=V_{DD}$$

small but $>0$, ratioed logic. $V_{OL}\propto (W_{2}/W_{1})$.

The $VTC$ is that of the saturated load inverter, Fig.12.

Frequency response with load $C_{L}$ at output,
$C_{L}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{ext}$:

$$\frac{V_{o}}{V_{in}}(s)= -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+sC_{L}}$$

dominant pole

$$\omega_{p}= \frac{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}{C_{L}}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}}$$

$$GBW\approx \frac{g_{m1}}{C_{L}}$$

Low $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m2}$ gives relatively wide band but low $dc$ gain.
To get high gain the diode load must be replaced by a current source
$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$, $|A_{v}|=g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$.

> *Remark:* With $B_{2}$ not tied to $S_{2}$ keep $g_{mb2}$ in (1)-(2).
> For $B_{2}=V_{DD}$, $S_{2}=V_{DD}$, $g_{mb2}$ drops out $ac$ because
> $v_{bs2}=0$. The textbook form $A_{v}=-g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2})$ is for an $n$MOS diode load where $V_{SB2}=V_{o}\ne 0$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 13.

answer.text:
With the usual square law in saturation the
circuit is the $p-$ channel dual of the $n-$ channel
common source stage with a diode load, Fig.1.

> {\it Remark on the symbol:} $M_{2}$ is the conventional
$p-$ MOS with $n-$ well $=V_{DD}$ , $V_{SB2}=0$.
$M_{1}$ is drawn as a $p-$ MOS used as a two terminal
load, $G_{1}=D_{1}=0$, $S_{1}=V_{o}$.  In a normal
$n-$ well process the $n-$ well of $M_{1}$ cannot be
$0$ for $V_{o}>0.6{\rm V}$ without forward biasing the
$S-$ well diode.  In the normal layout $M_{1}$ is put
in its own well strapped to $S_{1}=V_{o}$ so that
$V_{SB1}=0$.  If the well is strapped to $GND$ as drawn
the conventional $g_{mb1}\ne 0$ must be retained.  Put
$g_{mb1}=0$ for the well $=S$ case.

\begin{center}
$M_{2}$ : C.S. driver \qquad $M_{1}$ : diode load
\end{center}

$$S_{2}=V_{DD}\;\;{\rm ac}\;0\qquad D_{2}=S_{1}=V_{o}\qquad
D_{1}=G_{1}=0\qquad B_{2}=V_{DD}\;\;{\rm ac}\;0\qquad 
B_{1}=0\;{\rm or}\;V_{o}$$

For $p-$ MOS with $|V_{Tp}|=-V_{Tp}>0$

$$I_{D}= {1\over 2}k_{p}{W\over L}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{SD}\right)\tag{1}$$
$$V_{Tp}=V_{T0p}-\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]\qquad |V_{Tp}|=|V_{T0p}|
+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right] \tag{2}$$
$$g_{m}=k_{p}{W\over L}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)
=\sqrt{2k_{p}{W\over L}I_{D}}={2I_{D}\over V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|}$$
$$g_{mb}=g_{m}{\gamma \over 2\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}}= \eta g_{m}
\qquad g_{ds}= \lambda I_{D}=r_{o}^{-1} \tag{3}$$

{\it D.C. - large signal:} Neglect $\lambda $ for the
transfer curve.

$M_{1}$ is diode connected, $V_{SG1}=V_{SD1}=V_{o}$,
$$V_{SD1}=V_{SG1}\ge V_{SG1}-|V_{Tp1}|$$
so $M_{1}$ is saturated iff it is on,

$$V_{o}>|V_{Tp1}(V_{o})| \tag{4}$$

$M_{2}$: $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{I}$, $V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$

$${\rm on:}\;\;V_{DD}-V_{I}>|V_{Tp0}| \tag{5}$$
$${\rm sat:}\;\;V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp0}|\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;
V_{o}\le V_{I}+|V_{Tp0}| \tag{6}$$

In saturation with $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$

$${1\over 2}k_{p1}\left(V_{o}-|V_{Tp1}|\right)^{2}
={1\over 2}k_{p2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{I}-|V_{Tp0}|\right)^{2} \tag{7}$$

i. e. for $V_{SB1}=0$, $|V_{Tp1}|=|V_{Tp0}|=|V_{Tp}|$,

$$V_{o}=|V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{{k_{p2}\over k_{p1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{I}-|V_{Tp}|\right)
=|V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{I}-|V_{Tp}|\right) \tag{8}$$

so that in saturation

$${{dV_{o}}\over {dV_{I}}}= -\sqrt{{k_{p2}\over k_{p1}}}
=-\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}} \tag{9}$$

is the large signal ``gain''.  With $V_{SB1}=V_{o}$,
$|V_{Tp1}|=|V_{Tp1}(V_{o})|$ Eq.7 is implicit,
$V_{o}$ is somewhat lower and the incremental gain is
reduced by the $V_{Tp}(V_{o})$ modulation.

For $V_{I}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp0}|$, $M_{2}$ is off, $I_{D}=0$,
$V_{o}=|V_{Tp1}|$ is the low level.  For $V_{I}$ very
low $M_{2}$ goes triode, $V_{o}\to V_{DD}$.  The useful
inverting amplifier region is $4-6$ where both devices
are saturated.  The nominal bias $Q$ is set by the
chosen $V_{IQ}$ and the ratio $(W/L)_{2}/(W/L)_{1}$.

In the $Q$ point $I_{DQ}$ is given by either side of 7.

{\it Small signal - linear amplifier:}

Put $v_{dd}=0$ ac.  For $p-$ MOS

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{sg}+g_{mb}v_{sb}+g_{ds}v_{sd}\tag{10}$$
directed from $S$ to $D$.

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}:&v_{s2}=0,\;v_{g2}=v_{i},\;v_{d2}=v_{o},\;v_{b2}=0\cr
&v_{sg2}=-v_{i},\;v_{sb2}=0,\;v_{sd2}=-v_{o}\cr
&i_{d2}=-g_{m2}v_{i}-g_{ds2}v_{o}\cr
M_{1}:&v_{s1}=v_{o},\;v_{g1}=0,\;v_{d1}=0,\;v_{b1}=0\;(V_{o})\cr
&v_{sg1}=v_{o},\;v_{sb1}=v_{o}\;(0),\;v_{sd1}=v_{o}\cr
&i_{d1}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}\;\;{\rm with}\;g_{mb1}\ne 0\cr
&i_{d1}=(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}\;\;{\rm with}\;B_{1}=S_{1}\cr} \tag{11}$$

KCL at $v_{o}$, $i_{d2}=i_{d1}$ for $R_{L}=\infty $,

$$-g_{m2}v_{i}-g_{ds2}v_{o}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{o} \tag{12}$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {{v_{o}}\over {v_{i}}}=
-{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}\;
\approx -{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}\;
{\rm for}\;g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1 \tag{13}$$

For the well strapped to source $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v0}=-{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}
\approx -{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}}} \tag{14}$$

With $g_{m}=\sqrt{2k_{p}(W/L)I_{D}}$ at the same $I_{DQ}$,

$$|A_{v0}|\approx \sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}\;
{1\over {1+\eta _{1}}}\tag{15}$$
$$\eta _{1}=g_{mb1}/g_{m1}\approx 0.1-0.3$$

so the stage is intrinsically low gain, $|A_{v}|\sim 1-10$
for reasonable geometries.  Including $r_{o}$,

$$A_{v}=-g_{m2}\left[ {1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}}\parallel
{1\over {g_{ds2}}}\right]
=-g_{m2}R_{o} \tag{16}$$

$$R_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\parallel {1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}\parallel r_{o2}\tag{17}$$
is the small signal resistance seen at the output.
For $B_{1}=S_{1}$, $R_{o}=1/(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})\parallel r_{o2}$.

$$R_{i}= \infty \;\;{\rm gate\;input}\tag{18}$$

$$R_{o}\approx 1/g_{m1}\sim {\rm few\;k\Omega }$$

The dominant pole is

$$\omega _{p}= {1\over {R_{o}C_{L}}}\qquad 
C_{L}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{ext} \tag{19}$$

with Miller multiplication of $C_{gd2}$,
$C_{in}=C_{gs2}+C_{gd2}(1+|A_{v}|)$.

In words: inverting, common source driver $M_{2}$ loaded
by a diode connected $p-$ MOS whose small signal
impedance is $1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})$.  The gain is the
$G_{m}$ of the driver times the load impedance, i. e.
essentially the ratio of the two transconductances.
Body effect of the load, if its well is grounded,
degrades the gain by $1/(1+g_{mb}/g_{m})$.  The circuit
draws static current $I_{DQ}$ and has small output swing
$|V_{Tp}|<V_{o}<V_{I}+|V_{Tp}|<V_{DD}$, and is used as a
wide band low gain level shifter, $p-$ input folded
load, or as the load device in a $p-$ MOS inverter.
High gain requires $g_{m2}\gg g_{m1}$, i. e.
$(W/L)_{2}\gg (W/L)_{1}$, or cascading.

answers.question: Find Rout in Figure 14.

answer.text:
With the bias sources shorted for signals the small
signal circuit is

$$\eqalign{
v_{g1}&=v_{g2}=0\cr 
v_{s2}&=0\cr 
v_{d2}&=v_{s1}=v_{x}}$$

so that, with the conventional ${{i}_{d}}={{g}_{m}}{{v}_{gs}}
+{{g}_{mb}}{{v}_{bs}}+{{g}_{ds}}{{v}_{ds}}$ into the drain,

$${{i}_{d2}}={{g}_{ds2}}{{v}_{x}}\tag{1}$$
$${{i}_{d1}}=-{{g}_{m1}}{{v}_{x}}-{{g}_{mb1}}{{v}_{x}}
+{{g}_{ds1}}\left( {{v}_{o}}-{{v}_{x}}\right) \tag{2}$$

and ${{i}_{s}}=-{{i}_{d}}$

$${{i}_{s1}}+{{i}_{d2}}=0\tag{3}$$

$${{i}_{d1}}={{i}_{d2}}\tag{4}$$

$${{g}_{ds1}}{{v}_{o}}=\left[ {{g}_{m1}}+{{g}_{mb1}}+{{g}_{ds1}}
+{{g}_{ds2}}\right]{{v}_{x}} \tag{5}$$

For a test source ${{v}_{o}}$ at the output

$${{i}_{o}}={{i}_{d1}}={{i}_{d2}}={{g}_{ds2}}{{v}_{x}}
={{g}_{ds1}}{{g}_{ds2}}{{v}_{o}}/
\left[ {{g}_{m1}}+{{g}_{mb1}}+{{g}_{ds1}}+{{g}_{ds2}}\right] $$

$${{R}_{o}}={{v}_{o}}/{{i}_{o}}=
{{{{g}_{m1}}+{{g}_{mb1}}+{{g}_{ds1}}+{{g}_{ds2}}}\over 
{{{g}_{ds1}}{{g}_{ds2}}}} \tag{6}$$

$${{R}_{o}}={{r}_{o1}}+{{r}_{o2}}+\left( {{g}_{m1}}+{{g}_{mb1}}\right)
{{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}={{r}_{o1}}+\left[ 1+\left( {{g}_{m1}}+
{{g}_{mb1}}\right){{r}_{o1}}\right]{{r}_{o2}} \tag{7}$$

where ${{r}_{o}}=1/{{g}_{ds}}=1/\lambda {{I}_{D}}$ in saturation.
For ${{g}_{m}}{{r}_{o}}\gg 1$

$${{R}_{o}}\approx \left( {{g}_{m1}}+{{g}_{mb1}}\right){{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}$$

and, for the connexion as drawn, the $n$ well of $M_{1}$
is strapped to its source, ${{v}_{bs1}}=0$, ${{g}_{mb1}}=0$,

$${{R}_{o}}\approx {{g}_{m1}}{{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}$$

in the familiar

$${{R}_{o}}={{r}_{o1}}+{{r}_{o2}}+{{g}_{m1}}{{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}
={{r}_{o1}}+\left( 1+{{g}_{m1}}{{r}_{o1}}\right){{r}_{o2}}\approx 
{{g}_{m1}}{{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}\tag{8}$$

form.  With ${{r}_{o1}}\approx {{r}_{o2}}={{r}_{o}}$,
${{R}_{o}}\approx {{g}_{m}}r_{o}^{2}$.  E.G. with
${{r}_{o}}=1/\lambda {{I}_{D}}$ and
${{g}_{m}}=\sqrt{2{{\mu }}{{C}_{ox}}W/L{{I}_{D}}}$,

$${{R}_{o}}\approx {{{g}_{m}}\over {\lambda _{1}{{\lambda }_{2}}I_{D}^{2}}}
\approx {{\sqrt{2{{\mu }}{{C}_{ox}}W/L}}\over 
{\lambda _{1}{{\lambda }_{2}}I_{D}^{3/2}}}$$

the conventional cascode multiplication of the
${{r}_{o2}}$ of the current source $M_{2}$ by the
intrinsic gain ${{g}_{m1}}{{r}_{o1}}$ of the cascode
device $M_{1}$.  Putting ${{g}_{m1}}\to {{g}_{m1}}+{{g}_{mb1}}$
is the result with the bulk of $M_{1}$ returned to
${{V}_{DD}}$.  Neglecting ${{r}_{o1}},{{r}_{o2}}$ against
${{g}_{m}}{{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}$ this is normally quoted as

$${{R}_{o}}\approx \left( {{g}_{m}}+{{g}_{mb}}\right){{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}
\approx {{g}_{m}}{{r}_{o1}}{{r}_{o2}}\;\;{\rm for}\;{{g}_{mb}}=0$$

and, for ${{r}_{o1}}={{r}_{o2}}$, ${{R}_{o}}\approx
{{g}_{m}}r_{o}^{2}$.  Any resistance in series with
${{V}_{b1}}$ will divide ${{R}_{o}}$ by that resistance.

answers.question: How do we ensure that M2 is in saturation in Figure 14?

answer.text:
With the normal sign convention $V_{TP}<0$

$${\rm sat}\iff V_{SG}>|V_{T}| \;\;{\rm and}\;\;
V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{T}=V_{SG}-|V_{T}|=V_{ov}$$

for the $p$ channel.  For $M_{2}$

$$V_{S2}=V_{DD}\qquad V_{D2}=V_{X}\qquad V_{G2}=V_{b2}$$

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{b2}>|V_{TP2}| \cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{SG2}+V_{TP2}} \tag{1}$$

i. e. with $|V_{T}|=-V_{T}$

$$V_{X}\le V_{b2}-V_{TP2}=V_{b2}+|V_{TP2}| \tag{2}$$

$$V_{b2}\ge V_{X}+V_{TP2}=V_{X}-|V_{TP2}| \tag{3}$$

and

$$V_{b2}<V_{DD}+V_{TP2}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP2}| \tag{4}$$

so that

$$V_{X}-|V_{TP2}|\le V_{b2}<V_{DD}-|V_{TP2}|\tag{5}$$

is a window $|V_{ov2}|=V_{SG2}-|V_{TP2}|$ wide.
In terms of overdrive

$$V_{SD2,sat}=|V_{ov2}|=V_{SG2}-|V_{TP2}|=V_{DD}-V_{b2}-|V_{TP2}|$$

(1) is

$$V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge |V_{ov2}|\tag{6}$$

$$V_{X}\le V_{DD}-|V_{ov2}|\tag{7}$$

at the edge of saturation

$$V_{X,edge}=V_{DD}-|V_{ov2}|\qquad 
V_{b2,edge}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP2}|-|V_{ov2}| \tag{8}$$

$V_{X}$ is the source of $M_{1}$,

$$V_{X}=V_{S1}=V_{b1}+V_{SG1}=V_{b1}+|V_{TP1}|+|V_{ov1}|
\tag{9}$$

apart from the body effect on $M_{1}$ if its $n$ well is
returned to $V_{DD}$, $|V_{TP1}|\rightarrow |V_{TP1}(V_{SB})|$.
(2) can be written as

$$V_{b1}+|V_{TP1}|+|V_{ov1}|\le V_{b2}+|V_{TP2}| \tag{10}$$

$$V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+|V_{ov1}|+|V_{TP1}|-|V_{TP2}|
\approx V_{b1}+|V_{ov1}|\tag{11}$$

for $|V_{TP1}|\approx |V_{TP2}|$ and

$$V_{b1}\le V_{DD}-|V_{TP1}|-|V_{ov1}|-|V_{ov2}| \tag{12}$$

for the conventional cascode and

$$V_{b1}\le V_{DD}-|V_{TP1}|-|V_{ov1}|-|V_{ov2}|+\Delta $$

with $\Delta \sim 0.1-0.2\,{\rm V}$ margin for the
so called wide swing - low voltage cascode.

In particular $M_{1}$ must itself stay saturated,

$$V_{D1}=V_{out}\le V_{b1}-V_{TP1}=V_{b1}+|V_{TP1}|\tag{13}$$

$$V_{X}-V_{out}=V_{SD1}\ge |V_{ov1}|\tag{14}$$

so that $V_{out}$ rising too high will pull $V_{X}$ up
through the saturated $M_{1}$ and push $M_{2}$ into the
triode.  Normally $V_{b1},V_{b2}$ are generated by a
replica bias branch that tracks $V_{T}$ and $V_{ov}$ with
temperature and process, e. g. in its simplest form

* a $p$ diode $M_{2R}$ : $S\to V_{DD}$, $G=D\to V_{b2}$,
carrying $I_{REF}=I_{D2}$ so that $V_{b2}=V_{DD}-V_{SG2R}$,
$V_{SG2R}=|V_{TP}|+|V_{ov2R}|$,
* in series with a $p$ diode $M_{1R}$ : $S\to V_{b2}$,
$G=D\to V_{b1}$, carrying the same $I_{REF}$ so that
$V_{b1}=V_{b2}-V_{SG1R}$,

or, for minimum headroom, the wide swing connection,
Fig. 3.32 in Razavi, where $V_{b2}$ is generated as
$V_{GS1R}+V_{DSAT2R}$ so that (8) is satisfied with a
$|V_{ov}|$ margin.  Any bias that satisfies (2)-(7) with
$\sim 100-200\,{\rm mV}$ of $V_{ov}$ margin will keep
$M_{2}$ saturated over PVT.  With the $n$ well of $M_{1}$
to $V_{DD}$, $|V_{TP1}|$ in (9)-(12) is increased by
$\Delta V_{T}= \gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right)$, $V_{SB}=V_{X}-V_{DD}$, and
more margin is required.

For hand calculation with $|V_{T}|$ the familiar form is

$$V_{SG2}>|V_{T}|\;\;,\;\;V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{T}|$$

$$V_{X}\le V_{b2}+|V_{T}|\;\;,\;\;V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{DD}-V_{b2}-|V_{T}|$$

Nominally $V_{b2}\approx V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-|V_{ov}|$,
$V_{X}\approx V_{DD}-|V_{ov}|$, $V_{b1}\approx
V_{b2}-|V_{ov}|$ for the wide swing cascode, $V_{b1}\approx
V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-2|V_{ov}|$ for the conventional cascode,
so that $M_{2}$ is at the edge of saturation with
$V_{SD2}=|V_{ov2}|$ of headroom.  Any $V_{b2}$ more
positive than (3) cuts $M_{2}$ off, any $V_{b2}$ more
negative than (3) drives $M_{2}$ triode.
