answers.question: Student A says the transconductance of a MOSFET goes up as the overdrive voltage increases. Student B says it goes down. Who is correct?

answer.text:
With a qualification they are {\it both} right:

$$g_{m} \equiv {\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}{\Bigl |}_{V_{DS}}$$

In saturation, long channel, strong inversion:

$$I_{D} = {1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})$$

$$V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{TH}$$

so for {\it a given geometry} $W/L = {\rm const}$:

$$g_{m}= \mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}(1+\lambda V_{DS}) = \sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}} = {2I_{D}\over V_{ov}} \propto V_{ov}$$

$$g_{m}\propto V_{ov}\propto \sqrt{I_{D}}$$

Turn up $V_{GS}$ on the {\it same} device $I_{D}\propto V_{ov}^{2}$ goes up faster than $V_{ov}$ and $g_{m}$ goes {\it up} linearly with $V_{ov}$. In that usual sense {\bf A is right} and B is confusing $I_{D}$ with a constant.

What B is thinking of is $g_{m}/I_{D}$ or $g_{m}$ {\it at constant bias current} $I_{D}=I_{B}= {\rm const}$, which is the normal analog design constraint.

At $I_{D}= {\rm const}$ to increase $V_{ov}= \sqrt{2I_{D}/\mu C_{ox}W/L}$ you have to {\it shrink} the device $W$, and

$$g_{m}= {2I_{B}\over V_{ov}} \propto {1\over V_{ov}} \propto \sqrt{W}$$

goes {\it down} with $V_{ov}$. The transconductance efficiency

$${g_{m}\over I_{D}} = {2\over V_{ov}}$$

always goes down with $V_{ov}$.

> {\it Fixed $W/L$: $g_{m}$ up with $V_{ov}$. Fixed $I_{D}$: $g_{m}$ down with $V_{ov}$.}

In most text books without qualification ``$g_{m}$ increases with overdrive'' is quoted, so A wins.

{\it Remark:} In weak inversion $g_{m}=I_{D}/nV_{T}$ independent of $V_{ov}$ and in velocity saturated short channel $g_{m}\to WC_{ox}v_{sat}$ saturates independent of $V_{ov}$ for large $V_{ov}$.

answers.question: Is the small-signal model of a PMOS device identical to that of an NMOS device?

answer.text:
For AC purposes yes - topologically and
analytically identical.

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$$

for both devices after linearization about the $Q$-point.

Low frequency `hybrid-pi`:

```
NMOS:                  PMOS:

  G o                  G o
     |                    |
     vgs                  vsg
  S o----o D          S o----o D
     |  /|\ |             |  /|\ |
     |   |  |             |   |  |
     | gm*vgs ro          | gm*vsg ro
     |   |  |             |   |  |
  S o----o D          S o----o D
     |                    |
    GND                  GND AC
```

* $g_{m}= \partial I_{D}/\partial V_{GS}|_{Q}= \sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}W/L I_{D}} = 2I_{D}/|V_{ov}|$
* $r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}$
* $g_{mb}= \chi g_{m}$

High frequency: $C_{gs},C_{gd},C_{gb},C_{sb},C_{db}$ same topology.

The only difference is DC bias polarity and reference direction:

Large signal:

* NMOS: $I_{D}= \frac12 \mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{DS})$ , $V_{GS}>0$, $V_{DS}>0$, current $D\to S$
* PMOS: $I_{D}= \frac12 \mu_{p}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda_{p}V_{SD})$ , $V_{SG}>0$, $V_{SD}>0$, current $S\to D$

Linearized: $v_{sg} = -v_{gs}$ and $i_{sd} = -i_{ds}$ so

$$g_{m}v_{sg}\; S\to D \equiv g_{m}v_{gs}\; D\to S$$

with $g_{m}>0$, $r_{o}>0$ in both cases.

Body terminal: NMOS body $p$-sub to $GND$, PMOS body $n$-well to $V_{DD}$. Both $GND$ and $V_{DD}$ are $AC$ ground, so $g_{mb}v_{bs}$ for NMOS becomes $g_{mb}v_{sb}$ for PMOS, same circuit to ground.

So with source defined as the carrier source terminal, and with $AC$ ground for supplies, you can replace a PMOS in any small signal AC equivalent circuit by the NMOS hybrid-pi / T model with its own $g_{m},r_{o},C_{gs}$ etc. Values differ because $\mu_{n}\ne \mu_{p}$ and $|V_{T}|,\lambda$ differ, but the *form* of the model is identical.

Pedantically it is the mirror image with all DC currents and voltages negated, which is the same linear circuit.

$$I_{X}\approx 0\tag{3}$$
exponential $\propto \exp \left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)/nV_{T}$ in

* $V_{T}<V_{X}<V_{T}+V_{DS}=V_{T}+1{\rm V}$ : saturated,

\left(1+\lambda \right)\approx {1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}

\right]\left(1+\lambda \right)
\approx k_{n}\left(V_{X}-V_{T}-{1\over 2}\right) \tag{5}$$

$${{dI_{X}}\over{dV_{X}}}=k_{n}V_{DS}=k_{n}\times 1{\rm V}= {\rm const.}$$

i. e. the normal $R_{on}^{-1}$ in deep triode.
Continuity at $V_{X}=V_{T}+1$ is preserved:

$$I_{X}\left(V_{T}+1^{-}\right)={1\over 2}k_{n}\cdot 1^{2}
 =k_{n}\left(1-{1\over 2}\right)=I_{X}\left(V_{T}+1^{+}\right)$$

answers.question: Can the device shown in Figure 3 act as a current source?

answer.text:
With the ${\rm 3T}$ symbolism the arrow is the
bulk.  In the normal ${\rm 3T}$ symbolism the arrow is on the
{\it source\/}.  I. e. as drawn the ${\rm ``}S{\rm ''}$ is the
upper terminal, the ${\rm ``}D{\rm ''}$ is the lower, grounded,
terminal and the bulk is strapped to the ${\rm ``}S{\rm ''}$.
For the conventional $n$ bulk ${\rm -}p$ channel symbolism the
arrow points out of the channel, Fig.3 is drawn as an $n$
channel device.  Put in more conventional form it is a grounded
gate, grounded drain common gate stage and the current $I_{X}$
is taken from the source, Fig.1.

> {\it Remark\/}: If you want to call the upper terminal the
> drain the device is a conventional $n{\rm MOS}$ with
> $S$ grounded.  Then $V_{GS}=0<V_{T}$ and the device is {\it
> off\/} in the conventional $n{\rm MOS}$ sense.  With the
> $p{\rm MOS}$ symbolism $V_{SG}=0<|V_{T}|$ and the device is
> off.  In either case you get no {\it saturated\/} current.

Put with the source up the large signal operation is, for a
$p$ channel device with $|V_{T}|=V_{Tp}$,

$$V_{S}=V_{X}\qquad V_{G}=0\qquad V_{D}=0\tag*{p}$$

$$V_{SG}=V_{X}\qquad V_{SD}=V_{X}$$

so that, apart from the sign, the conventional saturation
criterion

$$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}\tag*{n}$$

$$V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}-|V_{T}|\tag*{p}$$

is

$$V_{X}\ge V_{X}-|V_{T}|$$

and is formally satisfied for any $V_{X}>|V_{T}|$ and

$$I_{X}=I_{S}=I_{D}= {1\over 2}k_{p}\left(V_{X}-|V_{T}|\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{X}\right]\tag*{p}$$

for $V_{X}>|V_{T}|$ and $I_{X}=0$ for $V_{X}<|V_{T}|$.
For the $n$ channel symbolism as drawn the bulk is the upper
terminal.  I. e. $B\equiv S\equiv V_{X}$, $D\equiv 0$.  For
$V_{X}>0$ the $B-D$ $p-n$ junction is forward biased and MOS
action is lost.  For $V_{X}<0$

$$V_{GS}=-V_{X}\qquad V_{DS}=-V_{X}\tag*{n}$$

$$I_{X}= {1\over 2}k_{n}\left(-V_{X}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1-\lambda V_{X}\right]\qquad -V_{X}>V_{T}\tag*{n}$$

In either case the device is {\it diode connected\/},
$G\equiv D$ a. c. ground, Fig.1.  Its small signal impedance
looking into the $S$, the $I_{X}$ terminal, is the conventional
common gate impedance with $R_{D}=0$, $R_{G}=0$,

$$R_{X}={R_{D}\parallel r_{o}+{1\over {g_{m}+g_{mb}}}\over {1+
{{R_{G}}\over {r_{o}}}}}\approx {1\over {g_{m}+g_{mb}}}\parallel
r_{o}\approx {1\over {g_{m}}}\tag{1}$$

i. e. a low impedance diode of $O\left(g_{m}^{-1}\right)$,
Fig.2, not the $r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$ high impedance normally
meant by a current source.  In the conventional language the
device is not in saturation as a current source; the current
is a strong, square law, function of the terminal voltage
$V_{X}$.  With $r_{o}<\infty $ the large signal $I_{X}(V_{X})$
is of course finite slope $1/r_{o}$ in saturation, but the
incremental slope at the $I_{X}$ terminal is dominated by
$g_{m}$.

Looking into the {\it drain\/}, the grounded terminal in
Fig.3, you do get the conventional

$$R_{D}\approx r_{o}\tag{2}$$

high impedance current source.  As normally drawn, with $I_{X}$
taken from the source/bulk terminal, it is a very poor,
low impedance, diode connected load.  In the ideal
$\lambda =0$ square law picture it can be said to be
{\it saturated\/} for $|V_{X}|>|V_{T}|$ of the correct
polarity, $V_{X}>|V_{Tp}|$ for $p{\rm MOS}$, $V_{X}<-V_{Tn}$
for $n{\rm MOS}$, but with the low incremental impedance
(1).

For the literal $n{\rm MOS}$ $B$ grounded symbolism the
device is cut off, $V_{GS}=0$, for $V_{X}>0$ and the $B-S$
diode forward biases for $V_{X}<0$.

> {\it N. B.\/}: With $\lambda \ne 0$ the usual
> $r_{o}^{-1}=\lambda I_{D}$ finite output conductance is of
> course present, so that in the large signal sense $I_{X}$ is
> never quite independent of $V_{X}$.  What is normally meant
> by a current source is $R_{X}\approx r_{o}\gg g_{m}^{-1}$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 4.

answer.text:
With ${\rm AC}$ ground on $V_{DD}$ this is the
$p$ version of the $n$ channel

$${\rm CS}+R_{S}$$

i. e. a series feedback common source voltage amplifier.
Put $v_{DD}=0$ for signals.

> {\it Remark:} On the symbol as drawn the $n$ well is
strapped to the source so $V_{SB}=0$ and $g_{mb}=0$.
If the well is strapped to $V_{DD}$ put $g_{m}\rightarrow
g_{m}+g_{mb}$ and $R_{S}\rightarrow R_{S}\parallel r_{well}$
in what follows.

$$V_{S}=V_{DD}-I_{S}R_{S}\qquad V_{D}=I_{D}R_{D}=V_{out}$$
$$V_{SG}=V_{S}-V_{in}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{S}-V_{in}$$

in saturation, long channel

$$I_{D}\approx {1\over 2}k_{p}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD}\right] \tag{DC}$$

$$V_{SD}=V_{S}-V_{D}=V_{DD}-I_{D}(R_{S}+R_{D})$$

so that e. g.

$$I_{D}={k_{p}\over 2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-I_{D}R_{S}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}$$

for $\lambda =0$, a quadratic for $I_{D}(V_{in})$.
$$V_{out}=I_{D}R_{D}$$

Saturation for the $p$:

$$V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}=V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$$

$$V_{DD}-I_{D}(R_{S}+R_{D})\ge V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{S}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|$$

i. e. $V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}|$ to first order.
For $V_{in}\rightarrow V_{DD}$ the device cuts off,
$I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=0$. For $V_{in}$ low enough the
device goes triode.

Small signal, $v_{sg}=v_{s}-v_{in}$, $v_{sd}=v_{s}-v_{d}$,
$g_{m}=\partial I_{D}/\partial V_{SG}$, $r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$,
put $V_{DD}=0$ AC:

$$\eqalign{
{\rm S}:&{v_{s}\over R_{S}}+{v_{s}-v_{d}\over r_{o}}+g_{m}v_{sg}=0\cr
{\rm D}:&{v_{d}\over R_{D}}+{v_{d}-v_{s}\over r_{o}}-g_{m}v_{sg}=0\cr
&v_{sg}=v_{s}-v_{in}}$$

$$v_{s}/R_{S}+v_{d}/R_{D}=0$$

in the usual small signal model $r_{o}$ between $S$ and $D$
and $g_{m}v_{sg}$ from $S$ to $D$.

Solving,

$$v_{d}\left[{1\over R_{D}}+{1\over r_{o}}\right]
+v_{s}\left[-{1\over r_{o}}-g_{m}\right]=-g_{m}v_{in}$$

with $v_{s}=-R_{S}v_{d}/R_{D}$,

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}={v_{d}\over v_{in}}
=-{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}+{R_{S}+R_{D}\over r_{o}}}
{r_{o}\over r_{o}}$$

i. e. with $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $,

$$A_{v}\approx -{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}}=-G_{m}R_{D}$$

inverting. $G_{m}=g_{m}/(1+g_{m}R_{S})$ is the
degenerated transconductance. For $g_{m}R_{S}\gg 1$

$$A_{v}\rightarrow -{R_{D}\over R_{S}}$$

independent of $g_{m}$, the usual series feedback
desensitisation and linearisation at the expense of gain.
Without degeneration $R_{S}=0$,

$$A_{v0}=-g_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\right)$$

With $r_{o}$ finite the more exact form is

$$A_{v}=-g_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel R_{oD}\right)
{1\over 1+G_{m}R_{S}}\approx -{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}}
{1\over 1+(R_{D}+R_{S})/g_{m}r_{o}R_{S}}$$

Normally $r_{o}\gg R_{D},R_{S}$ and the $r_{o}$ correction
is negligible.

With body effect, $g_{m}v_{sg}\rightarrow g_{m}v_{sg}
+g_{mb}v_{sb}$, $v_{sb}=v_{s}$ if body to $V_{DD}$,
$g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in the denominator:

$$A_{v}\approx -{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}}$$

$$R_{in}= \infty \;{\rm at\;LF}$$

the gate draws no DC current, $C_{gs},C_{gd}$ Miller
multiplied at HF.

Output resistance, $v_{in}=0$, $v_{x}$ on $v_{out}$,
$i_{x}$ into $v_{out}$:

$${v_{s}\over R_{S}}+{v_{s}-v_{x}\over r_{o}}+g_{m}v_{s}=0$$
$$i_{x}={v_{x}\over R_{D}}+{v_{x}-v_{s}\over r_{o}}-g_{m}v_{s}$$

$$R_{out}\equiv {v_{x}\over i_{x}}=R_{D}\parallel
\left[\,r_{o}+R_{S}+g_{m}r_{o}R_{S}\,\right]
=R_{D}\parallel \left[\,r_{o}+(1+g_{m}r_{o})R_{S}\,\right]$$

$$\approx R_{D}\parallel g_{m}r_{o}R_{S}\approx R_{D}\qquad 
g_{m}r_{o}R_{S}\gg R_{D}$$

With body to $V_{DD}$: $g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$,

$$R_{oD}=r_{o}+(1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o})R_{S}$$

So the degeneration raises the impedance looking into the
drain by $\approx g_{m}r_{o}R_{S}$ but it is normally
swamped by $R_{D}$.

In words: inverting voltage amplifier, high $R_{in}$,
moderate $R_{out}\approx R_{D}$, voltage gain reduced
from $g_{m}R_{D}$ to $g_{m}R_{D}/(1+g_{m}R_{S})$,
much more linear, much less $g_{m}$ sensitive, larger
bandwidth, series feedback. Bypass $R_{S}$ with $C_{S}$
to get $A_{v0}$ back for AC.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 5.

answer.text:
This is the $n-$ channel {\it common drain}
or {\it source follower} or {\it grounded drain}
voltage buffer. $D$ is at $a.c.$ ground $V_{DD}$,
input at $G$, output at $S$ on $R_{S}$.

$$V_{o}=I_{D}R_{S}\qquad V_{GS}=V_{i}-V_{o}$$

$$I_{D}= \frac{k_{n}}{2}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)\;\;{\rm sat.}$$
$$k_{n}= \mu _{n}C_{ox}W/L\qquad 
g_{m}= \left.\frac{\partial I_{D}}{\partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
=k_{n}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)=\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D}}$$
$$g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}= \lambda I_{D}\qquad 
g_{mb}= \eta g_{m}\;\; \eta \approx 0.1-0.3$$

In the figure the bulk is strapped to the source,
$g_{mb}=0$. If the bulk is to $GND$, $g_{mb}\ne 0$.

> {\it D.C. large signal:}

$M_{1}$ off for $V_{i}<V_{T}$ , $V_{o}=0$.

For $V_{i}>V_{T}$

$$I_{D}=V_{o}/R_{S}= \frac{k_{n}}{2}\left(V_{i}-V_{o}-V_{T}\right)^{2}$$

$$V_{o}=V_{i}-V_{T}-\sqrt{\frac{2V_{o}}{k_{n}R_{S}}}$$

i. e. $V_{o}$ {\it follows} $V_{i}$ with a $d.c.$
level shift

$$V_{GS}=V_{T}+\sqrt{2I_{D}/k_{n}}$$

Saturation condition $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$:

$$V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{i}-V_{o}-V_{T}\;\; \Rightarrow\;\;
V_{i}\le V_{DD}+V_{T}$$

so normally always saturated until $V_{i}$ very large.
Cut off on negative going $V_{i}$ limits negative
swing to $0$. Positive swing limited to
$V_{DD}-V_{DS,sat}$. With $R_{S}$ to $GND$ it can
source $I_{D,max}\approx k_{n}(V_{DD}-V_{T})^{2}/2$
but can only sink $V_{o}/R_{S}$. For large
symmetrical swing $R_{S}$ is normally replaced by
a current source $I_{SS}$ with $r_{oS}\gg R_{S}$.

Small signal $a.c.$ equivalent, $V_{DD}=0$:

```
          D o--0
              |
          +---+
          |  _|_
      Cgd | |   | Cgs
  G o-----| |---+----o S
          | |_| |    |
          |   |      |
         vgs gm.vgs gmb.vbs ro
          |   |      |
          +---+------+
              |
             Rs
              |
             GND
```

$$v_{gs}=v_{i}-v_{o}\qquad v_{bs}=v_{b}-v_{o}$$
$$v_{ds}= -v_{o}\;\;{\rm for}\;v_{d}=0$$

KCL at $S$:

$$g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}=v_{o}/R_{S}$$

With $v_{b}=0$:

$$g_{m}(v_{i}-v_{o})-g_{mb}v_{o}-g_{ds}v_{o}=v_{o}/R_{S}$$

$$g_{m}v_{i}=v_{o}\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+R_{S}^{-1}\right)$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{o}}{v_{i}}=
\frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+R_{S}^{-1}}\;$$

$$A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}(r_{o}\parallel R_{S})}
{1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})(r_{o}\parallel R_{S})}>0$$

In most text book form:

* Bulk to source, $g_{mb}=0$, $\lambda =0$, $r_{o}\to\infty$:

$$\;A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}R_{S}}{1+g_{m}R_{S}}=
\frac{1}{1+1/g_{m}R_{S}}<1\;$$

$$A_{v}\to 1\;\;{\rm for}\;\;g_{m}R_{S}\gg 1$$

* With $r_{o}$ but $g_{mb}=0$:

$$\;A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}(r_{o}\parallel R_{S})}
{1+g_{m}(r_{o}\parallel R_{S})}\;$$

* With bulk to $GND$:

$$\;A_{v}\approx \frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}\approx
\frac{1}{1+\eta}\approx 0.7-0.9\;{\rm for}\;
R_{S}\parallel r_{o}\gg 1/g_{m}\;$$

This is $100\%$ series voltage feedback. Loop gain
$T=(g_{m}+g_{mb})(r_{o}\parallel R_{S})$, closed loop
gain $T/(1+T)$.

No phase inversion.

Input impedance at low frequency:

$$\;R_{in}= \infty \;{\rm ideally}\;$$

limited by biasing network and $C_{gd},C_{gs}$ at
high frequency. Bootstrapped $C_{gs}$: $C_{in}\approx
C_{gd}+C_{gs}(1-A_{v})\approx C_{gd}$ very small,
wide band.

Output impedance: put $v_{i}=0$, drive $v_{x}$ at
$S$, measure $i_{x}$.

$$i_{x}=v_{x}/R_{S}-g_{m}(-v_{x})-g_{mb}(-v_{x})-g_{ds}(-v_{x})$$

$$\;R_{out}\equiv \frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}}=
\frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+R_{S}^{-1}}
= \left[\frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}\parallel r_{o}\right]\parallel R_{S}\;$$

Intrinsic follower without $R_{S}$:

$$\;R_{o}= \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}\parallel r_{o}\approx
\frac{1}{g_{m}}\;$$

e. g. $g_{m}=1-5\,{\rm mA/V}\to R_{o}=200-1000\,\Omega
\parallel R_{S}$. Low, but not as low as op-amp.

For $g_{mb}=0$, $r_{o}\to\infty$: $R_{out}=R_{S}\parallel 1/g_{m}$.

Current gain $\approx g_{m}R_{S}/(1+g_{m}R_{S})\cdot
R_{in}/R_{out}\gg 1$. Power gain $>1$ although
voltage gain $<1$.

In words: unity voltage buffer, high $R_{in}$, low
$R_{out}$, current and power gain, very linear due
to feedback, level shift $V_{GS}$, used as impedance
transformer, output stage, to drive resistive or
large capacitive load $C_{L}$ with pole
$p_{o}\approx 1/R_{out}C_{L}$ and to isolate a high
impedance node from a low impedance load. Replacing
$R_{S}$ by an active current source $r_{oS}$ gives
$A_{v}\to g_{m}/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\to 1$ and
$R_{out}\approx 1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 6.

answer.text:
This is the grounded gate, common gate,
source driven stage, the $MOS$ dual of the
common base.

$$V_{DD}= {\rm ac~gnd}$$

$$R_{D} {\rm ~to~ac~gnd~at~drain},~G~{\rm to~ac~gnd},~
S={\rm input},~D={\rm output}$$

$$M_{1}~N~{\rm channel},~{\rm arrow~on~}S$$
normally $B$ tied to $S$, $g_{mb}=0$.
If $B$ to $GND$, $V_{SB}=V_{in}$ and $g_{mb}\ne 0$.
Put $g_{m}^{\prime}=g_{m}+g_{mb}$ for the
general case.

In the following $g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\lambda I_{D}$,
$g_{m}= \mu C_{ox}W/L\,(V_{GS}-V_{T})=
\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D}}$, $k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}W/2L$.

> {\it Large signal:}

$$V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$$
$$V_{DS}=V_{D}-V_{S}=V_{out}-V_{in}$$
$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$$

Cut off: $V_{GS}<V_{T}$

$$V_{in}>V_{DD}-V_{T}\;\;,\;\;I_{D}=0\;\;,\;\;V_{out}=V_{DD}$$

Saturation, square law neglecting $r_{o}$:

$$I_{D}= {\frac{k_{n}}{2}}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}
\qquad V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}{\frac{k_{n}}{2}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T}\right)^{2}\tag{1}$$

parabolic, non inverting. Saturation condition

$$V_{out}-V_{in}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T}$$

$$V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{T}\tag{2}$$

$$I_{D}R_{D}\le V_{T}$$

for larger $I_{D}$, i. e. small $V_{in}$,
$$V_{out}<V_{DD}-V_{T}$$
the device goes triode

$$I_{D}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{T})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]$$

For small signal about a bias $I_{D0}$ with
$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$ the device is in
saturation and (1) linearised gives the small
signal gain.

> {\it Small signal ac model:}

$V_{DD}=0$, $G=0$, $S=v_{s}$, $D=v_{out}$

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{s}$$
$$v_{bs}=v_{b}-v_{s}=-v_{s}\;\;{\rm if~}B=GND$$
$$v_{ds}=v_{out}-v_{s}$$

hybrid $\pi$ : $g_{m}v_{gs}$ and $g_{mb}v_{bs}$
from $D$ to $S$, $r_{o}=1/g_{ds}$ from $D$ to $S$,
$R_{D}$ from $D$ to gnd.

KCL at $D$:

$${\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}}}+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{s})
+g_{m}(-v_{s})+g_{mb}(-v_{s})=0$$

$${\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}}}+g_{ds}v_{out}
= v_{s}\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\right) \tag{3}$$

Hence source to drain voltage gain

$${\frac{v_{out}}{v_{s}}}=
{\frac{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}{g_{ds}+1/R_{D}}}
=\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\right)R_{D}\parallel r_{o} \tag{4}$$

$$A_{v0}\approx \left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)R_{D}\parallel r_{o}
\approx g_{m}R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$$

for $g_{m}\gg g_{ds}$.  For $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$

$$A_{v0}\approx \left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)R_{D}\approx g_{m}R_{D}>0$$

non inverting, same magnitude as common source
but positive.  Indeed from (1)

$$A_{v0}={\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}}=k_{n}R_{D}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{IN}-V_{T}\right)=g_{m}R_{D}$$

Current gain $\approx 1$.  The stage is a
current buffer, voltage amplifier with low $R_{in}$.

Input resistance at the source.  Inject $v_{x}$
at $S$, current $i_{x}$ into $S$.

$$i_{x}=-i_{d}= -\left[g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}\right]$$

$$i_{x}= -\left[-g_{m}v_{x}-g_{mb}v_{x}+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{x})\right]$$

$$i_{x}=v_{x}(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})-g_{ds}v_{out}\tag{5}$$

But $v_{out}=i_{x}R_{D}$ from KCL at $D$,
$v_{out}/R_{D}+i_{d}=0$, $i_{d}=-i_{x}$.

$$i_{x}=v_{x}(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})-g_{ds}R_{D}i_{x}$$

$$R_{in}\equiv {\frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}}}=
{\frac{1+g_{ds}R_{D}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}}
={\frac{1+R_{D}/r_{o}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+1/r_{o}}}\tag{6}$$

$$R_{in}= {\frac{R_{D}+r_{o}}{1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}}}$$

For $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$,

$$R_{in}\approx {\frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}}\approx {\frac{1}{g_{m}}}$$

low, $\sim 50-500\,{\rm \Omega}$ typical.  With a
source resistance $R_{S}$ in series with $v_{in}$,
$v_{s}=v_{in}R_{in}/(R_{in}+R_{S})$ and from (4)

$${\frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}}}=
{\frac{g_{m}^{\prime}R_{D}\parallel r_{o}}{1+g_{m}^{\prime}R_{S}}}
\;{\frac{1}{1+g_{ds}R_{S}}}\approx
{\frac{g_{m}^{\prime}R_{D}}{1+g_{m}^{\prime}R_{S}}}\tag{7}$$

for $r_{o}\gg R_{D},R_{S}$.  For $R_{S}\gg R_{in}$,
$A_{v}\approx R_{D}/R_{S}$.

Output resistance at the drain.  With $R_{S}$ from
source to gnd, turning off $v_{in}$, test source
$v_{x}$ at drain:

$$R_{o,d}=r_{o}+\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}\right]R_{S}\tag{8}$$

so at the $V_{out}$ node

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o,d}\tag{9}$$

For ideal voltage drive $R_{S}=0$,

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}\;\;{\rm if}\;R_{D}\ll r_{o}$$

high.  For $R_{S}\ne 0$ the impedance looking
into the drain is boosted by $g_{m}r_{o}$.

In words: CG is non inverting, $A_{v}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}$,
$R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}$ low, $R_{out}\approx R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$
high, $A_{i}\approx 1$.  No Miller multiplication
of $C_{gd}$ because $G$ is ac ground, so the
input pole $1/R_{in}C_{gs}$ and output pole
$1/R_{out}C_{gd}$ are at high frequency.  Wide
band, used as $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ matched RF input,
as current buffer and as the upper device of a
cascode.  With $B$ to $GND$ replace $g_{m}$ by
$g_{m}+g_{mb}$ everywhere.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 7.

answer.text:
With the conventional small signal notation
the circuit is a $CG$ with the input shorted out.
Put $V_{B}=V_{G0}$ for the d. c. bias and
$v_{b}=0$ for signals.

$$\eqalign{
V_{GS0}&=V_{B}-V_{S0}\cr
I_{D0}&={1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{GS0}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS0}\right]\cr
V_{DS0}&=V_{D0}-V_{S0}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}-V_{S0}}$$

In the figure $V_{S0}=0$ so that

$$I_{D0}=f(V_{B})\qquad V_{0}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}\tag{1}$$

and saturation

$$V_{0}>V_{B}-V_{T}\tag{2}$$

is obtained by choice of $V_{B}$ and $R_{D}$.
For signals put $V_{DD}=0$.

> {\it As drawn} $S$ is $a.c.$ ground.

\begin{center}
{\it Fig.1 Small signal}
\end{center}

$$v_{g}=0\qquad v_{s}=v_{i}{\rm \;through\;}C_{1}{\rm \;to\;
ground}$$

i. e. with an ideal $V_{in}$, $R_{s}=0$,

$$v_{s}=0\tag{3}$$

for all $s$ with $C_{1}\ne 0$.
In the conventional hybrid $\pi $ with $b\equiv s$, Fig.1,

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=0\tag{4}$$

$$g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}=0\tag{5}$$

so that to first order

$$i_{d}=0\qquad v_{out}=-i_{d}R_{D}^{\prime}=0\tag{6}$$

$$R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel r_{0}\qquad r_{0}=1/g_{ds}$$

and

$$A_{v}(s)\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}(s)\equiv 0\tag{7}$$

in the band pass where $1/sC_{1}\to 0$.
$C_{1}$ is shorted on its right by the ground at $S$
and on its left by the ideal source $V_{in}$.
It carries the short circuit current $i_{C1}=v_{in}sC_{1}$
to ground and plays no signal role.  The $a.c.$
equivalent is a $CS$ with $v_{g}=v_{s}=0$.

In particular

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{0}\approx R_{D}\tag{8}$$

$$R_{in}= {v_{x}\over i_{x}}{\Bigl |}_{S}\approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}
\approx {1\over g_{m}}\tag{9}$$

normally, but $R_{in}$ is shorted to ground so that
the resistance seen by $V_{in}$ is

$$R_{in,ext}= {1\over sC_{1}}\parallel 0 =0\tag{10}$$

and $V_{in}$ is $a.c.$ shorted to ground.

{\it Remark:} With the ground at $S$ removed and
replaced by the normal $CG$ bias, e. g. $R_{S}$ to
ground or $I_{SS}$ with $r_{SS}\to \infty $ to ground,
the circuit is the conventional $CG$ high pass
amplifier.  With $r_{0}\to \infty $, $g_{mb}=0$ for
$b$ tied to $s$, Fig.1,

$$ \left(v_{s}-v_{in}\right)sC_{1}+v_{s}g_{m}+{v_{s}+v_{out}\over r_{0}}
+{v_{out}\over R_{D}}=0\tag{11}$$

$$v_{out}=-g_{m}v_{s}R_{D}^{\prime}\tag{12}$$

so that with $R_{S}\to \infty $

$$v_{s}=v_{in}{sC_{1}\over sC_{1}+g_{m}+g_{ds}}\tag{13}$$

$$A_{v}(s)={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}{sC_{1}\over sC_{1}+g_{m}}
{1\over 1+g_{ds}R_{D}^{\prime}{sC_{1}\over sC_{1}+g_{m}}}\tag{14}$$

$$\approx g_{m}R_{D}{s\tau\over 1+s\tau}\qquad 
\tau =C_{1}/g_{m}\tag{15}$$

i. e. high pass with

$$\omega_{L}\approx {g_{m}\over C_{1}}={1\over R_{in}C_{1}}\tag{16}$$

and in the band pass, $sC_{1}\to \infty $,

$$A_{v0}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}>0\tag{17}$$

$$R_{in0}\approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}\tag{18}$$

$$R_{out0}\approx R_{D}\parallel \left[r_{0}+
\left(1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{0}\right)R_{S}\right]\tag{19}$$

the normal non inverting $CG$ stage.  With finite
$R_{S}$ from $S$ to ground

$$A_{v0}= {g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}}\approx
{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}}\tag{20}$$

etc.  As drawn $R_{S}=0$ and (20) $\to 0$.

answers.question: How many poles does the circuit of Figure 8 have?

answer.text:
With the conventional {\it e. g.} Spencer - Ghausi
count the independent energy stores the circuit is
second order.  In the small signal model put
${r_{o}}^{-1}=0$ for brevity and put the bulk at
a. c. ground.  With

$${\rm G}:\;(V_{g}-V_{in})R_{S}^{-1}+V_{g}sC_{GS}+
\left(V_{g}-V_{d}\right)sC_{GD}=0\tag{1}$$
$${\rm D}:\;\left(V_{d}-V_{g}\right)sC_{GD}+V_{d}sC_{DB}+
V_{d}R_{D}^{-1}+g_{m}V_{g}=0\tag{2}$$

$$\eqalign{
\Delta (s)&={\rm det}\left[
\matrix{
R_{S}^{-1}+s\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-sC_{GD}\cr
g_{m}-sC_{GD} &R_{D}^{-1}+s\left(C_{GD}+C_{DB}\right)\cr}\right]\cr
&=R_{S}^{-1}R_{D}^{-1}+s\left[{C_{GS}+C_{GD}\over R_{D}}+
{C_{GD}+C_{DB}\over R_{S}}+g_{m}C_{GD}\right]\cr
&+s^{2}\left[C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}C_{DB}\right] \tag{3}}$$

and, e. g.,

$${{V_{d}}\over {V_{in}}}=-{{g_{m}-sC_{GD}}\over {R_{S}\Delta (s)}}
\tag{4}$$

so that, with $R_{D}\rightarrow R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$ if you
want $r_{o}<\infty $, $V_{o}(s)/V_{in}(s)$ is a proper
rational function with a quadratic denominator and a linear
numerator, {\it i. e.} two finite poles and one finite,
right half plane, zero at

$$s_{z}=+g_{m}/C_{GD}\tag{5}$$

the conventional Miller input pole

$$\omega _{p1}^{-1}\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+C_{GD}
\left(1+g_{m}R_{D}\right)\right] \tag{6}$$

and output pole

$$\omega _{p2}^{-1}\approx R_{D}\left[C_{DB}+C_{GD}
{{1+R_{S}C_{GS}g_{m}/C_{GD}}\over {1+R_{S}C_{GS}/C_{GD}}}\right]
\approx R_{D}\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)\tag{7}$$

for $R_{S}C_{GS}g_{m}\gg 1$.
In the normal language the circuit is a two pole, one zero,
circuit.

Formally there are three capacitors in the signal circuit,
$C_{GS}$, $C_{GD}$, $C_{DB}$, the fourth capacitor drawn,
$C_{SB}$, being short circuited by the a. c. ground on the
source, Fig. 1, so that its pole is at $|s|=\infty $.
The three capacitors $C_{GS}$, $C_{GD}$, $C_{DB}$ form the
capacitive loop

$${\rm G}-C_{GS}-{\rm GND}-C_{DB}-{\rm D}-C_{GD}-{\rm G}\tag{8}$$

so that only two of the three capacitor voltages are
independent.  Counting the degenerate capacitor the
denominator (3) is normally referred to as a three pole
denominator, four pole if you count the shorted $C_{SB}$,
with one, resp. two, of the poles at $s=\infty $.
With the usual abuse of language the circuit is often
referred to simply as a {\it three pole}, {\it four pole
counting $C_{SB}$}, circuit.  Neglecting the $s=\infty $
pole{\rm s} it is second order in the finite $s$--plane.

> {\it Remark:}  With $C_{SB}\ne 0$ and a finite source
> impedance $R_{S}^{\prime }$ in series with the source the
> conventional count is three finite poles, four counting
> $C_{GD}$, the $C_{SB}$ pole being at
> $\omega _{pS}\approx \left(R_{S}^{\prime }\parallel
> g_{m}^{-1}\right)^{-1}C_{SB}^{-1}$.  For the circuit as
> drawn $R_{S}^{\prime }=0$ and $\omega _{pS}\rightarrow
> \infty $.

In particular, putting $C_{SB}\rightarrow 0$ the circuit is
normally quoted as the conventional three capacitor, two
independent state, Miller compensated common source stage.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 9.

answer.text:
With the usual low frequency $h_{\pi }=\infty $
model the forward amplifier is the $CG$ stage

$${\rm M}_{1}\;\;g_{m},g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}\;\;{\rm body\;to\;
source\;so\;}g_{mb}=0$$

$$V_{gs}=V_{g}-V_{s}=V_{F}-V_{in}\qquad 
V_{ds}=V_{d}-V_{s}=V_{out}-V_{in}$$

$$I_{d}=g_{m}V_{gs}+g_{ds}V_{ds}
      =g_{m}(V_{F}-V_{in})+g_{ds}(V_{out}-V_{in})\tag{1}$$

directed from $D$ to $S$, i. e. out of the $V_{out}$
node into the device.

> {\it Topology :} $V_{out}$ is sampled by the
> divider $R_{1},R_{2}$ and the sample $V_{F}$ is
> subtracted in series from $V_{in}$ at the
> $V_{gs}$ port.  Voltage sampling, series mixing.
> In the conventional $series-shunt$ or $voltage-series$
> or $shunt-series$ nomenclature a $voltage-series$
> feedback amplifier.  Negative feedback: $V_{out}\uparrow
> \rightarrow V_{F}\uparrow \rightarrow V_{gs}\uparrow
> \rightarrow I_{d}\uparrow \rightarrow V_{out}=V_{DD}
> -I_{d}R_{D}\downarrow $.

For $I_{g}=0$

$$ \frac{V_{F}-V_{out}}{R_{1}}+\frac{V_{F}}{R_{2}}=0\tag{2}$$

$$V_{F}= \beta V_{out}\qquad 
\beta \equiv \frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{3}$$

is the {\it feedback factor}.  The ideal, $A\rightarrow \infty $,
closed loop gain is

$$V_{F}\approx V_{in}\;\;{\rm for\;large\;loop\;gain}$$

$$A_{id}= \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}}\Biggr|_{id}= \frac{1}{\beta}
      =1+\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}>0\tag{4}$$

non inverting $CG$ gain.  The divider loads the output
with

$$R_{F}=R_{1}+R_{2}\tag{5}$$

to ac ground.  No loading at the input, $R_{iF}=\infty $.

KCL at the $V_{out}$ node, $V_{DD}$ ac ground,

$$\frac{V_{out}}{R_{D}}+\frac{V_{out}-V_{F}}{R_{1}}+I_{d}=0\tag{6}$$

with (1)(3)

$$\frac{V_{out}}{R_{D}}+\frac{V_{out}}{R_{F}}
      +g_{m}(\beta V_{out}-V_{in})+g_{ds}(V_{out}-V_{in})=0$$

$$\left[\frac{1}{R_{D}}+\frac{1}{R_{F}}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta \right]V_{out}
      =(g_{m}+g_{ds})V_{in}\tag{7}$$

$$\;A_{f}\equiv \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}}
      =\frac{g_{m}+g_{ds}}{g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta }\; \tag{8}$$

For $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $

$$A_{f}= \frac{g_{m}}{R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}
      =\frac{g_{m}R_{D}R_{F}}{R_{D}+R_{F}+g_{m}R_{D}R_{2}}\tag{9}$$

$$A_{f}= \frac{g_{m}R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\parallel r_{o}}
            {1+g_{m}\beta \,R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\parallel r_{o}}
            \times \frac{g_{m}+g_{ds}}{g_{m}}\approx 
            \frac{A_{0}}{1+\beta A_{0}} \tag{10}$$

where

$$A_{0}=g_{m}\,R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\parallel r_{o}
      =\frac{g_{m}}{g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}}\tag{11}$$

is the open loop $CG$ gain loaded by $R_{F}$ and

$$T\equiv \beta A_{0}= \frac{g_{m}\beta}{g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}}
   =g_{m}\beta \,R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\parallel r_{o}
   \approx g_{m}\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\tag{12}$$

is the loop gain, return ratio.  E. {\rm g}. breaking the
loop at the gate, $V_{in}=0$, $V_{t}$ injected at the gate,
$V_{d}=-g_{m}V_{t}R_{D}\parallel R_{F}$, $V_{r}=\beta V_{d}$,
$T=-V_{r}/V_{t}=g_{m}\beta R_{D}\parallel R_{F}$.  In the
usual $R_{F}\gg R_{D}$

$$T\approx g_{m}R_{D}\beta =g_{m}R_{D}\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{13}$$

and

$$A_{f}= \frac{1}{\beta}\frac{T}{1+T}\xrightarrow[T\gg 1]{}\frac{1}{\beta}
      =1+\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\tag{14}$$

the familiar desensitised gain.  E. {\rm g}. $g_{m}R_{D}=10$,
$R_{1}=9R_{2}$, $\beta =0.1$, $T\approx 1$, $A_{f}\approx 5$,
$T\gg 1$ requires $g_{m}R_{D}\gg 1/\beta$.

{\it Input impedance.}  Let $I_{in}$ be the current
injected into the source terminal.  $I_{in}=-I_{d}$,

$$I_{in}=-(g_{m}+g_{ds})V_{in}+(g_{m}\beta+g_{ds})V_{out}
      =V_{in}\left[(g_{m}+g_{ds})-(g_{m}\beta+g_{ds})A_{f}\right] \tag{15}$$

With (8)

$$Z_{in\,f}\equiv \frac{V_{in}}{I_{in}}
   =\frac{g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}
          {(g_{m}+g_{ds})(R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1})}\tag{16}$$

$$Z_{in\,f}= \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{ds}}
            \left[1+\frac{g_{m}\beta+g_{ds}}{R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}}\right]
          =\frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\left[1+T\frac{g_{m}\beta+g_{ds}}{g_{m}\beta}\right]$$

For $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $

$$Z_{in\,f}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m}}+ \beta R_{D}\parallel R_{F}
            =\frac{1}{g_{m}}+\frac{R_{2}R_{D}}{R_{D}+R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{17}$$

$$Z_{in\,0}= \frac{1+g_{ds}R_{D}\parallel R_{F}}{g_{m}+g_{ds}}
          \approx \frac{1}{g_{m}}\tag{18}$$

is the $CG$ impedance without feedback but loaded by $R_{F}$.
Hence

$$Z_{in\,f}\approx Z_{in\,0}(1+T)\;\;{\rm to\;within\;the\;
      loading\;factor\;}(1+R_{D}/R_{F})^{-1}$$

Series mixing raises the normally low $1/g_{m}$ input
impedance by $1+T$ to a value that can be made e. {\rm g}.
$50\,{\rm \Omega}$ for LNA matching: $Z_{in\,f}\approx
R_{2}$ for $R_{D}\gg R_{F}$ and $g_{m}R_{2}\gg 1$,
$Z_{in\,f}\approx R_{D}\parallel R_{2}$ for $R_{F}\gg R_{D}$.

{\it Output impedance.}  Put $V_{in}=0$, inject $V_{x}$ at
$V_{out}$, measure $I_{x}$.

$$I_{x}= \frac{V_{x}}{R_{D}}+\frac{V_{x}-V_{F}}{R_{1}}+I_{d}
     =V_{x}\left[\frac{1}{R_{D}}+\frac{1}{R_{F}}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta\right]\tag{19}$$

since $V_{F}=\beta V_{x}$ and $I_{d}=g_{m}\beta V_{x}+g_{ds}V_{x}$.

$$\;Z_{out\,f}\equiv \frac{V_{x}}{I_{x}}
      =\frac{1}{g_{ds}+R_{D}^{-1}+R_{F}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}
      =\frac{R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\parallel r_{o}}{1+T}\; \tag{20}$$

including $R_{D}$.  Looking into the drain alone

$$Z_{d\,f}= \frac{1}{g_{ds}+R_{F}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}
        =\frac{R_{F}\parallel r_{o}}{1+g_{m}\beta R_{F}\parallel r_{o}}\tag{21}$$

$$Z_{out\,0}=R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\parallel r_{o}\tag{22}$$

so that

$$Z_{out\,f}= \frac{Z_{out\,0}}{1+T}\tag{23}$$

Voltage sampling lowers the output impedance by $1+T$.
For $T\gg 1$

$$Z_{out\,f}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m}\beta}= \frac{R_{1}+R_{2}}{g_{m}R_{2}}
            \parallel R_{D}\parallel R_{F}\tag{24}$$

which can be a few $10\,{\rm \Omega}$.

In Blackman terms $Z_{in}$ sees series mixing,
$Z_{out}$ sees shunt sampling, as above.

DC bias, $M_{1}$ saturated:

$$I_{D}= \frac{V_{DD}-V_{OUT}}{R_{D}},\;\;
  V_{F}=V_{OUT}\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}},\;\;
  V_{GS}=V_{F}-V_{IN}=V_{TH}+\sqrt{2I_{D}/k_{n}},\;\;
  V_{DS}=V_{OUT}-V_{IN}>V_{GS}-V_{TH}$$

fixes $V_{IN},V_{OUT}$.  Body to source as drawn so no
$g_{mb}$; if body to ground replace $g_{m}\rightarrow
g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in $T$ and $Z_{in}$.

The circuit is a single pole loop and is unconditionally
stable; at high frequency $C_{gs},C_{gd},C_{db}$ add poles
in $A_{0}(s)$ and the usual $T(s)$ phase margin must be
checked.  Apart from that the resistive feedback makes the
closed loop gain essentially $1+R_{1}/R_{2}$, desensitised
to $g_{m},r_{o}$ and $R_{D}$, with raised $Z_{in}$ and
lowered $Z_{out}$, the classic series-shunt feedback
amplifier realized with a $CG$ forward stage.

The topology recognition as series-shunt (voltage-series) feedback, the KCL derivation, and the large-loop-gain approximation are all correct and match the golden solution. Input/output impedance discussion and body effect notes are extra refinements that do not contradict the essential answer.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 10.

answer.text:
This is the $n-$ channel common drain with
active load, Fig.1. $M_{2}$ is the $W/L$
current source $I_{0}$.

$$I_{0}=I_{D2}={1\over 2}k_{2}\left( V_{b}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left( 1+\lambda _{2}V_{out}\right) =I_{D1}$$

$M_{1}$ is the follower. In normal operation

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{out}=V_{T1}(V_{SB})+V_{ov1}$$

$$V_{ov1}=\sqrt{{2I_{0}\over k_{1}}}\qquad 
k=\mu _{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\Phi _{F}+V_{SB1}}-
\sqrt{2\Phi _{F}}\right] \tag{1}$$

$$V_{SB1}=V_{S1}-V_{B1}$$

For $p-$ substrate $V_{B1}=0$, $V_{SB1}=V_{out}$ and
(1) makes the $V_{in}-V_{out}$ characteristic non linear.
In triple well or with $p-$ follower $V_{B1}=V_{S1}$,
$V_{SB1}=0$, $g_{mb1}=0$.  In the following $g_{mb1}$
is retained. $V_{b}=V_{B2}$ is signal ground.

$$V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T1}=V_{ov1}\tag{2a}$$
$$V_{DS2}=V_{out}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T2}=V_{ov2}=V_{b}-V_{T2}\tag{2b}$$

so that for $V_{in}<V_{DD}+V_{T1}$ $M_{1}$ is always
saturated. The low swing limit is (2b)

$$V_{out,min}\approx V_{ov2}\;\;{\rm or}\;\;V_{b}-V_{T2}$$
$$V_{out,max}=V_{in,max}-V_{T1}-V_{ov1}\approx V_{DD}-V_{T1}-V_{ov1}$$

for $V_{in,max}\approx V_{DD}$. For $V_{in}<V_{T1}+V_{ov1}$
$M_{1}$ is off and $M_{2}$ pulls $V_{out}\rightarrow 0$.
Large signal

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{T1}(V_{out})-\sqrt{2I_{0}/k_{1}}$$

i. e. a $DC$ level shift with unity incremental slope
apart from $V_{T1}(V_{out})$ and $\lambda $.

Small signal $v_{b}=0$, $v_{dd}=0$ Fig.2.

$$\eqalign{
i_{d1}&=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}\cr
i_{d2}&=g_{m2}v_{gs2}+g_{mb2}v_{bs2}+g_{ds2}v_{ds2}}$$

$$g_{m}=\sqrt{2kI_{0}}={2I_{0}\over V_{ov}}\qquad 
g_{ds}= \lambda I_{0}=r_{o}^{-1}\qquad 
g_{mb}=\chi g_{m}\;\;,\;\;
\chi ={\gamma \over 2\sqrt{2\Phi _{F}+V_{SB}}}$$

For $M_{1}$: $v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}$ , $v_{bs1}=-v_{out}$
if $V_{B1}=0$ , $0$ if $V_{B1}=V_{S1}$, $v_{ds1}=-v_{out}$.
For $M_{2}$: $v_{gs2}=0$, $v_{bs2}=0$, $v_{ds2}=v_{out}$.

KCL at $v_{out}$: $i_{d1}=i_{d2}$ with the sign
$d\rightarrow s$ for $n$MOS,

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{out})-g_{mb1}v_{out}-g_{ds1}v_{out}
=g_{ds2}v_{out}$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\; \tag{3}$$

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})\over 
1+(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})}$$

For $r_{o1},r_{o2}\rightarrow \infty $

$$A_{v0}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}={1\over 1+\chi _{1}}<1$$

typically $0.7-0.9$. With $V_{B1}=V_{S1}$, $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})\over 1+g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})}
\approx 1-{1\over g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})}\approx 1$$

In any case $A_{v}>0$, $<1$, non inverting, $100\%$
series voltage feedback.

Output resistance $v_{in}=0$, $v_{x}$ applied at output,
$i_{x}$ injected.

$$v_{gs1}=-v_{x}\;\;v_{bs1}=-v_{x}\;\;v_{ds1}=-v_{x}$$
$$i_{d1}=-(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{x}\;\;{\rm into\;drain}$$
Source current $=-i_{d1}$. $i_{d2}=g_{ds2}v_{x}$ into drain,
out of the node. KCL $i_{x}=-(i_{d1})+i_{d2}$ with usual
signs gives

$$\;R_{out}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}=
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}\parallel {1\over g_{ds2}}
={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\; \tag{4}$$

$$\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$$

and $\approx 1/g_{m1}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ if
$g_{mb1}=0$.  I. e. the impedance looking into the source
of a common gate with gate grounded, $1/(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})$,
in parallel with the load $r_{o2}$.

$$R_{in}= \infty \;{\rm at\;low\;frequency}\tag{5}$$

apart from $C_{gs1},C_{gb1}$.

With $C_{L}$ at the output the dominant pole is

$$\omega _{p}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}$$

the follower can drive a large $C_{L}$ with low $R_{out}$.
It is the conventional voltage buffer, impedance
transformer, level shifter with current gain $\approx
g_{m1}R_{L}$ but no voltage gain. Increasing $I_{0}$ or
$W_{1}/L_{1}$ increases $g_{m1}$ and lowers $R_{out}$ and
makes $A_{v}\rightarrow 1$. Cascoding $M_{2}$ increases
$r_{o2}$ but $R_{out}$ remains $\approx 1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$.

> *Remark:* In many CMOS processes the $n$MOS body is the
> common $p$-substrate $=GND$, so $g_{mb1}\ne 0$ and (3)(4)
> apply. With isolated well, $p$MOS follower or triple well
> $V_{B1}$ can be strapped to $V_{S1}$ and $g_{mb1}=0$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 11(a).

answer.text:
Figure 11a is the complementary inverter, {\tt NOT},
in 3 terminal notation.

$$k_{n}=\mu _{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}\;\;,\;\;k_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$$
$$V_{Tn}>0\;\;,\;\;V_{Tp}<0\;\;,\;\;|V_{T}|\approx 0.5-0.8{\rm V}$$

Body to supply so that in normal operation

$$V_{SB1}=0\;\;,\;\;V_{SB2}=0$$

no body effect. $M_{1}$ is the $n$ driver, $M_{2}$ the
$p$ active load. In steady state there is no d.c. path
$V_{DD}\to GND$.

> {\it In Fig.11b the $p$ device has its source on the
> output node. $V_{SB1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}\ne 0$, body effect,
> $V_{T}=V_{T0}+\gamma (\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}-
> \sqrt{2\phi _{F}})$ and the device works inverted.
> $V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$, $V_{OL}=|V_{Tp}|$, no rail to
> rail. Fig.11a is the correct ratioless rail to rail
> inverter.}

{\it Large signal:}

$$I_{Dn}= \cases{
0 & $V_{GS}<V_{Tn}$ cut off\cr
k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right] & triode\cr
{k_{n}\over 2}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS}) & saturation}$$

$$I_{Dp}= \cases{
0 & $V_{SG}<|V_{Tp}|$\cr
k_{p}\left[(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|)V_{SD}-V_{SD}^{2}/2\right] & triode\cr
{k_{p}\over 2}(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD}) & saturation}$$

$$I_{Dn}=I_{Dp}\;\;,\;\;V_{GS}=V_{i}\;\;,\;\;V_{SG}=V_{DD}-V_{i}$$
$$V_{DS}=V_{o}\;\;,\;\;V_{SD}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$$

* $V_{i}=0\equiv {\rm ``0''}$ :

$$V_{GS1}=0<V_{Tn}\;\;M_{1}\;{\rm OFF}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|\;\;M_{2}\;{\rm ON}$$

No d.c. current, $V_{o}$ pulled to $V_{DD}$ through
$r_{on,p}$ in triode.

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}\;\;,\;\;I_{DD}=0+{\rm leakage}$$

Input impedance $\approx \infty $.

* $V_{i}=V_{DD}\equiv {\rm ``1''}$ :

$$V_{SG2}=0<|V_{Tp}|\;\;M_{2}\;{\rm OFF}$$
$$V_{GS1}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}\;\;M_{1}\;{\rm ON}$$

$$V_{OL}=0\;\;,\;\;I_{DD}=0$$

Truth table $V_{o}= \bar V_{i}$.

For $0<V_{i}<V_{DD}$ both conduct. Conventional 5
region VTC, $V_{o}(V_{i})$:

* A: $V_{i}<V_{Tn}$ : $n$ off, $p$ triode $V_{o}=V_{DD}$
* B: $V_{Tn}<V_{i}<V_{M}$ : $n$ sat, $p$ triode
* C: $V_{i}\approx V_{M}$ : $n$ sat, $p$ sat, high gain
* D: $V_{M}<V_{i}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $n$ triode, $p$ sat
* E: $V_{i}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $n$ triode, $p$ off $V_{o}=0$

e.g. in B:

$$ {k_{n}\over 2}(V_{i}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
k_{p}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)(V_{DD}-V_{o})-
{(V_{DD}-V_{o})^{2}\over 2}\right] $$

and dual in D. At the logic threshold $V_{i}=V_{o}=V_{M}$
both saturated, $I_{Dn}=I_{Dp}$:

$${k_{n}\over 2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{M})=
{k_{p}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}))$$

For $\lambda \approx 0$

$$V_{M}={V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\,(V_{DD}+V_{Tp})\over
1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}}$$

with $V_{Tp}=-|V_{Tp}|$. For matched device
$k_{n}=k_{p}$, $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$

$$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

ratioless. $V_{M}$ can be moved by $\sqrt{\beta _{p}/\beta _{n}}$.
Normally $\mu _{n}\approx 2-3\mu _{p}$ so for symmetric
rise/fall

$$(W/L)_{p}\approx {\mu _{n}\over \mu _{p}}(W/L)_{n}\approx 2-3\,(W/L)_{n}$$

makes $k_{n}\approx k_{p}$.

Noise margins from $dV_{o}/dV_{i}=-1$:

$$V_{IL}\approx {2V_{o}-V_{DD}+V_{Tp}+ \sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}\,V_{Tn}\over
1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}$$
$$V_{IH}\approx {V_{DD}+V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\,(2V_{o}+V_{Tp})\over
1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}}$$

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\;\;,\;\;NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}$$

$\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ for matched $V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$, very
large, steep transition.

Small signal at $V_{M}$, both saturated, common source
in parallel:

$$g_{m1}=k_{n}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})\;\;,\;\;g_{m2}=k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)$$
$$g_{ds1}=\lambda _{n}I_{D}\;\;,\;\;g_{ds2}=\lambda _{p}I_{D}$$
$$r_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}=1/(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})$$

$$A_{v}={dV_{o}\over dV_{i}}=-{g_{m1}+g_{m2}\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
\approx -{1\over \lambda _{n}+\lambda _{p}}\sqrt{{2\over I_{D}}}
\left(\sqrt{k_{n}}+\sqrt{k_{p}}\right)$$

$|A_{v}|\approx 20-50\,{\rm dB}$ for long channel,
$>10$ for short channel. The inverter can be used as a
high gain push pull analog amplifier biased at $V_{M}$.

Dynamics: $C_{L}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{w}+C_{g,next}$

$$t_{pHL}\approx {C_{L}V_{DD}\over 2I_{Dn,sat}}\approx
0.69\,R_{on,n}C_{L}$$
$$t_{pLH}\approx {C_{L}V_{DD}\over 2I_{Dp,sat}}\approx
0.69\,R_{on,p}C_{L}$$
$$t_{p}={t_{pHL}+t_{pLH}\over 2}$$

Input capacitance $C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{gs2}$.

Power:

$$P_{stat}=V_{DD}I_{leak}\approx 0$$
$$P_{dyn}= \alpha C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc}$$

$I_{sc}$ is the crowbar current when both conduct during
$V_{IL}<V_{i}<V_{IH}$, $\approx 10-20\%$ of $P_{dyn}$.
No static power, full $0$ to $V_{DD}$ swing, high input
impedance, low output impedance $r_{on}\approx 1/k(V_{DD}-V_{T})$
in either state, regenerative, the basic VLSI building
block for all static CMOS logic, ring oscillators, SRAM,

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 11(b).

answer.text:
With the conventional notation $M_{1}=n$,
$M_{2}=p$ Fig.11a is the conventional

$${\rm C-MOS}=p{\rm \;up\;}n{\rm \;down\;common\;source}$$

inverter.  In the conventional symbol the arrow is the
$p$ substrate - $n$ source or the $n$ well - $p$ source
diode.  I. e. the arrow is on the {\it source} and

* $n$ : arrow {\it into} the channel, body $=p$ to
$V_{SS}=0$, source $=V_{SS}$ for the lower device
* $p$ : arrow {\it out} of the channel, body $=n$ to
$V_{DD}$, source $=V_{DD}$ for the upper device

so that in normal operation $V_{SB}=0$ and

$$V_{Tn}=V_{T0n}\qquad |V_{Tp}|=|V_{T0p}| \tag{1}$$

and the stage is a complementary common source stage,
Fig.1a.

$${\rm Fig.1a:}\;\;S_{2}=V_{DD}\;D_{2}=D_{1}=V_{o}\;
S_{1}=0\;\;G_{1}=G_{2}=V_{i}$$

$$V_{i}=0: p\;{\rm on}\;n\;{\rm off}\;V_{o}=V_{DD}$$
$$V_{i}=V_{DD}: n\;{\rm on}\;p\;{\rm off}\;V_{o}=0$$

no ${\rm d.c.}$ current in the steady state, rail to
rail swing, small signal

$$A_{v}=-{\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}\gg 1 \tag{2}$$

sharp transfer with $V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$ and
${\rm NM}_{L}\approx {\rm NM}_{H}\approx V_{DD}/2$.

Fig.11b is the same topology $V_{DD}-M_{1}-V_{o}-M_{2}-0$
$G_{1}=G_{2}=V_{i}$ but malformed.  In the usual
text book version it is drawn as

* $M_{1}$ on top with its {\it source} on the output
side, $D_{1}=V_{DD}\;S_{1}=V_{o}$, body $=V_{o}$ or
$0$
* $M_{2}$ on the bottom with $D_{2}=V_{o}\;S_{2}=0$
correct, or vice versa $S_{2}=V_{o}\;D_{2}=0$

i. e. either the $n$ and the $p$ are interchanged,
Fig.1b, or, what is the same, the source-drain of the
$p$ - or of the $n$ - is interchanged.  In any case the
stage ceases to be a complementary common source stage
and becomes a complementary {\it common drain} - source
follower - push pull stage with the output taken on the
sources.

> {\it In Fig.11b as drawn $M_{1}$ is a source follower
> whose source is $V_{o}$ and whose body is $V_{o}$,
> $M_{2}$ is normally connected.  With the conventional
> $M_{1}=n\;M_{2}=p$ labelling Fig.11b is the
> $n$ up $p$ down follower.  Interchanging the labels it
> is the $p$ up with $S_{p}=V_{o}\;D_{p}=V_{DD}$ mal
> connection.  The discussion is identical apart from the
> interchange $n\leftrightarrow p$.}

The consequences are:

* No inversion in the follower version.  With $n$ up
$p$ down

$$V_{i}=0\;{\rm :}\;V_{GS1}= -V_{o}<V_{Tn}\;n\;{\rm off}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{o}-0\;p\;{\rm on\;if\;}V_{o}>|V_{Tp}|$$

so $V_{o}$ is pulled {\it low}.  With

$$V_{i}=V_{DD}\;{\rm :}\;p\;{\rm off}\;n\;{\rm on}$$

$V_{o}$ is pulled {\it high}.  $V_{o}$ follows $V_{i}$,
it is a non inverting buffer, not an inverter.  With
only the $p$ reversed it remains inverting but with a
degraded high level.  In both cases the complementary
character is lost.

* Threshold drop.  For the follower $n$ on top, in
saturation, square law, neglecting $g_{ds}$,

$$I_{D1}= {\frac{k_{n}}{2}}\left(V_{i}-V_{o}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}
\tag{3}$$

so that with the $p$ off, $I_{D1}=0$,

$$V_{o}=V_{i}-V_{Tn}\qquad V_{i}>V_{Tn} \tag{4}$$

and dually for the $p$ follower

$$V_{o}=V_{i}+|V_{Tp}|\qquad V_{i}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}| \tag{5}$$

Hence

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}<V_{DD}\tag{6a}$$
$$V_{OL}=|V_{Tp}|>0\tag{6b}$$

in the $n$ up $p$ down follower both levels are
degraded.  In the more usual textbook malformation,
$n$ down correct, $p$ up with $S_{p}=V_{o}$,

$$V_{OL}=0\;{\rm good}\qquad 
  V_{OH}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-{\rm body\;effect}<V_{DD}\tag{7}$$

and vice versa.  There is a dead zone

$$|V_{Tp}|<V_{i}<V_{DD}-V_{Tn}\tag{8}$$

where, for enhancement devices, both devices are off,
the output is high impedance and the logic level is
undefined, determined by leakage and load.

* Body effect.  In Fig.11b the body of the follower
device is not at ${\rm a.c.}$ ground.  E. g. for the
$n$ follower with $p$ substrate to $0$,

$$V_{SB1}=V_{o}-0>0\tag{9}$$

$$V_{Tn}=V_{T0n}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB1}}
-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right] >V_{T0n}\tag{10}$$

so that (6a) becomes implicit

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{T0n}-\gamma\left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{OH}}
-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right] \tag{11}$$

typically $0.2-0.4\,{\rm V}$ extra loss.  If the $n$
well of the $p$ follower is left at $V_{DD}$ while
$S_{p}=V_{o}$,

$$V_{SBp}=V_{DD}-V_{o}>0\tag{12}$$

$$|V_{Tp}|=|V_{T0p}|+\gamma_{p}\left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SBp}}
-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right] \tag{13}$$

with the same degradation of $V_{OL}$.  If the body is
strapped to the source, $V_{SB}=0$, the $n$ follower
needs a separate $p$ well, the $p$ follower needs the
$n$ well strapped to $V_{o}$, i. e. a hot well, with
latch up and forward bias risk when $V_{o}$ tries to go
above $V_{DD}$ or below $0$ and the source-body diode
forward biases.

* Small signal gain $<1$.  The stage is a common drain,

$$A_{v}= {\frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+g_{L}}}\approx
0.7-0.9 \tag{14}$$

$$R_{o}\approx {\frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}}\tag{15}$$

No regeneration, no restoration.  The large signal
transfer is the source follower transfer, Fig.2, shallow,
with $|A_{v}|<1$ everywhere, noise margins

$${\rm NM}_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\ll V_{DD}/2\tag{16}$$
$${\rm NM}_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\ll V_{DD}/2$$

essentially zero in the dead zone.  It cannot be
cascaded as logic.

* ${\rm D.C.}$ behaviour.  Apart from the dead zone,
when one device is on the other is off, so static
current is nominally zero, but the on device is
source loaded, $V_{DS}$ small, and any load current
must be supplied through $g_{m}$, with large $V_{GS}$
overdrive.  In the transition both devices can be on
as followers, giving a large crowbar current limited
only by $g_{m}$.

In short Fig.11b is not a logic inverter.  At best it
is a push pull source follower - level shifter - buffer
with

$$V_{o}\approx V_{i}-V_{T}\tag{17}$$

threshold limited swing, strong body effect, gain $<1$,
no rail to rail operation, undefined high impedance
state for $|V_{Tp}|<V_{i}<V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$ and, if
interpreted as $p$ up $n$ down with $S_{p}=V_{o}$,
an inverter with $V_{OL}=0$ but

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{T0}-\Delta V_{T}(V_{SB})$$

and the complementary properties, sharp transfer,
full swing and $A_{v}\gg 1$ of Fig.11a are lost.  It is
usable, if at all, only as an analog source follower
output stage, not as a digital restoring gate.  The
cure is to restore Fig.11a: $S_{p}=V_{DD}$ to $n$ well
to $V_{DD}$, $S_{n}=0$ to $p$ sub to $0$, drains common
to $V_{o}$, common source operation.

The candidate answer never commits to this identification. Instead it spends most of its length assuming M1=n, M2=p (or vice versa) and analyzing the circuit as a malformed complementary CMOS stage (interchanged source/drain). When it does mention the all-NMOS interpretation briefly, it describes a follower-buffer with gain <1 and level-shifted swing, which contradicts the golden solution's central result that the two NMOS devices drive the output in opposite directions and the circuit's behavior is set by current balance with a possible zero-gain bias point. The candidate's main conclusion (a non-inverting source-follower buffer or a degraded inverter with body effect) is wrong, and the topology/device-role identification is not established per the scoring gate. At best the answer shows some relevant circuit understanding of source-follower action and body effect, warranting partial credit, but the dominant mechanism and correct identification are missed.

It analyzes the circuit as a complementary push-pull stage with one NMOS and one PMOS (or as a malformed CMOS inverter with interchanged devices), but the golden solution states that Figure 11(b) has two NMOS devices. Therefore, despite extensive discussion of source followers and threshold drops, the fundamental topology recognition is wrong, and the answer cannot receive a nonzero score.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 12.

answer.text:
This is the $n$ channel common source with
$p$ channel ``diode'' load. $M_{2}$ is
always saturated.

$$V_{SG2}=V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}\tag{1}$$

$$V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}+V_{Tp}=V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp}|$$

is identically satisfied. $M_{2}$ is a
two terminal load to $ac$ ground $V_{DD}$.

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}\tag{2}$$

in $dc$ steady state.

> {\it With $B_{1}\to GND$ , $B_{2}\to V_{DD}$,
> $V_{BS1}=V_{BS2}=0$ and $g_{mb1}=g_{mb2}=0$
> to first order. If the $n$ well is not tied
> to the source $g_{mb2}\ne 0$ must be retained.}

### 1. Large signal

Neglecting $1/\lambda $:

$$I_{D}= {1\over 2}\mu _{n}C_{ox}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
\left(V_{GS1}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}\;\;V_{GS1}>V_{Tn}\tag{3a}$$

$$I_{D}= {1\over 2}\mu _{p}C_{ox}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}
\left(V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}\tag{3b}$$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}\qquad V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$$

* $V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ : $M_{1}$ off, $I_{D}=0$

$$V_{SG2}=|V_{Tp}|\;\;,\;\;V_{oH}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}| \tag{4}$$

in the ideal square law. In reality subthreshold
conduction.

* $V_{in}>V_{Tn}$ and $M_{1}$ saturated

$$V_{DS1}=V_{o}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{Tn}=V_{in}-V_{Tn}\tag{5}$$

then (3a)=(3b)

$$V_{o}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-
\sqrt{{{\mu _{n}(W/L)_{1}}\over {\mu _{p}(W/L)_{2}}}}\,
\left(V_{in}-V_{Tn}\right) \tag{6}$$

linear $V_{o}(V_{in})$ with slope

$${{dV_{o}}\over {dV_{in}}}=-
\sqrt{{k_{n}\over k_{p}}}=-
\sqrt{{{\mu _{n}(W/L)_{1}}\over {\mu _{p}(W/L)_{2}}}} \tag{7}$$

where $k=\mu C_{ox}W/L$.

$M_{1}$ enters triode for

$$V_{o}<V_{in}-V_{Tn}\tag{8}$$

i. e. for

$$V_{in}>V_{Tn}+{{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|}\over {1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}}
\tag{9}$$

Then

$$\eqalign{
I_{D1,{\rm tri}} &=\mu _{n}C_{ox}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
\left[\left(V_{in}-V_{Tn}\right)V_{o}-{1\over 2}V_{o}^{2}\right] \cr
&= {1\over 2}\mu _{p}C_{ox}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}=I_{D2,{\rm sat}} } \tag{10}$$

which defines $V_{oL}=V_{o}(V_{in}=V_{DD})>0$.
For $k_{n}\gg k_{p}$, $V_{oL}\to V_{DSAT1}\ll V_{DD}$.
The $VTC$ is that of a loaded inverter with
static current $I_{D}$ and static dissipation
$V_{DD}I_{D}$. High gain only in the saturated-
saturated region (6).

With $\lambda \ne 0$

$$I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{n1}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{o})$$
$$I_{D2}={1\over 2}k_{p2}(V_{DD}-V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}
(1+\lambda _{p}(V_{DD}-V_{o}))$$

### 2. Small signal

$$g_{m}= \mu C_{ox}{W\over L}(V_{GS}-V_{T})
      =\sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}={2I_{D}\over {V_{GS}-V_{T}}}$$
$$g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}= \lambda I_{D}\qquad 
  r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

Small signal model: $V_{DD}=ac$ ground, $M_{1}$:
$g_{m1}v_{in}$ from $d$ to $s$, $r_{o1}$ $d-s$,
$M_{2}$: gate tied to drain, source to $ac$ ground.

KCL at $o$:

$$g_{m1}v_{in}+g_{ds1}v_{o}+g_{m2}(-v_{o})+g_{mb2}(-v_{o})
      +g_{ds2}v_{o}=0\tag{11}$$

with sign for $p$MOS. More conventionally
looking into the source of a diode connected
device:

$$Z_{d2}= {1\over {g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}}\approx {1\over g_{m2}}
\tag{12}$$

$$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel Z_{d2}
        ={1\over {g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}\tag{13}$$

$$R_{in}= \infty \tag{14}$$
to first order, $C_{gs1}$ at high frequency.

Voltage gain:

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{in}}=-g_{m1}R_{out}$$

$$\;A_{v}=-{{g_{m1}}\over {g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}\;
\approx -{{g_{m1}}\over {g_{m2}}}\,{1\over {1+(g_{mb2}/g_{m2})
+(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})/g_{m2}}}\tag{15}$$

With $B_{2}$ tied to source, $g_{mb2}=0$,

$$A_{v}\approx -{{g_{m1}}\over {g_{m2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}
      \approx -{g_{m1}\over g_{m2}}\tag{16}$$
for $g_{m}\gg g_{ds}$.

With $\lambda =0$ the gain is independent of bias:

$$|A_{v0}|={g_{m1}\over g_{m2}}=
\sqrt{{{2k_{n1}I_{D}}\over {2k_{p2}I_{D}}}}
 =\sqrt{{{k_{n1}}\over {k_{p2}}}}
 =\sqrt{{{\mu _{n}(W/L)_{1}}\over {\mu _{p}(W/L)_{2}}}}\tag{17}$$

Including $g_{mb2}$:

$$|A_{v}|={g_{m1}\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}=
{1\over {1+\eta }}{{g_{m1}}\over {g_{m2}}}\qquad 
\eta =g_{mb2}/g_{m2}\approx 0.2-0.3\tag{18}$$

Typically $|A_{v}|\approx 3-10$.  E. g. $\mu _{n}\approx
2-3\mu _{p}$, $(W/L)_{1}=10(W/L)_{2}\to |A_{v}|\approx
\sqrt{20-30}\approx 4.5-5.5$.

With finite $r_{o}$:

$$|A_{v}|={{g_{m1}}\over {g_{m2}}}\,
{1\over {1+(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})^{-1}/g_{m2}}}
\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m2}}\left[1-{{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\over g_{m2}}\right]$$

The dominant pole is at the output:

$$\omega _{p}= {1\over {R_{out}C_{L}}}\approx {{g_{m2}}\over {C_{L}}}
\qquad C_{L}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{ext}\tag{19}$$

so $GBW\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$.

Remarks:

* Self biased, no extra bias line, but low $R_{out}\approx
1/g_{m2}$ so low gain compared to current source load
$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$, $A_{v}=-g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$.
* Swing limited: $V_{oH}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$, $V_{oL}$ from (10),
$\approx 0.1-0.3\,{\rm V}$ if $(W/L)_{1}\gg (W/L)_{2}$.
Not rail to rail.
* Gain is ratioed, set by geometry, relatively linear and
process insensitive to first order.
* Useful as wideband load, level shifter, or load of
differential pair where $A_{v}=-g_{m,in}/(g_{m,load}+g_{mb,load})$.
To increase gain increase $(W/L)_{1}/(W/L)_{2}$ and increase
$L$ to reduce $\lambda $, at expense of area, capacitance and
$V_{oL}$.

It correctly notes the stage is inverting, the output is at the drain of M1, and the gain is modest due to the diode-connected load. answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 13.

answer.text:
With the usual square law in the
pentode region the circuit is the $p-$ channel
version of the saturated load inverter.

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}&:S=V_{DD},D=V_{o},G=V_{i},B=V_{DD}\cr
M_{1}&:S=V_{o},D=0,G=0,B=S\cr}
\tag{1}$$

in the conventional $3\,{\rm T}$ symbolism.
In $4\,{\rm T}$ symbolism the $n-$ well of $M_{1}$
is shown grounded.  In that case $V_{SB1}=V_{o}$
and

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{o}}
-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]\tag{2}$$

has to be carried along.  With the $3\,{\rm T}$
symbolism of Fig.13 $V_{BS1}\equiv 0$ and
$g_{mb1}\equiv 0$.  Put $g_{mb1}=0$ in what
follows for Fig.13.  Put $g_{mb1}\ne 0$ for the
$4\,{\rm T}$ grounded well version.

> {\it Remark:} With $B_{1}=0$ the $p^{+}-n$
> source junction of $M_{1}$ is forward biased
> for $V_{o}>0.6{\rm V}$.  In normal $n-$ well
> CMOS $M_{1}$ must be put in its own well
> strapped to $S_{1}=V_{o}$.

For a $p$MOS

$$I_{D}={1\over 2}k_{p}{W\over L}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{SD}\right)\qquad V_{SG}>|V_{T}|\tag{3}$$

$$V_{SG1}=V_{o}\qquad V_{SD1}=V_{o}\tag{4}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{i}\qquad V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}\tag{5}$$

so that

$$V_{GS1}=V_{DS1}=-V_{o}\tag{6}$$

$M_{1}$ is diode connected, $G_{1}\equiv D_{1}$,
and

$$V_{SD1}\ge V_{SG1}-|V_{T1}|\tag{7}$$

is identically satisfied for $|V_{T1}|>0$.
$M_{1}$ is saturated as soon as it is on,
$V_{o}>|V_{T1}|$, and cut off for $V_{o}<|V_{T1}|$.

$$V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{T2}|\tag{8}$$

$${\rm sat.}\;M_{2}: V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|$$

$$V_{o}\le V_{i}+|V_{T2}|\tag{9}$$

$$V_{SG2}>|V_{T2}|: V_{i}<V_{DD}-|V_{T2}|\tag{10}$$

for $M_{2}$ on.  KCL at the output node,
conventional current flowing down,

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}\tag{11}$$

* $M_{2}$ off, $V_{i}>V_{DD}-|V_{T2}|$: $I_{D}=0$.
$M_{1}$ discharges $C_{L}$ until $V_{SG1}=|V_{T1}|$.
In the square law model

$$V_{o}=|V_{T1}|\qquad {\rm ideally}\;0<V_{o}<|V_{T1}|
\;{\rm floating}\tag{12}$$

In practise subthreshold conduction pulls $V_{o}\to 0$
with $I_{D}=I_{0}\exp \left[(V_{o}-|V_{T}|)/nV_{t}\right]$.

* Both on and saturated, $\lambda =0$ for
illustration,

$${1\over 2}k_{p1}\left(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|\right)^{2}
={1\over 2}k_{p2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|\right)^{2}\tag{13}$$

$$V_{o}=|V_{T1}|+\sqrt{{k_{p2}\over k_{p1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|\right)\tag{14}$$

$$k_{p}= \mu _{p}C_{ox}W/L\tag{15}$$

With $|V_{T1}|\approx |V_{T2}|=|V_{T}|$

$$V_{o}\approx |V_{T}|+\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T}|\right)\tag{16}$$

i. e. a linear inverting transfer with

$${{dV_{o}}\over {dV_{i}}}= -\sqrt{{k_{p2}\over k_{p1}}}
=-{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}}}\tag{17}$$

in first order, $g_{m}=k_{p}(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)=
\sqrt{2k_{p}I_{D}}$.

Including $\lambda $,

$$k_{p1}\left(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|\right)^{2}(1+\lambda _{1}V_{o})
=k_{p2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda _{2}(V_{DD}-V_{o})\right]\tag{18}$$

* $M_{2}$ triode, $V_{o}>V_{i}+|V_{T2}|$,

$$I_{D2}=k_{p2}\left[(V_{SG2}-|V_{T2}|)V_{SD2}-{1\over 2}
V_{SD2}^{2}\right]\tag{19}$$

$$=I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{p1}(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}\tag{20}$$

$V_{o}$ saturates toward $V_{DD}$,

$$V_{o,max}\approx V_{DD}-V_{DSAT2}\tag{21}$$

The large signal voltage transfer is therefore

```
Vo
^
|          M2 triode
|         /
|        /  both saturated  dVo/dVi = -sqrt(k2/k1)
|       /  -----------------
|      /
|     /
|----/--------------------- Vi
     |                    VDD-|VT|
     |<-- M2 on -->|<--M2 off--> Vo = |VT|
```

In normal bias both devices saturated.

Small signal, Fig.13 $B_{1}=S_{1}$:

Put $v_{dd}=0$ a.c.  $M_{2}$ is common source,
$M_{1}$ is common gate with $G_{1}$ and $D_{1}$
a.c. ground and $S_{1}=v_{o}$ as input.

For $M_{1}$ with $v_{g1}=v_{d1}=0$, $v_{s1}=v_{o}$,
$v_{bs1}=0$,

$$v_{gs1}=-v_{o}\qquad v_{ds1}=-v_{o}\qquad v_{bs1}=0\tag{22}$$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}
=-(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}\tag{23}$$

With the current reference $i_{x}$ injected into
$S_{1}$, $i_{x}=i_{d1}$,

$$Z_{o1}\equiv {{v_{o}}\over {i_{x}}}=
{1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}}\tag{24}$$

$$g_{ds}=1/r_{o}= \lambda I_{D}\tag{25}$$

For the $4\,{\rm T}$ grounded well case
$v_{bs1}=-v_{o}$ and

$$Z_{o1}={1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}}\tag{24a}$$

formally the same, now $g_{mb1}\ne 0$.

$M_{2}$: $v_{sg2}=-v_{i}$, $v_{sd2}=-v_{o}$,

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}
=-g_{m2}v_{i}-g_{ds2}v_{o}\tag{26}$$

with sign such that the small signal current
sourced into the output node is $g_{m2}v_{i}$.

KCL at $v_{o}$:

$$g_{m2}v_{i}= \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{o}\tag{27}$$

Hence the low frequency small signal voltage gain

$$A_{v}\equiv {{v_{o}}\over {v_{i}}}=
-{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}
\approx -{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}\tag{28}$$

For Fig.13 as drawn $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v}\approx -{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}
\approx -{{g_{m2}}\over {g_{m1}}}\approx
-\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}\tag{29}$$

for $\lambda \to 0$ and the same $I_{D}$.
In particular for matched devices $A_{v}\approx -1$.
With body effect $A_{v}\approx -g_{m2}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})
\approx -1/(1+\eta )$, $\eta =g_{mb}/g_{m}\approx 0.2-0.3$,
$|A_{v}|\approx 0.7-0.8$.

Output resistance at $v_{o}$:

$$R_{o}=r_{o2}\parallel Z_{o1}
={1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}\parallel r_{o2}
\approx {1\over {g_{m1}}}\tag{30}$$

Input resistance $R_{i}=\infty $ at the gate of $M_{2}$.

With a capacitive load $C_{L}$ the dominant pole is

$$\omega _{p}= {1\over {R_{o}C_{L}}}
\approx {{g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\over {C_{L}}}\tag{31}$$

$$A_{v}(s)= {{A_{v0}}\over {1+sR_{o}C_{L}}}\tag{32}$$

The circuit is the $p$MOS saturated load inverter,
a low gain, low $R_{o}$, inverting $g_{m}-g_{m}$
transconductor.  It can be used as a level shifter,
as a $1/g_{m}$ load for a $p$MOS input stage or,
with $(W/L)_{2}\gg (W/L)_{1}$, as a low gain
wide band amplifier.  High gain requires replacing
$M_{1}$ by a current source, $G_{1}=V_{B}$, giving
$R_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ and
$A_{v}=-g_{m2}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$.

answers.question: Find Rout in Figure 14.

answer.text:
With the bias sources ideal, ${\rm d}V_{b1}={\rm d}V_{b2}=0$,
put a ${\rm d}V_{0}$ on the drain of $M_{1}$ and call
${\rm d}V_{X}$ the signal on the common source drain
${\rm d}V_{X}\equiv {\rm d}V_{S1}={\rm d}V_{D2}$,
Fig.1b.  For the $n$ channel equivalent

$${\rm d}I_{D}=g_{m}{\rm d}V_{GS}+g_{mb}{\rm d}V_{BS}+g_{o}{\rm d}V_{DS}
\qquad g_{o}=r_{o}^{-1}$$

$${\rm d}V_{GS1}=-{\rm d}V_{X}\qquad 
  {\rm d}V_{DS1}={\rm d}V_{0}-{\rm d}V_{X}\qquad 
  {\rm d}V_{BS1}={\rm d}V_{B1}-{\rm d}V_{X}$$

$${\rm d}V_{GS2}=0\qquad {\rm d}V_{DS2}={\rm d}V_{X}\tag{*}$$

so that, with the conventional positive $g_{m}$,

$${\rm d}I_{D1}= -g_{m1}{\rm d}V_{X}-g_{mb1}{\rm d}V_{X}
        +g_{o1}\left({\rm d}V_{0}-{\rm d}V_{X}\right) \tag{1}$$
$${\rm d}I_{D2}=g_{o2}{\rm d}V_{X} \tag{2}$$

and, KCL at $X$,

$${\rm d}I_{D1}={\rm d}I_{D2}\tag{3}$$

for the current ${\rm d}I_{0}={\rm d}I_{D1}$ injected in the
output

$${\rm d}I_{0}=g_{o1}\left({\rm d}V_{0}-{\rm d}V_{X}\right)
        -\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right){\rm d}V_{X}\tag{4}$$

From (1)-(3)

$${\rm d}V_{X}\left(g_{o1}+g_{o2}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)=g_{o1}{\rm d}V_{0}$$

$${\rm d}V_{X}={\rm d}V_{0}{\frac{g_{o1}}
        {g_{o1}+g_{o2}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}\tag{5}$$

and from (4)-(5)

$${\rm d}I_{0}= {\rm d}V_{0}g_{o1}
        -{\rm d}V_{X}\left(g_{o1}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)
        ={\rm d}V_{0}{\frac{g_{o1}g_{o2}}
        {g_{o1}+g_{o2}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}$$

i. e. in the conventional $r_{o}=1/g_{o}$ notation

$$\eqalign{
R_{0}&={\rm d}V_{0}/{\rm d}I_{0} \cr
     &={{g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}\over {g_{o1}g_{o2}}}\cr
     &=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}r_{o2}\cr
     &=\left[1+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}\right]r_{o2}+r_{o1}} \tag{6}$$

the familiar cascode multiplication of $r_{o2}$ by the
intrinsic gain of the cascode device $M_{1}$.
For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$R_{0}\approx \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}r_{o2}\tag{7}$$

and, for $r_{o1}\approx r_{o2}=r_{o}$,

$$R_{0}\approx \left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)r_{o}^{2}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\tag{8}$$

As drawn $M_{1}$ is in its own $n$ well with $B_{1}=S_{1}=X$
so that ${\rm d}V_{BS1}=0$ and $g_{mb1}=0$ in (6)-(8),

$$R_{0}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}
      =\left(1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\right)r_{o2}+r_{o1}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}$$

In the conventional $n$ well CMOS process with a common
$n$ well at $V_{DD}$, ${\rm d}V_{B1}=0$, ${\rm d}V_{BS1}=
-{\rm d}V_{X}$ and (6)-(8) apply with $g_{mb1}\ne 0$.
Neglecting the body effect $g_{mb1}\rightarrow 0$ is
normally quoted as

$$R_{0}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\qquad {\rm per\; side}$$

more precisely $R_{0}= \left(1+g_{m}r_{o}\right)r_{o}+r_{o}$.
With $g_{m}r_{o}\sim 20-50$, $r_{o}\sim 10-100{\rm k}$,
$R_{0}\sim 0.5-5{\rm M\Omega }$ is typical.  Any finite
impedance in series with $V_{b1}$ appears divided by
$g_{m1}r_{o1}$ at the output.

answers.question: How do we ensure that M2 is in saturation in Figure 14?

answer.text:
With the normal sign convention ${\rm  }V_{TP}<0$

$${\rm  }|V_{TP}|=-V_{TP}\qquad V_{ov}=V_{SG}-|V_{TP}|>0$$

for the $p$ channel

$${\rm  sat:}\;\;V_{SG}>|V_{TP}|\;\;{\rm  and}\;\;V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}-|V_{TP}|
      =V_{ov}\tag{1}$$

i. e. with the conventional $V_{DS}<0$

$$|V_{DS}|\ge |V_{GS}|-|V_{TP}|\qquad 
V_{DS}\le V_{GS}-V_{TP}\;.$$

For $M_{2}$

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{b2}\cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{X}}$$

so that (1) is

$$V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{DD}-V_{b2}-|V_{TP2}|$$

$$V_{X}\le V_{b2}+|V_{TP2}|\tag{2}$$

$$V_{SD2}\ge V_{ov2}$$

i. e. the drain of $M_{2}$, the cascode node $X$,
must be at least $V_{ov2}$ below $V_{DD}$.
Put in terms of $M_{1}$,

$$V_{X}=V_{S1}=V_{b1}+V_{SG1}=V_{b1}+|V_{TP1}|+V_{ov1}\tag{3}$$

so that (2) is

$$V_{b1}+|V_{TP1}|+V_{ov1}\le V_{b2}+|V_{TP2}|$$

For $|V_{TP1}|\approx |V_{TP2}|$

$$V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}\tag{4}$$

apart from a $100-200\,{\rm mV}$ margin and, if the
$n$ well of $M_{1}$ goes to $V_{DD}$, $\Delta |V_{T}|$
due to body effect on $M_{1}$.

In particular $V_{b1}=V_{b2}$ puts $M_{2}$ in the
triode.  $V_{b1}$ must be put {\it below} $V_{b2}$ by
about one $V_{ov}$.

With (3) in (2) the conventional {\it wide swing}
cascode bias is, at the edge of saturation,

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG2}&=|V_{TP}|+V_{ov2}\cr
V_{b2}&=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-V_{ov2}\cr
V_{b1}&=V_{b2}-V_{ov1}-{\rm marg.}\cr
      &=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-V_{ov2}-V_{ov1}-{\rm marg.}\cr
V_{X}&=V_{DD}-V_{ov2}\cr
V_{D1,{\rm max}}&=V_{b1}+|V_{TP}|\approx V_{DD}-V_{ov1}-V_{ov2}}$$

so that as long as the compliance is respected

$$V_{out}\le V_{b1}+|V_{TP}|\tag{5}$$

$$V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}$$

$M_{1}$ stays saturated, (2) stays satisfied and

$$R_{out}\approx \left(1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\right)r_{o2}+r_{o1}
      \approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\qquad M_{1},M_{2}{\rm  sat}$$

and collapses to $\approx r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ if (2)
is violated.  Eq. 4-5 is normally generated with a
replica bias, e. g. a diode connected $p$ device
carrying $I_{D1}=I_{D2}$ to generate $V_{b2}$ and
$V_{b1}=V_{b2}-V_{ov}$ with a source follower level
shift, Fig. 3.14 in Razavi.  Any bias that guarantees
(2), normally $V_{b2}=V_{b1}+V_{ov1}+{\rm marg.}$, will
do.  With $V_{b1}$ low enough $V_{X}$ is pulled low
enough to give $M_{2}$ the required $V_{SD}\ge V_{ov2}$
headroom.

> {\it Remark:} If the well of $M_{1}$ is strapped to
> $V_{DD}$, $|V_{TP1}|=|V_{TP0}|+\gamma
> \left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right)$,
> $V_{SB}=V_{X}-V_{DD}$, and (4) becomes
> $V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}+|V_{TP1}|-|V_{TP2}|$.

This matches the golden solution's essential point: M2 saturation depends on internal node X set by V_b1 and M1, not just V_b2. The answer also correctly notes V_b1 = V_b2 puts M2 in triode, providing additional correct insight.

It matches the golden solution's essential mechanism and conclusion.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 15.

answer.text:
With $M_{1}$ in ${\rm sat.}$ and $M_{2}$ in
${\rm sat.}$ and $V_{B1}$ a.c. ground the circuit is
the conventional telescopic $n$ cascode, Fig.1.
$I_{1}=I_{D1}=I_{D2}$ in the d.c. steady state.

$$I_{D}= {\frac12}k_{n}{\frac{W}{L}}(V_{GS}-V_{T})^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)\tag{1}$$

$$g_{m}=k_{n}{\frac{W}{L}}(V_{GS}-V_{T})= \sqrt{2k_{n}{\frac{W}{L}}I_{D}}
\qquad r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}\tag{2}$$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}\;\;,\;\;V_{GS2}=V_{B1}-V_{X}\;\;,\;\;
V_{BS1}=0\;\;,\;\;V_{BS2}=-V_{X}\tag{3}$$

$$V_{X}=V_{B1}-V_{GS2}=V_{B1}-V_{T}-V_{ov2}\tag{4}$$
$$V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{T}= \sqrt{2I_{1}/k_{n}W/L}$$

Saturation:

$$\eqalign{
V_{DS1}=V_{X}&\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T}=V_{ov1}\cr
V_{DS2}=V_{out}-V_{X}&\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T}=V_{ov2}\cr
V_{out}&\ge V_{B1}-V_{T}\cr
V_{out}&\ge V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}\cr
V_{B1}&=V_{X}+V_{GS2}=V_{ov1}+V_{T}+V_{ov2}\;\;{\rm min.}\cr
V_{out,max}&=V_{DD}-V_{ov,I1}\tag{5}}$$

For $V_{in}<V_{T}$, $M_{1}$ off, $M_{2}$ off, $V_{out}$
pulled to $V_{DD}-V_{DS,I1}$ by $I_{1}$.
For $V_{in}>V_{T}$ $I_{D1}$ rises $\propto (V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}$,
$V_{out}$ falls.  With an ideal $I_{1}$ the d.c.
$V_{out}$ is indeterminate in saturation, any
$V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}<V_{out}<V_{DD}-V_{ov,I1}$ satisfies
$I_{D1}=I_{1}$. In practice $r_{oI}<\infty $ fixes it.
For large $V_{in}$ $M_{1}$ triodes, $V_{X}\to 0$,
$M_{2}$ triodes, $V_{out}\to V_{DS,sat1}+V_{DS,sat2}$.

Small signal, Fig.2, $V_{B1}=0$, $V_{DD}=0$,
$r_{o1}=1/g_{ds1}$, $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}$, $r_{oI}=1/g_{dsI}$,
$g_{mb2}=\chi g_{m2}$ if the $n$ well is grounded.
For triple well $g_{mb2}=0$.

Hybrid $\pi $ between $D$ and $S$:

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}\tag{6a}$$
$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{gs2}+g_{mb2}v_{bs2}+g_{ds2}v_{ds2}\tag{6b}$$
$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}\;\;v_{ds1}=v_{x}\;\;v_{gs2}=-v_{x}\;\;
v_{bs2}=-v_{x}\;\;v_{ds2}=v_{out}-v_{x}\tag{7}$$

$G_{m}=i_{out}/v_{in}|_{v_{out}=0}$ and
$R_{out}=v_{x}/i_{x}|_{v_{in}=0}$ give
$A_{v}=-G_{m}R_{out}$.

Short circuit transconductance: $v_{out}=0$

$$v_{x}\approx -{\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}v_{in}
\approx -{\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}}v_{in}\tag{8}$$

so the voltage gain to the cascode node is $\approx -1$,
Miller multiplication of $C_{gd1}$ is

$$C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}\left(1-A_{vX}\right)
\approx C_{gs1}+2C_{gd1}\tag{9}$$

instead of $C_{gs1}+(1+g_{m1}r_{o})C_{gd1}$ for the
simple common source.  The current in the short is

$$i_{sc}\approx g_{m1}v_{in}{\frac{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}}}
\approx g_{m1}v_{in}\tag{10}$$

$$G_{m}\approx g_{m1}\tag{11}$$

i. e. the cascode is a current buffer. $M_{2}$ does not
degrade $g_{m}$.

Output resistance: $v_{in}=0$, apply $v_{x}$ at $v_{out}$.

Looking into the source of $M_{2}$ with drain load
$R_{D}=r_{oI}$,

$$R_{s2}= {\frac{R_{D}+r_{o2}}{1+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}}}
\approx {\frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}}\;\;R_{D}\ll (g_{m}r_{o})r_{o}
\tag{12}$$
$$\approx {\frac{R_{D}}{(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}}}\;\;R_{D}\sim r_{o}$$

At node $X$

$$R_{X}=r_{o1}\parallel R_{s2}\tag{13}$$

At the output, $v_{in}=0$,

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel \left\{r_{o2}+\left[1+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}\right]r_{o1}\right\}\tag{14}$$

For the ideal $I_{1}$, $R_{D}\to\infty $,

$$R_{o,cas}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}
\approx (g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}\tag{15}$$

$$R_{o,cas}\approx g_{m2}r_{o1}r_{o2}\;\;{\rm no\;body\;effect}$$

i. e. $g_{m2}r_{o2}$ times larger than the simple
$CS$ $r_{o1}$.  With finite $r_{oI}$,

$$R_{out}=R_{o,cas}\parallel r_{oI}\tag{16}$$

If $I_{1}$ is a simple $p$MOS, $r_{oI}=r_{op}\sim r_{o}$,
$R_{out}\approx r_{op}$ and the cascode alone does not
increase gain.  A $p$ cascode load is then required to
obtain $R_{out}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$.

Voltage gain, open circuit:

$$A_{v}={\frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}}}=-G_{m}R_{out}
\approx -g_{m1}R_{out}\tag{17}$$

$$\left|A_{v}\right| =g_{m1}\left\{\left[r_{o1}+r_{o2}
+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}\right]\parallel r_{oI}\right\}\tag{18}$$

Ideal load:

$$A_{v}\approx -g_{m1}(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}
\approx -g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o1}r_{o2}\tag{19}$$

$$A_{v}\approx -(g_{m}r_{o})^{2}\;\;{\rm matched\;devices}$$

$\approx g_{m2}r_{o2}$ times the $CS$ gain
$-g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{oI})$.  E.G. $g_{m}=1\,{\rm mS}$,
$r_{o}=100\,{\rm k\Omega }$, $g_{m}r_{o}=100$,
$R_{o,cas}\approx 10\,{\rm M\Omega }$, $|A_{v}|\approx 10^{4}$,
$80\,{\rm dB}$ ideal, $\approx g_{m}r_{o}=100$, $40\,{\rm dB}$
with simple $r_{oI}=r_{o}$ load.  Sign is inverting.

Frequency response: $C_{X}$ at $X$, $C_{L}$ at output,
$C_{L}=C_{gd2}+C_{db2}+C_{dbI}+C_{ext}$,
$C_{X}=C_{gd1}+C_{db1}+C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}$.

$$A_{v}(s)\approx {\frac{-g_{m1}R_{out}}
{\left(1+sR_{out}C_{L}\right)\left(1+sR_{X}C_{X}\right)}}\tag{20}$$

Dominant pole

$$\omega_{p1}\approx 1/R_{out}C_{L}\tag{21}$$

Non dominant pole

$$\omega_{p2}\approx 1/R_{X}C_{X}\approx
{\frac{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}{C_{X}}}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{D}\sim r_{o}
\tag{22}$$
$$\approx 1/r_{o1}C_{X}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{D}\to\infty $$

In the usual design $R_{D}\sim r_{o}$, $\omega_{p2}\gg\omega_{p1}$,
GBW $\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$, cascode extends bandwidth by
removing Miller effect.  Zero due to $C_{gd2}$ at
$\approx (g_{m2}+g_{mb2})/C_{gd2}$.

In summary $M_{1}$ is the $g_{m}$ device, $M_{2}$ is a
common gate current buffer that shields $M_{1}$ from
$V_{out}$, suppresses Miller effect, raises $R_{out}$ by
$\approx g_{m2}r_{o2}$ and the low frequency voltage gain
by the same factor, at the cost of one $V_{ov}$ of
headroom and an extra pole at $X$.  Input $R_{in}=\infty $,
output $R_{out}$ high, suitable as high gain stage in
op-amps with capacitive load.  Noise and offset referred
to input dominated by $M_{1}$, $M_{2}$ contribution
$\approx (g_{m2}/g_{m1})^{2}$ smaller.  Regulated cascode
can raise $R_{out}$ to $\approx (g_{m}r_{o})^{2}r_{o}$.

answers.question: Is the circuit of Figure 16 a cascode structure?

answer.text:
With the symbols as they are normally
read the circuit is {\it not\/} a {\it useful\/} cascode.
In the conventional 3 terminal symbolism the arrow is the
source.  ${\rm M}_{2}$ is drawn as an $n$ channel device,
drain on top, source at the bottom, ${\rm M}_{1}$ as a $p$
channel device, source on top, drain, {\rm GND}, at the
bottom, Fig.1.  The two sources are commoned at the
intermediate node $X$.

$$\eqalign{

answers.question: Explain why the Miller effect is less pronounced in a cascode.

answer.text:
In a single inverting stage the feedback
capacitance $C_{gd} \equiv C_{\mu}$ is Miller multiplied
by the stage voltage gain. The cascode makes that
gain $\approx 1$.

### 1. Recall: Miller multiplication

For any impedance $Z$ connected between input and output
nodes with voltage gain $A_{v}=V_{o}/V_{i}$:

$$Z_{M,in}= \frac{Z}{1-A_{v}} \qquad Z_{M,out}= \frac{Z}{1-1/A_{v}}$$

For a capacitance $C$ between input and output:

$$C_{M,in}= C(1-A_{v}) \qquad C_{M,out}= C(1-1/A_{v})$$

For a Common Source / Common Emitter with inverting gain
$A_{v}= -g_{m}R_{L}' \ll -1$:

$$C_{in}= C_{gs}+C_{gd}(1-A_{v}) \approx C_{gs}+C_{gd}(1+g_{m}R_{L}')$$

$$C_{out}\approx C_{gd}$$

If $|A_{v}| = 50-100$, $C_{gd}$ appears at the input as
$50-100 \times C_{gd}$. With source resistance $R_{sig}$ this creates a low frequency dominant input pole:

$$\omega_{p,in} \approx \frac{1}{R_{sig}\left[C_{gs}+C_{gd}(1+g_{m}R_{L}')\right]}$$

Physically: $V_{o}$ swings large and opposite to $V_{i}$, so the voltage across $C_{gd}$ is $(1-A_{v})V_{i}$ and a large charge $Q=C_{gd}(1-A_{v})V_{i}$ must be supplied by the source. Bandwidth is severely reduced. This is the Miller effect.

### 2. Cascode

```
         Vout
          |
         D2
  Vb -- G2  CG/CB - common gate/base, gate AC ground
         S2
         D1
  Vin - G1  CS/CE - common source/emitter
         S1
         GND
```

Overall gain is still large: $A_{v}=A_{v1}\cdot A_{v2}\approx -g_{m1}R_{out}$ where $R_{out}\approx g_{m2}r_{o1}r_{o2}$ is very large.

But Miller multiplication sees only the gain *across* the capacitor.

* **Transistor 1 - CS/CE:** Its load is not $R_{D}$ but the input impedance looking into the source of the CG stage.

$$R_{L1}= r_{o1} \parallel R_{in2}$$

$$R_{in2}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}$$

Hence

$$A_{v1}= \frac{v_{d1}}{v_{g1}} = -g_{m1}R_{L1} \approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}} \approx -1$$

if $M1,M2$ carry same current and are similar size. For BJT: $A_{v1}\approx -g_{m1}/g_{m2}\approx -1$.

Therefore for $C_{gd1}$ / $C_{\mu 1}$ of the input device:

$$C_{M1}= C_{gd1}(1-A_{v1}) \approx C_{gd1}(1-(-1)) = 2C_{gd1}$$

instead of $C_{gd1}(1+g_{m}R_{L}) \approx 50-100\,C_{gd1}$.

Physically the CG device clamps the drain/collector of $M1/Q1$ to $V_{B}-V_{GS2}\approx$ constant. The node $D1=S2$ is a low impedance virtual ground for signals. $v_{d1}$ swings only $\approx v_{i}$, not $A_{v}v_{i}$, so the voltage across $C_{gd1}$ is $\approx 2v_{i}$ and little extra charge is required. The input pole becomes:

$$\omega_{p,in}\approx \frac{1}{R_{sig}[C_{gs1}+2C_{gd1}]}$$

pushed up by factor $\approx g_{m}R_{L}/2$.

* **Transistor 2 - CG/CB:** Its gate/base is AC ground. Its $C_{gd2}$ / $C_{\mu 2}$ is connected between output and AC ground, not between input and output. Its $C_{gs2}$ / $C_{\pi 2}$ is between input ($S2$) and AC ground. There is no capacitance directly bridging its input to its output to be Miller multiplied. The gain from source to drain of a CG stage is $A_{v2}\approx +g_{m2}R_{L} >0$, non-inverting, so even if you apply Miller formally there is no $1-A_{v}$ enlargement.

The only capacitance at the output is $C_{gd2}+C_{db2}$ un-multiplied, and the capacitance at the intermediate node $D1/S2$ is $C_{gd1}+C_{db1}+C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}$ with low resistance $1/g_{m2}$, giving a non-dominant pole at $\approx g_{m2}/C_{x}$ at very high frequency.

> In short: The cascode splits a high gain $A_{v}$ into a low gain $A_{v1}\approx -1$ stage where Miller $C$ lives, and a high gain $A_{v2}$ stage where no Miller $C$ exists. The total gain remains $-g_{m1}R_{out}$ but the Miller multiplication factor is reduced from $1+g_{m}R_{L}$ to $\approx 2$.

This unilateralizes the amplifier, greatly reduces input capacitance, reverse feedthrough $y_{12}$, and extends $f_{H}$ and gain-bandwidth product. This is why the cascode, invented to cure the Miller effect in triodes, is the standard wideband / high frequency gain stage. The effect is not zero - $2C_{gd1}$ remains - but is $20-50\times$ smaller than in a single CS/CE stage.
