answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 7.

answer.text:
With the ground as drawn the circuit is
degenerate. Put $C_{1}\to 0$ for $f\to 0$ and
$C_{1}\to {\rm s.c.}$ for $f\gg 1/R_{in}C_{1}$ it
is nominally the conventional common gate, {\it i. e.}
common base, current buffer.

> {\it Remark:} As drawn in Fig.7 the ${\rm ac}$
> source is ${\rm ac}$ shorted to earth so that in the
> ideal sense $v_{s}\equiv 0$ and the stage has no
> signal gain at all.  In any normal realisation the
> earth on the source is replaced by a ${\rm dc}$
> current source, $I_{EE}$, or a large $R_{S}$ to
> $-V_{SS}$ which is ${\rm ac}$ open.  What follows is
> normally quoted as the {\it intended} circuit.  With
> the earth left in $R_{in}=0$, $A_{v}=0$.

\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=0.6\textwidth]{cg_small_signal}
\end{center}

{\it ${\rm dc}$:} $C_{1}$ is open

$${\rm NMOS:}\;\;V_{GS0}=V_{b}-V_{S0}$$

With the earth as drawn $V_{S0}=0$

$$V_{GS0}=V_{b}\tag{1}$$
$$I_{D0}= {1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{b}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda \left(V_{D0}-V_{S0}\right)\right]\tag{2}$$
$$V_{D0}=V_{out0}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}\tag{3}$$

Saturation for signal swing

$$V_{DS0}\ge V_{GS0}-V_{T}\tag{4}$$
$$V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}\ge V_{b}-V_{T}\tag{5}$$

normally $V_{b}$ is generated by a diode connected
bias so that (2) is well defined.  With $V_{S0}=0$
the whole $I_{D0}$ must be supplied through $R_{D}$.

{\it ${\rm ac}$:} $V_{DD}\to {\rm ac\;gnd}$, $V_{b}\to
{\rm ac\;gnd}$, $C_{1}\to 1/sC_{1}\to 0$ in band.

Put for the MOSFET in saturation

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}\tag{6}$$

In Fig.7 the bulk is strapped to the source so that
in the conventional 3 terminal symbol

$$v_{bs}=0\qquad g_{mb}=0\tag{7}$$

in the 4 terminal case $g_{mb}\ne 0$ and $g_{m}\to
g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in what follows.  Let $r_{o}=1/g_{ds}$.

With the conventional small signal model, Fig.7b,
gate ${\rm ac}$ $0$, source $v_{s}$, drain $v_{d}=v_{out}$

$$\eqalign{
v_{gs}&=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{s}\cr
v_{ds}&=v_{d}-v_{s}\cr
i_{d}&=-g_{m}v_{s}+g_{ds}\left(v_{d}-v_{s}\right)\cr
v_{d}&=-i_{d}R_{D}\;\;{\rm at\;the\;output\;node}\tag{8}}$$

so that with $v_{s}=v_{in}$ in band, {\it i. e.} with
the earth on the source removed,

$$-{{v_{d}}\over {R_{D}}}=-g_{m}v_{s}+g_{ds}v_{d}-g_{ds}v_{s}$$

$$\left({1\over {R_{D}}}+g_{ds}\right)v_{d}
      =\left(g_{m}+g_{ds}\right)v_{s}\tag{9}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {{v_{out}}\over {v_{s}}}=
{{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over {G_{D}+g_{ds}}}=
{{g_{m}r_{o}+1}\over {1+r_{o}/R_{D}}}\tag{10}$$

$$A_{v}\approx g_{m}R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx g_{m}R_{D}
\qquad r_{o}\gg R_{D}\tag{11}$$

$>0$, non inverting, the normal CG current buffer
voltage gain.  With $g_{mb}\ne 0$

$$A_{v}={{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\over {G_{D}+g_{ds}}}\approx
\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)R_{D}\tag{12}$$

With the earth left in as drawn $v_{s}\equiv 0$ for an
ideal $V_{in}$, $R_{sig}=0$,

$$v_{gs}=0\;\;,\;\;i_{d}=g_{ds}v_{d}\;\;,\;\;
v_{d}=-g_{ds}v_{d}R_{D}\tag{13}$$

so that $v_{d}=0$ to first order.  More generally with
a source resistance $R_{sig}$ in series with $V_{in}$
and $C_{1}$

$$v_{s}=V_{in}{{R_{in}}\over {R_{sig}+R_{in}+1/sC_{1}}}\tag{14}$$

and (10) is multiplied by the divider (14).

Input resistance at the source, Fig.7c, $v_{g}=0$,
$v_{d}=-i_{d}R_{D}$,

$$i_{d}=-g_{m}v_{x}+g_{ds}\left(v_{d}-v_{x}\right)$$
$$v_{d}=-i_{d}R_{D}=R_{D}g_{m}v_{x}-R_{D}g_{ds}v_{d}
      +R_{D}g_{ds}v_{x}$$

$$v_{d}=v_{x}R_{D}{{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over {1+R_{D}g_{ds}}}\tag{15}$$

The current furnished to the source is, $i_{g}=0$,

$$i_{x}=i_{s}=-i_{d}={{v_{d}}\over {R_{D}}}
      =v_{x}{{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over {1+R_{D}g_{ds}}}\tag{16}$$

$$R_{in}\equiv {{v_{x}}\over {i_{x}}}=
{{1+R_{D}g_{ds}}\over {g_{m}+g_{ds}}}=
{{1+R_{D}/r_{o}}\over {g_{m}+g_{ds}}}\tag{17}$$

$$\approx {1\over {g_{m}+g_{mb}}}\approx {1\over {g_{m}}}
\qquad R_{D}\ll r_{o}\tag{18}$$

the well known low, $\sim 10-10^{2}{\rm \Omega}$,
input resistance of the CG stage, which makes it
useful as a $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ wide band input or as
the cascode device.  With the earth as drawn the
resistance seen looking into $C_{1}$ is

$$R_{in}^{\prime}=R_{in}\parallel 0 =0\tag{19}$$

so that $V_{in}$ is ${\rm ac}$ shorted to ground.
$C_{1}$ has $0$ ${\rm ac}$ volts across it and carries
no signal current.  Formally with (14)

$${{V_{out}}\over {V_{in}}}(s)=
{{g_{m}R_{D}}\over {1+g_{m}R_{sig}}}{{sC_{1}R_{in}^{\prime}}
\over {1+sC_{1}R_{in}^{\prime}}}\to 0\tag{20}$$

for $R_{in}^{\prime}\to 0$.  For $R_{sig}\ne 0$ the
finite divider form is

$${{V_{out}}\over {V_{in}}}(s)\approx
{{g_{m}R_{D}}\over {1+g_{m}R_{sig}}}{{sC_{1}/g_{m}}
\over {1+sC_{1}/g_{m}}}\tag{21}$$

high pass with

$$\omega_{L}\approx {1\over {R_{in}C_{1}}}\approx
{{g_{m}}\over {C_{1}}}\tag{22}$$

normally $>10\,{\rm MHz}$ for $C_{1}\sim {\rm pF}$.

Output resistance at the drain, $V_{in}\to 0\Rightarrow
v_{s}=0$,

$$R_{o}\equiv {{v_{x}}\over {i_{x}}}\Bigl|_{v_{s}=0}
      =r_{o}\tag{23}$$

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}\tag{24}$$

With a finite $R_{sig}$ in the source

$$R_{o}=r_{o}\left[1+\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)R_{sig}\right]
      +R_{sig}\tag{25}$$

the usual inductive wide band output.

In normal use the earth on the source in Fig.7 is
deleted and replaced by a ${\rm dc}$ bias current
source $I_{EE}$ to $-V_{SS}$ or a large $R_{S}$ to
$-V_{SS}$ which is ${\rm ac}$ open, Fig.7d.  Then
(10)-(12), (17)-(18), (24)-(25) apply with $R_{sig}$
the resistance of $V_{in}$.  The stage is non
inverting, $A_{v}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}$, $R_{in}\approx
1/g_{m}$, $R_{out}\approx R_{D}$, wide band because
the Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$ is absent,
input pole $\sim g_{m}/C_{gs}$, output pole $\sim
1/R_{D}C_{L}$.  It is used as $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ input,
as current buffer and as the upper device of the
cascode.

> With the circuit as literally drawn the input is
> shorted to ${\rm ac}$ ground, $A_{v}=0$, $R_{in}=0$,
> $V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}$ ${\rm dc}$ only.  $C_{1}$
> is inoperative.  Delete the ground on the source.

answers.question: How many poles does the circuit of Figure 8 have?

answer.text:
With the usual ${\rm d}{\rm c}$ short the source is an
incremental earth and the ${\rm d}{\rm c}$ blocking capacity
${{C}}_{{SB}}$ is in parallel on a short.  Modulo that
short there is one capacity per non earth incrementtal node,
Fig.1, viz. the ${\rm Miller}$ capacity ${{C}}_{{GD}}$ counted
twice.  Formally one pole per independent capacity.  In
${\cal R}{\cal C}$ terms

$${{C}}_{{GS}}\;,\;{{C}}_{{GD}}\;,\;{{C}}_{{DB}}\;\;{\rm and\;,
formally,}\;\;{{C}}_{{SB}} \tag{*}$$

so that, with ${{C}}_{{SB}}$ shorted, three nominal
capacities, four with $(*)$.  The ${{C}}_{{GS}}-{{C}}_{{GD}}-
{{C}}_{{DB}}$ ${\rm \Delta}$ on the two non earth nodes
${{V}}_{{G}},{{V}}_{{D}}\equiv {{V}}_{{o}}$ is second order.
E. {\rm g.} with ${{r}}_{{o}}\rightarrow \infty $ put
${{V}}_{{G}}={{V}}_{{g}}$, ${{V}}_{{D}}={{V}}_{{o}}$

$$\eqalign{
{{V}_{{g}}\over {{R}_{{S}}}}+s{{C}}_{{GS}}{{V}_{{g}}}
 +s{{C}}_{{GD}}\left({{V}_{{g}}}-{{V}_{{o}}}\right)&=
        {{{V}_{{in}}}-{{V}_{{g}}}\over {{R}_{{S}}}}\cr
{{g}_{{m}}}{{V}_{{g}}}+{{{{V}_{{o}}}\over {{R}_{{D}}}}}
 +s{{C}}_{{GD}}\left({{V}_{{o}}}-{{V}_{{g}}}\right)
 +s{{C}}_{{DB}}{{V}_{{o}}}&=0\cr} \tag{1}$$

so that, eliminating ${{V}_{{g}}}$,

$${{V}_{{o}}\over {{V}_{{in}}}}=-{{{1\over {{R}_{{S}}}}
\left({{g}_{{m}}}-s{{C}}_{{GD}}\right)}\over
{D\left(s\right)}} \tag{2}$$

$$\eqalign{
D\left(s\right)&=s{{C}}_{{GD}}\left({{g}_{{m}}}-s{{C}}_{{GD}}\right)
+\left({1\over {{R}_{{D}}}}+s\left({{C}}_{{GD}}+{{C}}_{{DB}}\right)
\right)\left({1\over {{R}_{{S}}}}+s\left({{C}}_{{GS}}+{{C}}_{{GD}}
\right)\right) \cr
&={1\over {{{R}_{{S}}}{{R}_{{D}}}}}+s\left[{{g}_{{m}}}{{C}}_{{GD}}
+{{{C}}_{{GS}}+{{C}}_{{GD}}\over {{R}_{{D}}}}+
{{{C}}_{{GD}}+{{C}}_{{DB}}\over {{R}_{{S}}}}\right]
+{{s}^{{2}}}\left[{{C}}_{{GS}}{{C}}_{{GD}}+{{C}}_{{GS}}{{C}}_{{DB}}
+{{C}}_{{GD}}{{C}}_{{DB}}\right] \tag{3}}$$

i. {\rm e.} second order in $s$ with the familiar
${\rm RHP}$ zero at

$${{s}_{{z}}}=+{{{{g}_{{m}}}\over {{C}}_{{GD}}}} \tag{4}$$

and, for ${{g}_{{m}}}{{R}_{{D}}}\gg 1$,

$$D\left(s\right)\approx {1\over {{{R}_{{S}}}{{R}_{{D}}}}}
\left[1+s{{R}_{{S}}}{{R}_{{D}}}{{g}_{{m}}}{{C}}_{{GD}}\right]
\left[1+s{{{{C}}_{{GS}}{{C}}_{{GD}}+{{C}}_{{GS}}{{C}}_{{DB}}
+{{C}}_{{GD}}{{C}}_{{DB}}\over {{g}_{{m}}}{{C}}_{{GD}}}}\right] \tag{5}$$

so that, to first order, the conventional
${\rm Miller}$ pole

$${{s}_{{p1}}}\approx -{1\over {{{R}_{{S}}}{{R}_{{D}}}{{g}_{{m}}}
{{C}}_{{GD}}}}\approx -{1\over {{{R}_{{S}}}{{C}}_{{M}}}} \tag{6}$$

and the output pole

$${{s}_{{p2}}}\approx -{{{{g}_{{m}}}{{C}}_{{GD}}}\over
{{{C}}_{{GS}}{{C}}_{{GD}}+{{C}}_{{GS}}{{C}}_{{DB}}
+{{C}}_{{GD}}{{C}}_{{DB}}}} \tag{7}$$

In particular for ${{C}}_{{DB}}\gg {{C}}_{{GS}},{{C}}_{{GD}}$,
${{s}_{{p2}}}\approx -{{g}_{{m}}}/{{C}}_{{DB}}$ and for
${{C}}_{{GS}}\gg {{C}}_{{GD}},{{C}}_{{DB}}$,
${{s}_{{p2}}}\approx -{{g}_{{m}}}{{C}}_{{GD}}/
{{C}}_{{GS}}\left({{C}}_{{GD}}+{{C}}_{{DB}}\right)$.
The conventional one pole per node
${{s}_{{p1}}}\approx -1/{{R}_{{S}}}{{C}}_{{GS}}$,
${{s}_{{p2}}}\approx -1/{{R}_{{D}}}{{C}}_{{DB}}$ is recovered
for ${{C}}_{{GD}}\rightarrow 0$.

Formally keeping the ${\rm AC}$ shorted ${{C}}_{{SB}}$ the
denominator is $3\left(4\right)$ order with the
${{C}}_{{SB}}$ pole at $\left|s\right|\rightarrow \infty $.
Normally quoted as a three pole, two finite pole, one
finite zero system.  With the ${\rm AC}$ short removed it is
normally quoted simply as a two pole, one zero system.
Any finite ${{R}_{{S}}}$ in the source lead adds the third
finite pole $s_{{p3}}\approx -1/{{R}_{{S}}}{{C}}_{{SB}}$.

> {\it Remark:}  Counting a pole per capacitor the circuit is
> $4$ pole, $3$ pole with the source ${\rm AC}$ shorted.  The
> incremental source node being an ${\rm AC}$ earth the
> ${{C}}_{{SB}}$ pole is at $s=\infty $ and the
> ${{C}}_{{GS}}-{{C}}_{{GD}}-{{C}}_{{DB}}$ network is second

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 9.

answer.text:
This is the 1 transistor series-shunt
{\it voltage series} feedback amplifier.
In the conventional $shunt-series$ nomenclature
it is a shunt-shunt amplifier.

\begin{center}
{\it $M_{1}$ is a $CG$ voltage amplifier
$R_{1},R_{2}$ is the $\beta $ circuit}
\end{center}

$$V_{F}=\beta V_{out}\qquad 
\beta ={{V_{F}}\over {V_{out}}}{\Bigl |}_{I_{g}=0}$$

with the gate open $I_{g}=0$

$${{V_{F}}\over {V_{out}}}={{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}$$

in parallel with the output, in series with the
input at the source

$$\eqalign{
V_{gs}&=V_{g}-V_{s}=V_{F}-V_{in}\cr
V_{ds}&=V_{d}-V_{s}=V_{out}-V_{in}}$$

so that an increase of $V_{in}$ decreases $V_{gs}$,
decreases $I_{D}$, increases $V_{out}$, increases
$V_{F}$ and restores $V_{gs}$.  Negative feedback.
$V_{out}/V_{in}>0$, non inverting.

With $V_{DD}$ ac ground small signal

$$\eqalign{
I_{D}&=g_{m}V_{gs}+g_{ds}V_{ds}\cr
&=g_{m}(V_{g}-V_{s})+g_{ds}(V_{d}-V_{s})\cr
g_{ds}&=r_{o}^{-1}\cr
g_{m}^{\prime}&=g_{m}+g_{mb}{\rm \;if\;body\;effect}}$$

Put $V_{s}=V_{in}$, $V_{d}=V_{out}$, $V_{g}=V_{F}$.

KCL at $V_{out}$ and at $V_{F}$:

$$\eqalign{
{{V_{out}}\over {R_{D}}}+{{V_{out}-V_{F}}\over {R_{1}}}+I_{D}&=0\cr
{{V_{F}-V_{out}}\over {R_{1}}}+{{V_{F}}\over {R_{2}}}&=0\;\;I_{g}=0}$$

so that, as far as the gate loading is concerned,

$$V_{F}=V_{out}{{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}=\beta V_{out}\tag{1}$$

$${{V_{out}-V_{F}}\over {R_{1}}}={{V_{out}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}\tag{2}$$

i. e. the feedback network loads the output with

$$R_{F}=R_{1}+R_{2}\tag{3}$$

to ac ground.  The $CG$ stage sees

$$R_{L}=R_{D}\parallel R_{F}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})\tag{4}$$

as drain load.  For $R_{F}\gg R_{D}$, $R_{L}\approx R_{D}$.
KCL at the drain with (1)(2):

$${{V_{out}}\over {R_{L}}}+g_{m}(\beta V_{out}-V_{in})
+g_{ds}(V_{out}-V_{in})=0$$

$${{V_{out}}\over {V_{in}}}=
{{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over {g_{ds}+R_{L}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}}\tag{5}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {{V_{out}}\over {V_{in}}}=
{{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over {R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})}}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty $

$$A_{v}\approx {{g_{m}}\over {R_{L}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}}
={1\over {\beta +1/g_{m}R_{L}}}={1\over \beta}
{1\over {1+1/g_{m}\beta R_{L}}}\tag{6}$$

The open circuit, loaded, $CG$ gain is

$$A_{0}=g_{m}R_{L}\parallel r_{o}\approx g_{m}R_{L}\tag{7}$$

and (6) is the familiar

$$A_{vf}={{A_{0}}\over {1+\beta A_{0}}}\tag{8}$$

apart from the $1+g_{ds}/g_{m}$ correction.
The loop or return ratio, breaking the loop at the
gate, $V_{s}=0$, $V_{g}=V_{t}$,

$$V_{d}=-g_{m}V_{t}\;R_{L}\parallel r_{o}\approx -g_{m}R_{L}V_{t}$$
$$V_{r}=\beta V_{d}$$

$$T\equiv -{{V_{r}}\over {V_{t}}}=g_{m}\beta R_{L}\parallel r_{o}
={{g_{m}\beta}\over {R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}}}\approx g_{m}\beta R_{L}\tag{9}$$

so that

$$A_{vf}={1\over \beta}{{T}\over {1+T}}\;{{1+g_{ds}/g_{m}}\over
{1+g_{ds}R_{L}/1+T}}\approx {1\over \beta}{{T}\over {1+T}}\tag{10}$$

For $T\gg 1$

$$A_{vf}^{id}={1\over \beta}={{R_{1}+R_{2}}\over {R_{2}}}=1+{{R_{1}}\over {R_{2}}}>0\tag{11}$$

exactly as a non inverting resistive op-amp.
The gain is stabilised against $g_{m},r_{o},R_{D},V_{DD},T$
to the ratio of two resistors.  In the usual design
$R_{F}\gg R_{D}$ and

$$A_{vf}\approx {{g_{m}R_{D}}\over {1+g_{m}R_{D}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})}}$$

$$T\approx g_{m}R_{D}{{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}$$

$T\gg 1$ requires $g_{m}R_{D}\gg 1+R_{1}/R_{2}$.

E. g. $R_{1}=9R_{2}$, $A_{vf}^{id}=10$, $T\approx 0.1g_{m}R_{D}$,
$g_{m}R_{D}>50$ for $1\%$ accuracy.

> {\it Remark:} With the usual $series-shunt$ two port
> decomposition the $A$ circuit is the $CG$ stage loaded at
> the output by $R_{1}+R_{2}$ and the $\beta $ circuit is
> (1).  Input loading of the $\beta $ circuit is nil,
> $I_{g}=0$, output loading is $R_{1}+R_{2}$.

Input resistance at the source.  With $V_{F}=\beta V_{out}$,
$V_{out}=A_{v}V_{in}$,

$$I_{in}=I_{s}= -I_{D}=g_{m}(V_{in}-V_{F})+g_{ds}(V_{in}-V_{out})$$

$$I_{in}=V_{in}(g_{m}+g_{ds})-V_{out}(g_{m}\beta+g_{ds})$$

$$I_{in}=V_{in}(g_{m}+g_{ds})\left[1-{{g_{m}\beta+g_{ds}}\over
{R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta}}\right]
=V_{in}(g_{m}+g_{ds}){{R_{L}^{-1}}\over {R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta}}$$

$$R_{if}\equiv {{V_{in}}\over {I_{in}}}=
{{R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta}\over {(g_{m}+g_{ds})R_{L}^{-1}}}
={{1+(g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta)R_{L}}\over {g_{m}+g_{ds}}}\tag{12}$$

$$R_{if}=R_{i0}(1+T)\tag{13}$$

where

$$R_{i0}={{1+g_{ds}R_{L}}\over {g_{m}+g_{ds}}}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\tag{14}$$

is the $CG$ input resistance with the gate ac ground
and drain load $R_{L}$.  For $r_{o}\to\infty$

$$R_{if}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+ \beta R_{L}
={1\over g_{m}}+{{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}R_{D}\parallel(R_{1}+R_{2})\tag{15}$$

$$R_{if}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+{{R_{D}R_{2}}\over {R_{D}+R_{1}+R_{2}}}$$

For $R_{D}\gg R_{F}$, $R_{L}\approx R_{F}$,

$$R_{if}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+R_{2}\tag{16}$$

The series mixing raises the normally low $1/g_{m}$
$CG$ input resistance by $1+T$.  It can be designed to
e. g. $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ wide band.

Output resistance at the drain.  Put $V_{in}=0$, apply
$V_{x}$ at $V_{out}$, $V_{F}=\beta V_{x}$,

$$I_{x}={{V_{x}}\over {R_{D}}}+{{V_{x}-V_{F}}\over {R_{1}}}
+g_{m}V_{F}+g_{ds}V_{x}$$

$$I_{x}=V_{x}\left[R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta\right]\tag{17}$$

$$R_{of}\equiv {{V_{x}}\over {I_{x}}}=
{1\over {R_{L}^{-1}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta}}
={{R_{L}\parallel r_{o}}\over {1+g_{m}\beta R_{L}\parallel r_{o}}}
={{R_{o0}}\over {1+T}}\tag{18}$$

$$R_{o0}=R_{L}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{L}\tag{19}$$

is the $CG$ output resistance with source ac ground,
loaded by $R_{F}$.  For $r_{o}\to\infty$

$$R_{of}\approx {1\over {R_{L}^{-1}+g_{m}\beta}}
=R_{L}\parallel {1\over g_{m}\beta}
=R_{L}\parallel {{R_{1}+R_{2}}\over g_{m}R_{2}}\tag{20}$$

$$\approx {{R_{1}+R_{2}}\over g_{m}R_{2}}\parallel R_{D}\parallel(R_{1}+R_{2})$$

For $T\gg 1$, $R_{of}\approx 1/g_{m}\beta\ll R_{D}$.
The shunt, voltage, sampling lowers the output
resistance by $1+T$, as usual for voltage feedback.

In Blackman terms $R_{if}=R_{i0}(1+T_{sc})/(1+T_{oc})$ etc.
Here $T_{sc}=T$, $T_{oc}=0$ for $R_{if}$ and vice versa for
$R_{of}$.

With $T\gg 1$ the closed loop amplifier is an almost
ideal voltage amplifier: $R_{if}$ high, $R_{of}$ low,
$A_{vf}\approx 1/\beta$ fixed by $R_{1},R_{2}$, distortion
reduced by $1+T$, bandwidth enlarged by $1+T$, $GBW\approx
A_{0}\omega_{0}$ conserved.  The resistive $\beta $ is
wide band.  The loop has essentially the single pole at
the output node $R_{L}C_{L}$ and is unconditionally stable
for normal $T$.  DC feedback through the same divider
stabilises the bias point $V_{GS}=V_{F}-V_{S}$,
$V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$, $V_{F}=\beta V_{out}$.

Including body effect replace $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in
$T$, $A_{v}$, $R_{if}$, $R_{of}$.  This is the classic
single transistor voltage-series feedback stage, the
discrete equivalent of the non-inverting op-amp
connection.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 10.

answer.text:
This is the $n-$ channel {\it common drain}
with active load, Fig.1.

\begin{center}
{\it $M_{1}$ is the driver $M_{2}$ is the $W/L$ current
source $I_{0}$}
\end{center}

$$I_{0}=I_{D1}=I_{D2}={1\over 2}k_{2}\left( V_{b}-V_{T2}-V_{DSAT2}\right)^{2}
\left( 1+\lambda _{2}V_{out}\right) \approx {1\over 2}k_{2}
\left( V_{b}-V_{T}\right)^{2}$$

$k=\mu _{n}C_{ox}W/L$ . $V_{b}$ is a $dc$ bias so
$M_{2}$ is $ac$ ground at the gate.

> {\it Large signal:}

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}$$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{T1}(V_{SB})+\sqrt{{2I_{0}\over k_{1}}\,{1\over
1+\lambda _{1}V_{DS1}}}$$

with $V_{SB}=V_{out}-V_{B}$. In the figure $V_{B}=V_{DD}$
$ac$ ground so

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{out}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right] $$

is $V_{out}$ dependent. If the $n$ well is available
$B_{1}$ can be strapped to $S_{1}$ and $V_{T1}=V_{T0}$.

In saturation

$$\eqalign{
V_{DS1}&\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\cr
V_{DD}-V_{out}&\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{T1}\cr
V_{in}&\le V_{DD}+V_{T1}\cr
V_{DS2}&\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T2}\cr
V_{out}&\ge V_{b}-V_{T2}=V_{DSAT2}}$$

so

$$V_{DSAT2}<V_{out}<V_{DD}-V_{DSAT1}\tag{1}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{T0}-\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{out}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]-\sqrt{2I_{0}/k_{1}}$$

i. e. a $dc$ level shift $\approx V_{T}+V_{ov1}$ with
follower action on the $ac$ component.  Class $A$.
$I_{0}$ must sink/source the load current.

> {\it Small signal $ac$ ground $V_{DD}$:}

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}\qquad v_{bs1}=-v_{out}\qquad 
v_{ds1}=-v_{out}\qquad v_{ds2}=v_{out}\qquad v_{gs2}=v_{bs2}=0$$

$$\eqalign{
i_{d1}&=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}\cr
&=g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{out})-g_{mb1}v_{out}-g_{ds1}v_{out}\cr
i_{d2}&=g_{ds2}v_{out}\cr}$$

with $g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\lambda I_{D}$ in saturation.
KCL at the output node, no external load,

$$i_{d1}=i_{d2}$$

$$g_{m1}v_{in}=\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{out}$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\; \tag{2}$$

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})\over 
1+(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})}$$

If the body can be tied to the source $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v0}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})\over 1+g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})}$$

Normally $(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})\ll g_{m1}$,

$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}={1\over 1+\chi}
\approx 0.7-0.9<1\tag{3}$$

$$\chi =g_{mb}/g_{m}= {\gamma \over 2\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}}$$

and $A_{v0}\approx 1-g_{ds}/g_{m}\approx 0.95-0.99$,
in phase, no inversion.  The active load gives
$r_{o2}\gg R_{D}$ so $A_{v}\to 1$ much closer than with
a resistive load and with much larger available swing
for the same $I_{0}$.

In the usual $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$ limit Eq.2 is often
quoted as $A_{v}\approx 1$.

> {\it Impedances:}

Gate current $=0$,

$$R_{in}= \infty \;\;{\rm at\; low\; frequency}\tag{4}$$

$$C_{in}\approx C_{gs1}+C_{gb1}+C_{gd1}(1-A_{v})+C_{gd2}$$

For $R_{out}$ put $v_{in}=0$, drive the output with
$v_{x}$, measure $i_{x}$.

$$i_{d1}=-(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{x}\qquad i_{d2}=g_{ds2}v_{x}$$

$$i_{x}=i_{d2}-i_{d1}=\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{x}$$

$$\;R_{out}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\; \tag{5}$$

$$\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\;\;{\rm for}\;
g_{mb}=0,\;r_{o}\to \infty $$

Typically $0.2-2\,{\rm k\Omega }$.  Low, good for driving
capacitive or low resistive loads, the classic buffer/
level shifter.  With an external load $R_{L}\parallel C_{L}$,

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+G_{L}}$$

$$R_{out}^{\prime}=R_{out}\parallel R_{L}\qquad 
\omega _{p}\approx {1\over R_{out}^{\prime}C_{L}}$$

is the dominant pole.  The follower is wide band,
input pole at $\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{in}$ is normally
very high because $C_{gd1}$ is bootstrapped by
$(1-A_{v})\ll 1$.

Remarks: Current gain $\approx g_{m1}R_{L}\gg 1$.
Power gain $>1$.  Distortion is dominated by
$g_{mb}(V_{out})$ and $\lambda $ modulation of $I_{0}$.
With $B_{1}=S_{1}$ the body effect is removed and
linearity and $A_{v}$ are improved.  The circuit is
the standard output stage of a two stage op-amp and
as a source follower buffer for impedance transformation.

For $g_{m}=1\,{\rm mA/V}$, $\chi =0.2$, $r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}=25\,{\rm k\Omega }$,
$A_{v}\approx 0.82$, $R_{out}\approx 0.8\,{\rm k\Omega }$,
$A_{v0}\approx 0.96$, $R_{out0}\approx 0.96\,{\rm k\Omega }$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 11(a).

answer.text:
Figure 11a is the conventional complementary
MOS inverter. With the usual notation

$$k_{n}=\mu _{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{n}\qquad 
  k_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{p}$$
$$V_{TN}>0\qquad V_{TP}<0\qquad |V_{TP}|=-V_{TP}$$

$$I_{Dn}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{TN})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]\;\;{\rm triode}$$
$$I_{Dn}=k_{n}/2\,(V_{GS}-V_{TN})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS})\;\;{\rm sat.}$$
and complementary for the $p$ device with
$V_{SG}=-V_{GS}$, $V_{SD}=-V_{DS}$.

$$M_{1}:n{\rm MOS}\;\;S=GND,\;D=V_{out},\;G=V_{in},\;B=GND$$
$$M_{2}:p{\rm MOS}\;\;S=V_{DD},\;D=V_{out},\;G=V_{in},\;B=V_{DD}$$

so that $V_{SB}=0$ for both devices to first order,
no body effect, $V_{GS1}=V_{in}$, $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$,
$V_{DS1}=V_{out}$, $V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$ and

$$I_{Dn}(V_{in},V_{out})=I_{Dp}(V_{in},V_{out})\tag{1}$$

at every static point.

> In Fig.11b the two devices are in series between
> $V_{DD}$ and $GND$ but the upper device is connected
> common drain, $D_{1}=V_{DD}$, $S_{1}=V_{out}$,
> $G_{1}=V_{in}$, $B_{1}=V_{out}$ and $D_{2}=V_{out}$,
> $S_{2}=GND$, $B_{2}=GND$.  I. e. $M_{1}$ is a source
> follower. $V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{out}$. It can pull
> $V_{out}$ only to $V_{in}-V_{TN}$ and the stage is
> ratioed, has static current for $V_{out}=L$ and
> $V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{TN}$ if $M_{1}$ is $n$MOS, or
> forward bias of the $S-B$ junction of $M_{1}$ if
> $M_{1}$ is $p$MOS with $B=V_{out}$. It is {\it not}
> a complementary inverter. What follows is the
> $p$ on top, $n$ on bottom, $S$ to supply, Fig.11a.

### 1. Large signal - logic function

* $V_{in}=0\equiv L$:

$$V_{GS1}=0<V_{TN}\;,\;M_{1}\;{\rm OFF}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}>|V_{TP}|\;,\;M_{2}\;{\rm ON}$$

No d.c. path to $GND$, $M_{2}$ in triode with
$V_{SD2}\approx 0$ pulls

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}\tag{2}$$

$I_{DD}=0$ except leakage.

* $V_{in}=V_{DD}\equiv H$:

$$V_{SG2}=0<|V_{TP}|\;,\;M_{2}\;{\rm OFF}$$
$$V_{GS1}=V_{DD}>V_{TN}\;,\;M_{1}\;{\rm ON}$$

$$V_{OL}=0\tag{3}$$

$I_{DD}=0$.

Hence

$$\begin{array}{c|c}
V_{in}&V_{out}\\ \hline
L&H\\
H&L
\end{array}\qquad V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$$

full rail to rail swing, ratioless, zero static power.
It is the basic CMOS logic gate.

### 2. Voltage transfer characteristic

With (1) five regions are obtained, Fig.1.

* **I:** $0\le V_{in}<V_{TN}$ : $M_{1}$ off, $M_{2}$ triode,
$V_{out}=V_{DD}$.

* **II:** $V_{TN}<V_{in}<V_{M}$ : $M_{1}$ sat., $M_{2}$ triode

$$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{in}-V_{TN})^{2}=
k_{p}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{in}+V_{TP})(V_{DD}-V_{out})
-\frac{(V_{DD}-V_{out})^{2}}{2}\right] \tag{4}$$

$V_{out}$ falls.

* **III:** $V_{in}\approx V_{M}$ : both saturated

$$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{TN})^{2}=
\frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{TP})^{2}\tag{5}$$

if channel length modulation neglected. This defines the
logic threshold or switching threshold $V_{M}$ where
$V_{in}=V_{out}=V_{M}$:

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{DD}+V_{TP}+V_{TN}\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}
{1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}\tag{6}$$

For the usual matched design

$$|V_{TP}|=V_{TN}=V_{T}\;,\;k_{n}=k_{p}\;\; \Rightarrow\;\;
V_{M}=V_{DD}/2 \tag{7}$$

and with $\lambda\ne 0$

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{DD}+V_{TP}+V_{TN}\sqrt{(k_{n}/k_{p})
(1+\lambda_{p}V_{M})/(1+\lambda_{n}V_{M})}}
{1+\sqrt{(k_{n}/k_{p})(1+\lambda_{p}V_{M})/(1+\lambda_{n}V_{M})}}$$

Both devices carry the same current $I_{DM}$.

* **IV:** $V_{M}<V_{in}<V_{DD}+V_{TP}$ : $M_{1}$ triode,
$M_{2}$ sat.

$$k_{n}\left[(V_{in}-V_{TN})V_{out}-V_{out}^{2}/2\right]=
\frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{in}+V_{TP})^{2}\tag{8}$$

* **V:** $V_{DD}+V_{TP}<V_{in}\le V_{DD}$ : $M_{2}$ off,
$M_{1}$ triode, $V_{out}=0$.

The VTC is very steep in III. To first order the
transition width $\approx 0$.

The unity gain points $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$ define

$$V_{IL}=V_{in}|_{dV_{o}/dV_{i}=-1\;{\rm in\;II}}\qquad
  V_{IH}=V_{in}|_{dV_{o}/dV_{i}=-1\;{\rm in\;IV}}$$
$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}\qquad V_{OL}=0$$

obtained from (4),(8) differentiated implicitly.
E.g. in II with $dV_{o}/dV_{i}=-1$

$$k_{n}(V_{IL}-V_{TN})=k_{p}\left[V_{DD}-V_{IL}+V_{TP}
-2(V_{DD}-V_{o})\right]$$

together with (4) gives $V_{IL},V_{o}(V_{IL})$.
Closed form is cumbersome. For the symmetric case
$V_{TN}=|V_{TP}|=V_{T}$, $k_{n}=k_{p}$:

$$V_{IL}\approx \frac{3V_{DD}}{8}+\frac{V_{T}}{4}\;,\;
  V_{IH}\approx \frac{5V_{DD}}{8}-\frac{V_{T}}{4}$$

in the square law long channel approximation, more
generally $V_{IL}=V_{M}-\Delta$, $V_{IH}=V_{M}+\Delta$
with $\Delta\ll V_{DD}$.

Noise margins

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}=V_{IL}$$
$$NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}=V_{DD}-V_{IH}\tag{9}$$

For the symmetric $V_{DD}=5{\rm V}$, $V_{T}=0.7{\rm V}$
$NM_{L}\approx NM_{H}\approx 1.8-2.0{\rm V}$, i.e.
$\approx 40\%$ of $V_{DD}$. With $V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$ the
margins are maximum and equal.

### 3. Small signal gain at $V_{M}$

Both in saturation

$$g_{m1}=k_{n}(V_{M}-V_{TN})\;,\;g_{m2}=k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{TP})$$
$$g_{ds1}=\lambda_{n}I_{DM}\;,\;g_{ds2}=\lambda_{p}I_{DM}$$

$$A_{v}= \left.\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}\right|_{V_{M}}
= -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
\approx -\frac{1}{(\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})}
\frac{g_{m}}{I_{D}}\approx -\frac{2}{(\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})(V_{M}-V_{T})}\tag{10}$$

typically $20$ to $100$, the inverter is a high gain
inverting amplifier at the switching point, hence
regenerative.

### 4. Dynamic and power

Static $P_{s}=V_{DD}I_{leak}\approx 0$.

Dynamic for a load $C_{L}$ switching at frequency $f$
with activity $\alpha$:

$$P_{d}= \alpha C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc}\tag{11}$$

$I_{sc}$ is the short circuit current flowing when both
devices are on during the transition, $I_{sc}\approx
I_{DM}$ for a time $t_{sc}$.

Propagation delay, first order $RC$:

$$t_{pHL}\approx 0.69\,R_{n}C_{L}\;,\;
  R_{n}\approx \left[k_{n}(V_{DD}-V_{TN})\right]^{-1}$$
$$t_{pLH}\approx 0.69\,R_{p}C_{L}\;,\;
  R_{p}\approx \left[k_{p}(V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|)\right]^{-1}\tag{12}$$

$$t_{p}= (t_{pHL}+t_{pLH})/2$$

Equal rise/fall requires $k_{n}\approx k_{p}$ i.e.
$(W/L)_{p}\approx (\mu_{n}/\mu_{p})(W/L)_{n}\approx
2-3\,(W/L)_{n}$.

Power-delay product $PDP = P_{d}t_{p}\approx C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}/2$.

In summary Fig.11a is the ideal ratioless, rail-to-rail,
zero static power CMOS inverter, the building block of
all static CMOS logic. Fig.11b with the upper device
as a source follower is not complementary: $V_{in}=L$
leaves the output floating, $V_{in}=H$ gives a
ratioed divider with $V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{TN}$,
$V_{OL}>0$ and static $I_{DD}\ne 0$, and with $p$MOS
on top and $B$ tied to $V_{out}$ the $S-B$ diode
forward biases for $V_{out}=L$. It is not used as a
logic inverter.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 11(b).

answer.text:
With the conventional $3T$ symbol the arrow is
the $p-n$ junction. $p^{+}\to n$ for the $p$ device,
$n^{+}\to p$ for the $n$ device.  In $a$:

$${\rm M_{2}}:p\;S=V_{DD}\;D=V_{o}\qquad 
  {\rm M_{1}}:n\;D=V_{o}\;S=0\tag{1}$$

common source, common drain, $B_{p}=V_{DD}$,
$B_{n}=0$, $V_{SB}=0$, full complementary.

In $b$ as drawn

$${\rm M_{1}}:p\;{\rm arrow\;on\;}V_{o}\qquad 
  {\rm M_{2}}:n\;{\rm arrow\;on\;}0\tag{2}$$

i. e.

$$\eqalign{
{\rm M_{1}}&p\;{\rm ``}S{\rm ''}=V_{o}\;{\rm ``}D{\rm ''}=V_{DD}\;
      B=V_{o}\cr
{\rm M_{2}}&n\;D=V_{o}\;S=0\;B=0\cr}\tag{3}$$

The $p$ device is put in backwards.  The high
voltage $p^{+}$ diffusion is the drain.  The
effective source is the $V_{DD}$ diffusion.
Put $S_{e}=V_{DD}$, $D_{e}=V_{o}$ for the $p$:

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG,e}&=V_{DD}-V_{in}\cr
V_{SD,e}&=V_{DD}-V_{o}\cr
V_{SB,e}&=V_{DD}-V_{B}=V_{DD}-V_{o}\cr}\tag{4}$$

$$V_{Tn}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}- 
\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right] \tag{5}$$

$$|V_{Tp}|=|V_{T0p}|+\gamma_{p}
\left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB,e}}-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right]
      =|V_{T0p}|+\gamma_{p}
\left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{DD}-V_{o}}-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right] \tag{6}$$

so $|V_{Tp}|=|V_{T0p}|$ for $V_{o}=V_{DD}$ and
$|V_{Tp}|\approx |V_{T0p}|+0.3-0.6{\rm V}$ for
$V_{o}\to 0$.

For the $n$ normal

$$\eqalign{
V_{GS,n}&=V_{in}\cr
V_{DS,n}&=V_{o}\cr}\tag{7}$$

$$I_{Dn}= \cases{
0 & $V_{GS}<V_{Tn}$\cr
K_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right] &
$V_{DS}<V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$ triode\cr
{K_{n}\over 2}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{DS}) &
$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$ sat.\cr}\tag{8}$$

$$I_{Dp,e}= \cases{
0 & $V_{SG,e}<|V_{Tp}|$\cr
K_{p}\left[(V_{SG,e}-|V_{Tp}|)V_{SD,e}-V_{SD,e}^{2}/2\right] &
$V_{SD,e}<V_{SG,e}-|V_{Tp}|$\cr
{K_{p}\over 2}(V_{SG,e}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda_{p}V_{SD,e}) &
$V_{SD,e}\ge V_{SG,e}-|V_{Tp}|$\cr}\tag{9}$$

with $K=\mu C_{ox}W/L$ and $I_{Dp,e}$ flowing
$V_{DD}\to V_{o}$, $I_{Dn}$ flowing $V_{o}\to 0$,
KCL at the output, no $dc$ load,

$$I_{Dp,e}(V_{in},V_{o})=I_{Dn}(V_{in},V_{o})\tag{10}$$

apart from the $p^{+}/n$ well diode

$$I_{D,B}=I_{S}\exp \left[(V_{DD}-V_{o})/V_{T}\right]\tag{11}$$

$p^{+}(V_{DD})\to n{\rm -well}(V_{o})$ which is
forward for $V_{o}<V_{DD}-0.6{\rm V}$ if the well
is strapped to $V_{o}$ as the symbol indicates.
In a normal $n$ well process the well must be
$V_{DD}$.  Strapping it to $V_{o}$ is a design
rule violation, latch up risk.  If the well is
correctly strapped to $V_{DD}$ the diode is
$V_{o}(p^{+})\to V_{DD}(n)$ reverse for $V_{o}<V_{DD}$
and (11) disappears but (6) remains with
$V_{SB,e}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$.

Formally (10) gives the normal inverter
characteristic.

* $V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ : $I_{Dn}=0\Rightarrow I_{Dp,e}=0
\Rightarrow V_{SD,e}=0\Rightarrow V_{o}=V_{DD}$.
$M_{2}$ off, $M_{1}$ deep triode, $V_{SG}=V_{DD}-V_{in}>
|V_{Tp}|$.

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}\tag{12}$$

no $dc$ current, diode $0$ bias.

* $V_{in}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $I_{Dp,e}=0\Rightarrow
I_{Dn}=0\Rightarrow V_{DS,n}=0\Rightarrow V_{o}=0$
in the ideal MOS model.

$$V_{OL,ideal}=0\tag{13}$$

$M_{1}$ off, $M_{2}$ deep triode.

For $V_{Tn}<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ both on.

$$V_{SD,e}\ge V_{SG,e}-|V_{Tp}|\iff V_{o}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}|
\tag{14} {\rm p\;sat.}$$

$$V_{DS,n}\ge V_{GS,n}-V_{Tn}\iff V_{o}\ge V_{in}-V_{Tn}
\tag{15} {\rm n\;sat.}$$

Both sat. only for

$$V_{in}-V_{Tn}\le V_{o}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}|\tag{16}$$

i. e. in the high gain region $V_{o}\approx V_{in}$.
Putting both in saturation in (10)

$${K_{n}\over 2}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
  {K_{p}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}(V_{o})|)^{2}\tag{17}$$

For $K_{n}=K_{p}$, $|V_{Tp}|\approx V_{Tn}=V_{T}$,
neglecting body effect,

$$V_{M}\approx {V_{DD}\over 2}\tag{18}$$

the usual $V_{M}$.  With (6) $V_{M}$ is shifted to

$$V_{M}\approx {V_{DD}-|V_{T0p}(V_{M})|+V_{Tn}\over
1+\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}}\tag{19}$$

$\approx 0.4-0.45V_{DD}$ for $K_{n}=K_{p}$.

For $V_{in}<V_{M}$ : $I_{Dp,sat}>I_{Dn,sat}$ so
$I_{Dp}$ must be degenerated to triode, $I_{Dn}$ sat.

$${K_{n}\over 2}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
K_{p}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|)(V_{DD}-V_{o})
-{1\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{o})^{2}\right]\tag{20}$$

For $V_{in}>V_{M}$ : $M_{1}$ sat., $M_{2}$ triode

$${K_{p}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}=
K_{n}\left[(V_{in}-V_{Tn})V_{o}-{1\over 2}V_{o}^{2}\right]\tag{21}$$

This is the normal sharp common source transfer
curve, Fig.$a$, with $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$, $V_{OL}=0$,
$|A_{v}|\approx (g_{mn}+g_{mp})/(g_{dsn}+g_{dsp})\gg 1$
in the both sat. region.

The malformation appears in the electrical
realisation:

* Body effect: $g_{mbp}$ degenerates the $p$
device, $|V_{Tp}|$ grows as $V_{o}$ falls,
transconductance $g_{m}/(1+\eta)$, gain
$\approx (g_{m}/(1+\eta))/g_{ds}$ reduced,
$V_{IL},V_{IH}$ degraded, noise margins
$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}$, $NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}$
shrunk by $0.2-0.4{\rm V}$.

* If the symbol is taken literally, $B_{p}=V_{o}$,
the $p^{+}(V_{DD})/n(V_{o})$ junction is forward
for $V_{o}<V_{DD}-0.6{\rm V}$.  For $V_{in}=V_{DD}$,
$V_{o}\to 0$ the diode is forward $V_{DD}$ across
it.  KCL becomes

$$I_{Dn}(V_{o})+I_{D,B}(V_{o})=0\tag{22}$$

with $I_{D,B}$ exponential.  The $n$ device must
sink the diode current.  In triode

$$K_{n}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{Tn})V_{o}-V_{o}^{2}/2\right]
\approx I_{S}e^{(V_{DD}-V_{o})/V_{T}}\tag{23}$$

$V_{o}$ is clamped to $V_{DD}-V_{D}\approx
V_{DD}-0.7{\rm V}$ for small $K_{n}$ and to
$0.5-1.5{\rm V}$ for very large $K_{n}$, i. e.

$$V_{OL}\approx 0.7-1.0{\rm V}\;{\rm to}\;V_{DD}-0.7{\rm V}
\tag{24}$$

not $0$, and a $dc$ current

$$I_{DD}\approx I_{Dn}(V_{OL})\approx {\rm mA}\tag{25}$$

flows $V_{DD}\to$ diode $\to V_{o}\to M_{2}\to GND$
even in the static $V_{in}=V_{DD}$ state.  The
proper CMOS inverter has $I_{DD,stat}\approx 0$
(${\rm pA}$).  Here $P_{stat}=V_{DD}I_{DD}\neq 0$,
ratioed logic.

Even with the well correctly tied to $V_{DD}$ the
diode is reverse, $V_{OL}=0$ is recovered in the
ideal model, but the circuit remains a source
follower with $V_{SB}\neq 0$, i. e. a common drain
inverter.  In the textbook common drain
interpretation, $M_{1}n\;D=V_{DD}\;S=V_{o}$,
$M_{2}p\;S=V_{o}\;D=0$, the swing is

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}(V_{OH})\tag{26}$$
$$V_{OL}=|V_{Tp}(V_{OL})|\tag{27}$$

threshold loss, no rail to rail, low gain
$A_{v}\approx g_{m}/(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})<1$.

In either interpretation the circuit inverts
logically, $V_{in}=0\to V_{o}=H$, $V_{in}=1\to
V_{o}=L$, but electrically it is not a
restoring CMOS gate: degraded $V_{OL}/V_{OH}$,
reduced $NM$, non zero static power, forward
biased well junction, latch up hazard and
strong body effect.  Interchanging $S$ and $D$
of $M_{1}$ so that $S_{p}=V_{DD}$, $B_{p}=V_{DD}$
restores Fig.$a$, the proper common source
CMOS inverter with $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$, $V_{OL}=0$,
$r_{o}\approx 1/(g_{dsn}+g_{dsp})$, $|A_{v}|\gg 1$
and $I_{stat}=0$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 12.

answer.text:
With the square law in the usual notation
${k_{n,p}}=\mu _{n,p}C_{ox}W/L$ the circuit is the
inverter with the active load.  Put

$${I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}\tag{*}}$$

$${I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{n}(V_{GS1}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS1})}$$
$${I_{D2}={1\over 2}k_{p}(V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD2})}$$

for $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$ and

$$I_{D1}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS1}-V_{Tn})V_{DS1}-{1\over 2}V_{DS1}^{2}\right]$$

in the triode.

For the {\it p} device

$$V_{SG2}=V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}\qquad V_{G2}=V_{D2}=V_{o}$$

so that

$$V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp}|\;\;{\rm i.\;e.}\;\;0\ge -|V_{Tp}|$$

is always satisfied when the device is on.  The
diode is always saturated.

For the $n$ device

$$V_{GS1}=V_{i}\qquad V_{DS1}=V_{o}$$

$${\rm sat:}\;\;V_{o}\ge V_{i}-V_{Tn}\tag{1}$$
$${\rm triode:}\;\;V_{o}<V_{i}-V_{Tn}\tag{2}$$

* {\it Cut off:} $V_{i}<V_{Tn}$

$$I_{D}=0\qquad V_{o}\approx V_{DD}\tag{3}$$

apart from leakage the output node is pulled to $V_{DD}$.
$|V_{SG2}|<|V_{Tp}|$.

* {\it Both saturated:} $V_{i}>V_{Tn}$ and (1) holds.
Neglecting $\lambda $ for the large signal

$${1\over 2}k_{n}(V_{i}-V_{Tn})^{2}={1\over 2}k_{p}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}\tag{4}$$

$${V_{o}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-\sqrt{{k_{n}\over k_{p}}}\,
\left(V_{i}-V_{Tn}\right) \over 
\sqrt{(1+\lambda _{n}V_{o})/(1+\lambda _{p}(V_{DD}-V_{o}))}} \tag{5}$$

to first order

$$V_{o}\approx V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-a\,(V_{i}-V_{Tn})\qquad 
a\equiv \sqrt{{k_{n}\over k_{p}}}=
\sqrt{{\mu _{n}(W/L)_{1}\over \mu _{p}(W/L)_{2}}}\tag{6}$$

i. e. a linear inverter with

$${dV_{o}\over dV_{i}}=-a=-\sqrt{{k_{n}\over k_{p}}}\tag{7}$$

The saturation condition (1) with (6) gives the
upper end of the high gain region

$$V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-a(V_{i}-V_{Tn})\ge V_{i}-V_{Tn}$$

$$V_{i}\le V_{Tn}+{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|\over 1+a}
      =V_{Tn}+{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-V_{Tn}\over 1+a}+{V_{Tn}\over 1+a}\tag{8}$$

normally $V_{i}-V_{Tn}\ll V_{DD}$ so the interval
$V_{Tn}<V_{i}<V_{Tn}+(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)/(1+a)$ is the
useful linear region.  In it

$$V_{o,{\rm max}}\approx V_{DD}\;\;{\rm for}\;V_{i}=V_{Tn}$$
$$V_{o}\approx V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|\;\;{\rm for}\;V_{i}\approx V_{Tn}$$

* {\it $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ saturated:} $V_{o}<V_{i}-V_{Tn}$

$$k_{n}\left[(V_{i}-V_{Tn})V_{o}-{1\over 2}V_{o}^{2}\right]
      ={1\over 2}k_{p}\left(V_{DD}-V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}\tag{9}$$

which for $V_{i}=V_{DD}$ defines the low level $V_{OL}$.
For $a\gg 1$, $V_{OL}\ll V_{DD}$ and to first order

$$V_{OL}\approx {k_{p}\over k_{n}}{(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}
\over 2(V_{DD}-V_{Tn})}\;\;{\rm for}\;V_{OL}\ll V_{DD}$$

in general the solution of (9).  The slope
$|dV_{o}/dV_{i}|$ falls rapidly.

The voltage transfer curve is therefore $V_{DD}$ for
$V_{i}<V_{Tn}$, a straight line of slope $-a$ given by
(6) and a shallow tail going to $V_{OL}$ when $M_{1}$
goes triode, Fig.1.

Small signal in the saturated high gain region, Fig.2.
With $v_{gs1}=v_{i}$, $v_{sg2}=-v_{o}$,

$$M_{1}: \;g_{m1}v_{i}+g_{ds1}v_{o}\;\;{\rm to\;ground}$$
$$M_{2}: \;g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{mb2}v_{sb2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}$$

For the conventional $n$-well process the $n$ bulk is
ground, the $p$ bulk is $V_{DD}$,

$$V_{SB1}=0\;\;V_{SB2}=0\;\;g_{mb1}=g_{mb2}=0$$

in general keep $g_{mb2}$.  With $v_{g2}=v_{d2}=v_{o}$,
$v_{s2}=0$,

$$i_{d2}= -g_{m2}v_{o}-g_{mb2}v_{o}-g_{ds2}v_{o}$$

so the impedance looking into the source of the diode is

$$Z_{d2}={1\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\approx {1\over g_{m2}}
\qquad g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1\tag{10}$$

KCL at the output

$$g_{m1}v_{i}+g_{ds1}v_{o}+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2})v_{o}=0$$

$${A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{i}}=-{g_{m1}\over 
g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\tag{11}}$$

$${R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\parallel {1\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}
      ={1\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}\tag{12}}$$

$$R_{in}=\infty \;\;{\rm capacitive}\;C_{gs1}+(1-A_{v})C_{gd1}$$

With $g_{mb}=0$, $\lambda =0$,

$$A_{v0}\approx -{g_{m1}\over g_{m2}}\tag{13}$$

and with $g_{m}=\sqrt{2kI_{D}}=\sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}(W/L)I_{D}}$,
$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$,

$${|A_{v0}|={g_{m1}\over g_{m2}}=
\sqrt{{k_{n}\over k_{p}}}=
\sqrt{{\mu _{n}(W/L)_{1}\over \mu _{p}(W/L)_{2}}}=a\tag{14}}$$

which is the large signal slope (7).  Including
$r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$,

$$|A_{v}|={g_{m1}\over g_{m2}}\,{1\over 
1+(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})/g_{m2}}=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\tag{15}$$

$$g_{m}r_{o}={2\over \lambda (V_{GS}-V_{T})}\gg 1$$

so the correction is $O(1/g_{m}r_{o})$.

In the triode $g_{m1}$ is replaced by the triode
transconductance and $g_{ds1}\gg g_{m1}$ so $|A_{v}|\ll
g_{m1}/g_{m2}$.

Remarks:

* Gain is the ratio of transconductances, essentially
independent of bias current and $\approx 3-10$ for
reasonable $(W/L)_{1}/(W/L)_{2}$.  Large gain requires
$(W/L)_{1}\gg (W/L)_{2}$ at the expense of area,
capacitance and $V_{OL}$.

* $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m2}$ is low, $\sim {\rm k\Omega }$.
The dominant pole is

$$\omega _{p}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}=
{g_{m2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\over C_{L}}\approx {g_{m2}\over C_{L}}$$

wide band but low gain.  Miller multiplication of
$C_{gd1}$ is $1+g_{m1}/g_{m2}$.

* Static power $P=V_{DD}I_{D}$ when $M_{1}$ is on.
Headroom $V_{DD}>V_{Tn}+|V_{Tp}|+V_{DSAT1}+V_{SDSAT2}$.

* Input referred thermal noise $\overline{v_{n}^{2}}=
4kT\gamma (g_{m1}+g_{m2})/g_{m1}^{2}$ per unit bandwidth.

This is the simplest CMOS common source gain stage,
useful as a wide band low gain stage, as active load
for a differential pair, or as a level shifter.  High
gain requires cascoding or current source loading.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit of Figure 13.

answer.text:
With the usual square law in saturation

$${I_{D}= {k_{p}\over 2}{W\over L}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{SD}\right)\tag{*}}$$
$$g_{m}=k_{p}{W\over L}\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)
      =\sqrt{2k_{p}{W\over L}I_{D}}\qquad 
  r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}\qquad g_{mb}=\eta g_{m}$$

$k_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}$ the circuit is the $p$-
channel version of the $n$ channel inverter with
enhancement load.  $M_{2}$ is the driver, common
source, $V_{S2}=V_{DD}$ a.c. ground, $M_{1}$ is the
load.  $G_{1}=D_{1}=0$ so $G_{1}$ is shorted to
$D_{1}$.

> {\it i. e.} a two terminal diode connected $p$MOS
> between $V_{out}$ and ground.  $S_{1}=V_{out}$ is
> the anode, $D_{1}=G_{1}=0$ the cathode.

In the conventional 3 terminal symbol the arrow is
the bulk.  For $M_{2}$ $B_{2}=S_{2}=V_{DD}$.
For $M_{1}$ $B_{1}=S_{1}=V_{out}$ if a separate
$n$-well is available, $V_{SB1}=0$ and there is no
body effect on $M_{1}$.  If $M_{1}$ is put in the
same $n$-well as $M_{2}$, $B_{1}=V_{DD}$,
$V_{SB1}=V_{out}-V_{DD}<0$ and

$$|V_{Tp1}|=|V_{Tp0}|+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi _{F}
+|V_{SB1}|}-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right)$$

and $g_{mb1}\ne 0$.  Putting $B_{1}=0$ would forward
bias the $S_{1}-B_{1}$ junction for $V_{out}>0.6{\rm V}$
and is not physical in bulk CMOS.  Formally it gives
$V_{SB1}=V_{out}$ and $g_{mb1}$ as below with
$V_{SB1}>0$.

In normal operation both devices are on

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG1}&=V_{out}-0> |V_{Tp1}|\cr
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{in}> |V_{Tp2}|\cr
V_{SD1}&=V_{out}-0\cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{out}}$$

Saturation, $V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$, is

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}:&V_{SD1}=V_{SG1}\ge V_{SG1}-|V_{Tp1}|\;\;{\rm always
\;in\;sat.\;when\;on}\cr
M_{2}:&V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp2}|\cr
&V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp2}|\cr
&V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp2}| \tag{1}}$$

$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$ so that with $\lambda =0$,
$\gamma =0$

$${k_{p1}\over 2}\left({W\over L}\right)_{1}
\left(V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}=
{k_{p2}\over 2}\left({W\over L}\right)_{2}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2} \tag{2}$$

$$\;V_{out}=|V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|\right)\; \tag{3}$$

in the both saturated region.  With $\lambda \ne 0$

$$(W/L)_{1}(V_{out}-|V_{Tp1}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{1}V_{out})
 =(W/L)_{2}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp2}|)^{2}
  \left[1+\lambda _{2}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right] \tag{2a}$$

and with body effect $|V_{Tp1}|=|V_{Tp1}(V_{SB1})|$.
E. {\it g.} for $(W/L)_{1}=(W/L)_{2}$,
$|V_{Tp1}|=|V_{Tp2}|$, $\lambda =0$,

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-V_{in}\tag{4}$$

i. e. the large signal inverter characteristic.
More generally

$${dV_{out}\over dV_{in}}=-
\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}<0 \tag{5}$$

in saturation.

Large signal regions, $\lambda =0$ for illustration:

* $V_{in}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp2}|$: $M_{2}$ off, $I_{D}=0$,
$M_{1}$ off, $V_{out}\approx 0$, more exactly
$V_{out}<|V_{Tp1}|$.

* $|V_{Tp1}|<V_{out}<V_{in}+|V_{Tp2}|$,
$V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp2}|$: both saturated, (3)
inverter with slope (5).

* $V_{out}>V_{in}+|V_{Tp2}|$: $M_{2}$ triode,
$M_{1}$ saturated,

$$I_{D1}={k_{p1}\over 2}(W/L)_{1}(V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}
 =k_{p2}(W/L)_{2}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|)
 (V_{DD}-V_{out})-{1\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{out})^{2}\right]$$

$V_{out}$ saturates at $V_{DD}-V_{DSAT2}$,
$V_{DSAT2}=V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp2}|$.  The available
swing is

$$|V_{Tp1}|<V_{out}<V_{DD}-|V_{DSAT2}|$$

typically $0.5-1{\rm V}$ to $V_{DD}-0.2{\rm V}$.
The bias point is very process sensitive and the
stage draws static current $I_{D}V_{DD}$.

Small signal, Fig.1, $v_{dd}=0$ a.c.

$M_{2}$: $v_{sg2}=-v_{in}$, $v_{sd2}=-v_{out}$,
$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}
      =-g_{m2}v_{in}-g_{ds2}v_{out}\tag{6}$$
directed from $V_{DD}$ into the output node.

$M_{1}$: $S_{1}=V_{out}$, $D_{1}=0$, $G_{1}=0$,
$B_{1}=S_{1}$ for separate well, $B_{1}=V_{DD}$ or
$0$ otherwise.

$$v_{sg1}=v_{s1}-v_{g1}=v_{out}\qquad 
  v_{sd1}=v_{out}\qquad 
  v_{sb1}=v_{s1}-v_{b1}= \cases{0&$B_{1}=S_{1}$\cr
                               v_{out}&$B_{1}=0$\cr
                               v_{out}-0&$B_{1}=V_{DD}$ a.c. $v_{out}$}$$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{mb1}v_{sb1}+g_{ds1}v_{sd1}
      =(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{out}\tag{7}$$

directed from the output node to ground.  $g_{mb1}=0$
for $B_{1}=S_{1}$.

KCL at the output, $i_{d2}=i_{d1}$:

$$-g_{m2}v_{in}-g_{ds2}v_{out}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{out}$$

$$\;A_{v}={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
      -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\; \tag{8}$$

For the normal separate well connection $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$\;A_{v}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
      \approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}\;,\;\;|A_{v}|\sim 1 \tag{8a}$$

With body effect

$$A_{v}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\approx
 -{1\over 1+\eta}\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}\tag{8b}$$

$\eta =g_{mb}/g_{m}\approx 0.2-0.4$, so $|A_{v}|$
is $0.7-1.0$ for $(W/L)_{1}=(W/L)_{2}$.  Including
$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}$,

$$R_{out}=r_{o2}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}
        \approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}
        \approx {1\over g_{m1}}\tag{9}$$

$$A_{v}=-g_{m2}R_{out}\tag{10}$$

$$R_{in}=\infty \;\;{\rm at\;d.c.}\tag{11}$$

$$C_{in}=C_{gs2}+C_{gd2}(1-A_{v})\approx C_{gs2}+2C_{gd2}$$

$$C_{out}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{L}$$

Dominant pole

$$\omega _{p}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{out}}
      \approx {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\over C_{out}}\tag{12}$$

i. e. a low impedance, wide band node.  The stage is
inverting, has voltage gain of order unity, current
gain $\approx g_{m2}/g_{ds}$, transconductance
$g_{m2}$ loaded by $g_{m1}$.  It is the $g_{m}-g_{m}$
loaded common source amplifier, the $p$MOS analogue of
the $n$MOS enhancement load inverter.  High gain
requires $R_{out}\to r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$, i. e.
a current source load, not a diode connected load.
In modern CMOS the $p$ load would be replaced by an
$n$MOS current mirror or the complementary CMOS
inverter is used to get $A_{v}=-g_{m}r_{o}$.

Any $\lambda $ correction is

$$|A_{v}|={g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\,
        {1\over 1+(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})}$$

and $g_{m}=\sqrt{2k_{p}(W/L)I_{D}}$, so that for
matched $k_{p}$ and $I_{D}$

$${g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}=\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}$$

which is the large signal slope (5).  Noise, PSRR
and supply sensitivity are poor because the bias
current is set by the ratioed $V_{SG}$'s.  The circuit
is useful as a level shifter, $V_{GS}$ multiplier or
as a low $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m}$ load, not as a
high gain voltage amplifier.

answers.question: Find Rout in Figure 14.

answer.text:
With the usual small signal picture put a
${\cal V}_{x}$ on the drain of ${\rm M}_{1}$ and
evaluate ${\cal I}_{x}$ , Fig.1.

$${\rm M}_{2}:~~v_{sg2}=0\qquad 
r_{2}=r_{o2}\tag{*}$$
to first order to ${\rm ac}$ ground.
Put $r_{1}=r_{o1}$ and for the moment $g_{mb}=0$.
For ${\rm M}_{1}$

$$v_{sg1}=v_{X}\tag{1}$$

$${\cal I}_{x}=g_{m1}v_{sg1}+{{v_{sd1}}\over {r_{1}}}
      =g_{m1}v_{X}+{{v_{X}-{\cal V}_{x}}\over {r_{1}}}\tag{2}$$

with the sign ${\cal I}_{x}$ into the drain, {\it i. e.}
out of the source of ${\rm M}_{1}$.
KCL at the cascode node $X$

$${{v_{X}}\over {r_{2}}}+{\cal I}_{x}=0\tag{3}$$

in $(*)$.
From (2)-(3)

$${\cal I}_{x}\left[1+{{r_{2}}\over {r_{1}}}+g_{m1}r_{2}\right]
      =-{{{\cal V}_{x}}\over {r_{1}}}$$

with the conventional positive current into the
circuit, ${\cal I}_{o}=-{\cal I}_{x}$,

$${\cal R}_{o}={{\cal V}_{x}\over {{\cal I}_{o}}}
      =r_{1}+r_{2}+g_{m1}r_{1}r_{2}
      =r_{1}+\left(1+g_{m1}r_{1}\right)r_{2}\tag{4}$$

For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$${\cal R}_{o}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\tag{5}$$

the $r_{o2}$ of the simple ${\rm M}_{2}$ current source
multiplied by the intrinsic gain $g_{m1}r_{o1}$ of the
cascode device.  For $r_{o1}=r_{o2}=r_{o}$

$${\cal R}_{o}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\tag{6}$$

In a normal $n$ well process the $n$ well of the
cascode ${\rm M}_{1}$ is on ${\rm V}_{DD}$ so that the
source - bulk voltage modulates $V_{T}$,

$$g_{m1}\rightarrow g_{m1}+g_{mb1}=g_{m1}(1+\eta ) \tag{7}$$

and, with the bulk effect,

$${\cal R}_{o}=r_{1}+\left[1+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{1}\right]r_{2}
      \approx \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{1}r_{2} \tag{8}$$

For the connexion as drawn, well of ${\rm M}_{1}$ on
$X$, well of ${\rm M}_{2}$ on ${\rm V}_{DD}$,
$g_{mb1}=g_{mb2}=0$ and (4)-(5) apply.  In compact
form (8) is normally quoted, with $g_{mb1}=0$ if the
well is strapped to the source.

> {\it Remark:}  With $r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$,
> $g_{m}=\sqrt{2\mu _{p}C_{ox}(W/L)I_{D}}$,
> ${\cal R}_{o}\propto 1/\lambda ^{2}I_{D}^{3/2}$,
> nominally $\sim 10^{5}-10^{6}{\rm \Omega }$.

answers.question: How do we ensure that M2 is in saturation in Figure 14?

answer.text:
With the normal sign convention ${\rm  p}~V_{T}<0$
$|V_{T}|=-V_{T}$ for the ${\rm p}$ channel

$${\rm sat.}\;\;V_{SG}>|V_{T}|\;\;{\rm and}\;\;
V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{T}=V_{SG}-|V_{T}|=V_{ov}\tag{*}$$

i. e. for the ${\rm n}$ channel $V_{D}\ge V_{G}-V_{Tn}$
for the ${\rm p}$ channel

$$V_{D}\le V_{G}-V_{Tp}=V_{G}+|V_{Tp}| \tag{**}$$

For $M_{2}$

$$S_{2}=V_{DD}\qquad D_{2}=V_{X}\qquad G_{2}=V_{b2}$$

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{b2}>|V_{Tp}| \cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp}|=V_{ov2}} \tag{1}$$

i. e. from {\rm (**)} 

$$V_{X}\le V_{b2}-V_{Tp}=V_{b2}+|V_{Tp}|\tag{2}$$

at least $V_{ov2}$ below $V_{DD}$.
In normal operation $M_{1}$ is also saturated so that,
with $S_{1}=V_{X}$,

$$V_{X}=V_{S1}=V_{G1}+V_{SG1}=V_{b1}+V_{SG1}
      =V_{b1}+|V_{Tp}|+V_{ov1}\tag{3}$$

apart from the body effect, $V_{T1}=V_{T0}$ in the
figure because the $n$ well of $M_{1}$ is strapped to
$X$, and (2) becomes

$$V_{b1}+|V_{Tp}|+V_{ov1}\le V_{b2}+|V_{Tp}|$$

$$\;V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}\;\tag{4}$$

and of course

$$V_{b2}\le V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-V_{ov2}\tag{5}$$

to keep $M_{2}$ on.  In words: $V_{b2}$ must be low
enough to turn $M_{2}$ on, Eq.5, but high enough, at
least one $p$ overdrive above $V_{b1}$, Eq.4, that the
source of $M_{1}$, Eq.3, does not pull the drain of
$M_{2}$ so high that $(*)$ is violated.  E. {\rm g.}
with $V_{ov}\approx 0.2{\rm V}$

$$V_{b2}\approx V_{b1}+0.2{\rm V}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-0.2{\rm V}$$

so that

$$V_{X}=V_{DD}-V_{ov2}\le V_{b2}+|V_{Tp}|$$

and $M_{2}$ is at the edge of saturation,
$V_{SD2}=V_{ov2}$.

In particular $V_{b1}=V_{b2}$ puts $M_{2}$ in the
triode, $V_{X}=V_{b2}+|V_{Tp}|+V_{ov1}>V_{b2}+|V_{Tp}|$.
The conventional way to generate (4)-(5) with minimum
head room, the wide swing cascode, is to generate
$V_{b1}=V_{GS}|_{I_{REF}}$ from a diode connected
${\rm p}$ carrying $I_{REF}$ and

$$V_{b2}=V_{b1}+V_{ov1}\approx V_{b1}+|V_{GS}-V_{T}|$$

e. {\rm g.} from a second diode of $(W/L)_{b2}=
{1\over 4}(W/L)_{1}$ carrying the same $I_{REF}$,
or from a $V_{GS}$ diode in series with a $V_{ov}$
source follower, so that nominally

$$V_{X}=V_{DD}-|V_{ov2}|\qquad 
V_{DSAT2}=|V_{ov2}|\qquad 
V_{DSAT1}=|V_{ov1}|$$

For the conventional, non wide swing, stack

$$V_{b1}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-V_{ov}\qquad 
  V_{b2}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-2V_{ov}-|V_{Tp}|$$

etc.  Any bias that satisfies (2), normally (4)-(5),
will do, with $\sim 50-100\,{\rm mV}$ of margin over
process.

With (2) satisfied the impedance looking into the
drain of $M_{1}$ is

$$R_{out}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;
  V_{o}\le V_{b1}+|V_{Tp}|\;\;{\rm and}\;\;
  V_{o}\le V_{b2}+|V_{Tp}|-V_{ov1}$$

i. e. $M_{1}$ saturated,

$$V_{SD1}=V_{X}-V_{o}\ge V_{ov1}\;\;,\;\;
  V_{o}\le V_{b1}+|V_{Tp}|$$

is normally the more restrictive condition.  For the
simple cascode $V_{o,min}\approx |V_{Tp}|+2|V_{ov}|$,
for the wide swing bias $V_{o,min}\approx 2|V_{ov}|$.
Any $V_{o}$ higher than that pulls $V_{X}=V_{o}+V_{SD1}$
up and drives $M_{2}$ triode via (2).

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 15.

answer.text:
This is the telescopic $n-$ channel
cascode $CS$ stage. $M_{1}$ is the $CS$ device,
$M_{2}$ the $CG$ cascode device, $I_{1}$ the
{\it a.c.} load. $V_{b1}$ is {\it a.c.} ground.

$$V_{GS1}=v_{in}\;\;,\;\;V_{GS2}=V_{b1}-V_{X}\;\;,\;\;
V_{DS1}=V_{X}\;\;,\;\;V_{DS2}=V_{out}-V_{X}$$

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{1}= {\frac12}\mu _{n}C_{ox}
{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1,2}V_{ov1,2}^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)$$

in saturation

$$g_{m}={\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}V_{ov}}={2I_{D}\over V_{ov}}
\qquad r_{o}={1\over \lambda I_{D}}={1\over g_{ds}}$$

$$g_{mb}=\chi g_{m}\;\;,\;\;\chi ={g_{mb}\over g_{m}}\approx 0.1-0.3$$

For the $n$MOS in $p$ substrate normally
$g_{mb2}\ne 0$ if the bulk is to $GND$.
In the drawing the bulk of $M_{2}$ is to its
source so that $g_{mb2}=0$ in the drawing.
Put $g_{mb2}=0$ for that case.  In general keep
$g_{m2}^{\prime}=g_{m2}+g_{mb2}$.

> {\it D.C. head room}

$$\eqalign{
V_{X}&=V_{b1}-V_{GS2}=V_{b1}-V_{T}-V_{ov2}\cr
V_{DS1}&=V_{X}\ge V_{ov1}\;\;{\rm for}\;M_{1}\;{\rm sat}\cr
V_{DS2}&=V_{out}-V_{X}\ge V_{ov2}\;\;{\rm for}\;M_{2}\;{\rm sat}}$$

$$\eqalign{
V_{b1}&\ge V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}+V_{T2}\cr
V_{out,min}&=V_{X}+V_{ov2}=V_{b1}-V_{T2}\cr
& =V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}\;\;{\rm for\;minimum}\;V_{b1}\cr
V_{out,max}&=V_{DD}-V_{ov,I1}}$$

With the ideal $I_{1}$, $r_{oI}=\infty $, the
d.c. value of $V_{out}$ is indeterminate in
open loop, it is fixed by the external load
or feedback.  With a $p$MOS mirror load
$r_{oI}=r_{o3}=1/\lambda _{p}I_{1}$.

Small signal $V_{b1}=0$, $V_{DD}=0$ for {\it a.c.}

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}\;\;,\;\;v_{gs2}=-v_{x}\;\;,\;\;
v_{bs2}=-v_{x}\;\;{\rm bulk\;to\;GND}\;\;0\;{\rm bulk\;to\;source}$$
$$v_{ds1}=v_{x}\;\;,\;\;v_{ds2}=v_{out}-v_{x}$$

Hybrid $\pi $ at $X$ and at $v_{out}$,
Fig.1, $g_{dsI}=1/r_{oI}$,

$$\eqalign{
{\rm KCL}_{X}:&\;\;g_{m1}v_{in}+g_{ds1}v_{x}
 =g_{m2}^{\prime}(-v_{x})+g_{ds2}(v_{out}-v_{x})\;\;{\rm with\;signs}\cr
{\rm KCL}_{out}:&\;\;g_{m2}^{\prime}(-v_{x})+g_{ds2}(v_{out}-v_{x})
 +g_{dsI}v_{out}=0}$$

More systematically, impedance looking into the
drain of a $CG$ device whose source sees $R_{S}$
to ground is

$$R_{o,CG}=r_{o2}+\left[1+g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o2}\right]R_{S}$$

Here $R_{S}=r_{o1}$ is the impedance looking into
the drain of $M_{1}$ with $v_{in}=0$.

Hence with $g_{m2}^{\prime}=g_{m2}+g_{mb2}$

$$R_{o,cas}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o1}r_{o2}
      =r_{o2}+\left(1+g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o2}\right)r_{o1}
      \approx g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o1}r_{o2}\tag{1}$$

for $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$.  With bulk to source
$g_{m2}^{\prime}=g_{m2}$,

$$R_{o,cas}\approx g_{m2}r_{o1}r_{o2}$$

i. e. the $r_{o1}$ of the $CS$ device is multiplied
by the intrinsic gain $g_{m2}r_{o2}$ of the cascode
device.  Compared to the simple $CS$ stage
$R_{o}=r_{o1}$ the increase is $\approx g_{m}r_{o}$,
$20-40\,{\rm dB}$.

With finite load $r_{oI}$

$$R_{out}=R_{o,cas}\parallel r_{oI}
      ={1\over g_{dsI}+{g_{ds1}g_{ds2}\over g_{m2}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}}
      \approx R_{o,cas}\parallel r_{oI}\tag{2}$$

For the ideal source $r_{oI}\to \infty $,
$R_{out}=R_{o,cas}$.

The short circuit output current is the drain
current of $M_{1}$,

$$i_{sc}=g_{m1}v_{in}\;{1\over 1+{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\over g_{m2}^{\prime}}}
      \approx g_{m1}v_{in}$$

so that the low frequency voltage gain is

$$A_{v}={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=-G_{m}R_{out}\tag{3}$$

$$A_{v}\approx -g_{m1}R_{out}
      =-g_{m1}\left[r_{o1}+r_{o2}+g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o1}r_{o2}\right]
        \parallel r_{oI}$$

Ideal load:

$$A_{v0}\approx -g_{m1}g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o1}r_{o2}
      =-g_{m1}r_{o1}\times g_{m2}^{\prime}r_{o2}\tag{4}$$

$$|A_{v0}|\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}g_{m2}r_{o2}\;\;{\rm no\;body\;effect}$$

i. e. the gain of the $CS$ stage $g_{m1}r_{o1}$
multiplied by the intrinsic gain of the cascode
device.  E.G. $g_{m}=1\,{\rm mA/V}$,
$r_{o}=10\,{\rm k\Omega }$, $g_{m}r_{o}=10$,
$R_{o,cas}\approx 1\,{\rm M\Omega }$,
$|A_{v0}|\approx 10^{4}\approx 80\,{\rm dB}$.
With a $p$MOS load $r_{o3}\approx r_{o1}$,
$R_{out}\approx r_{o3}\parallel R_{o,cas}\approx r_{o3}$,
$|A_{v}|\approx g_{m1}r_{o3}\approx 10$, the cascode
is normally used with a cascode $p$MOS load to
retain the high $R_{out}$.

In two stage form: impedance at $X$

$$R_{X}=r_{o1}\parallel R_{in2}\;\;,\;\;
R_{in2}\approx {1+r_{o2}g_{dsI}\over g_{m2}^{\prime}}\approx
{1\over g_{m2}^{\prime}}$$

$$A_{v1}={v_{x}\over v_{in}}=-g_{m1}R_{X}\approx -{g_{m1}\over g_{m2}^{\prime}}
      \approx -1$$

$$A_{v2}={v_{out}\over v_{x}}\approx g_{m2}^{\prime}R_{out}$$

$$A_{v}=A_{v1}A_{v2}\approx -g_{m1}R_{out}$$

The Miller multiplication of $C_{gd1}$ is

$$C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}\left(1-A_{v1}\right)
      \approx C_{gs1}+2C_{gd1}$$

instead of $C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1+g_{m1}r_{o1})$ for the
simple $CS$ stage.  The input pole is pushed out.

Input impedance $Z_{in}=1/sC_{in}\to \infty $ at
d.c.

Output impedance is (1)-(2), inductive at high
frequency.

Frequency response: two poles, dominant at the
high impedance output node, non dominant at the
low impedance cascode node $X$.

$$C_{L}=C_{db2}+C_{gd2}+C_{dbI}+C_{ext}\;\;{\rm at}\;v_{out}$$
$$C_{X}=C_{db1}+C_{gd1}+C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}+C_{gs2ov}\;\;{\rm at}\;X$$

$$\omega _{p1}={1\over R_{out}C_{L}}\;\;{\rm dominant}\tag{5}$$
$$\omega _{p2}\approx {g_{m2}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\over C_{X}}
      \approx {g_{m2}^{\prime}\over C_{X}}\;\;{\rm non\;dominant}\tag{6}$$
$$\omega _{z}\approx {g_{m1}\over C_{gd1}}\;\;{\rm RHP\;zero\;if\;}C_{gd1}{\rm \;kept}$$

Normally $\omega _{p2}\gg \omega _{p1}$ because
$R_{X}\approx 1/g_{m2}$ is low.  The $-3\,{\rm dB}$
bandwidth is $\omega _{-3dB}\approx \omega _{p1}$,
the gain bandwidth product

$${\rm GBW}=|A_{v0}|\omega _{p1}\approx {g_{m1}\over C_{L}}
      =\omega _{u}\tag{7}$$

and $\omega _{p2}>\omega _{u}$ is required for

normally referred to simply as {\it the} cascode.

answers.question: Explain why the Miller effect is less pronounced in a cascode.

answer.text:
In a $CE/CS$ stage the feedback capacitance
$C_{m}=C_{\mu}=C_{gd}=C_{bc}$ is connected
between two nodes with large anti-phase voltage
swing and is Miller multiplied.

By Miller's theorem an impedance $Z$ connected
between input and output of an amplifier of
voltage gain $K=V_{o}/V_{i}$ can be replaced by

$$Z_{i}= \frac{Z}{1-K} \qquad Z_{o}= \frac{Z}{1-1/K}$$

at input and output. For a capacitance:

$$C_{M,i}= C_{m}(1-K) \qquad C_{M,o}= C_{m}(1-1/K)$$

For an inverting amplifier $K=-|A_{v}|<0$:

$$C_{M,i}= C_{m}(1+|A_{v}|) \approx |A_{v}|C_{m}$$

### 1. Common Emitter/Source alone

$$K_{1}= -g_{m}R_{L}' = -g_{m}(R_{D}||R_{L}||r_{o}) \approx -50 {\rm \;to\;} -500$$

$$C_{in}= C_{gs}+C_{gd}(1+ g_{m}R_{L}')$$
$$C_{out}\approx C_{gd}$$

$$f_{H,i}= \frac{1}{2\pi R_{sig} C_{in}}$$

is very low. The input pole becomes dominant and the
bandwidth is $1/|A_{v}|$ times smaller. Physically a
small $v_{i}$ produces a large $-v_{o}$ so a large
displacement current $C_{m}d(v_{i}-v_{o})/dt \approx
C_{m}(1+|A_{v}|)dv_{i}/dt$ must be supplied by the source.

### 2. Cascode: $CS-CG$ / $CE-CB$

```
Vin --+-- G1 D1 -- S2 D2 --+-- Vout
      S1                  G2=AC gnd
      |                   B2=AC gnd
     gnd                  gnd
 Q1: CS/CE  Q2: CG/CB
```

The cascode is two stages in series with overall gain
still large:

$$A_{v}= A_{v1}\cdot A_{v2}$$

* **Stage 1 - the input $CS/CE$ device:** Its load is
not $R_{D}$ but the input impedance looking into the
source/emitter of the $CG/CB$ device.

$$R_{in2} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}} || r_{o2} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}$$

typically $50-500\,\Omega$.

Hence

$$A_{v1}= \frac{v_{d1}}{v_{i}} = -g_{m1}(r_{o1}||R_{in2}) \approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}} \approx -1$$

if $I_{D1}=I_{D2}$.

Miller multiplication for $C_{gd1}/C_{\mu1}$ is then:

$$C_{M1,i}= C_{gd1}(1-A_{v1}) \approx C_{gd1}(1+1)=2C_{gd1}$$

instead of $C_{gd1}(1+g_{m}R_{L}')\approx 100\,C_{gd1}$.

Physically the drain of $Q1$ is pinned by the low
impedance source of $Q2$. $v_{d1}$ hardly moves, so
$v_{i}-v_{d1}\approx v_{i}$ and little current is fed
back through $C_{gd1}$. The Miller feedback is
degenerated.

$$C_{in,cascode}\approx C_{gs1}+2C_{gd1} \ll C_{gs1}+g_{m}R_{L}'C_{gd1}$$

The input pole $f_{p1}=1/2\pi R_{sig}C_{in}$ is pushed
up by $\approx g_{m}R_{L}'/2$.

* **Stage 2 - the $CG/CB$ device:** It has no Miller
effect at all. Its feedback capacitance $C_{gd2}/C_{\mu2}$
is connected between drain/collector = output and
gate/base = AC ground, not between input and output.

$$C_{gd2} {\rm \;is\; from\; output\; to\; ground}$$

Its input capacitance is $C_{gs2}/C_{\pi2}$ from source/emitter
to ground. The stage is non-inverting, $A_{v2}\approx +g_{m2}R_{L}'$,
so $1-K$ does not give multiplication between its input
and output.

The only capacitance between input and output of the
whole cascode is $C_{gd1}$ already accounted for with
$A_{v1}\approx -1$, and the feedthrough $C_{gd2}$ from
output to the intermediate node $D1/S2$, which creates a
pole at the intermediate node:

$$f_{p,int}\approx \frac{g_{m2}}{2\pi(C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}+C_{gd1}+C_{db1})}$$

which is very high because the resistance there is $\approx 1/g_{m2}$.

Overall:

$$A_{v,tot}=A_{v1}A_{v2}\approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}}\cdot g_{m2}R_{out}\approx -g_{m1}R_{out}$$

$$R_{out}\approx g_{m2}r_{o2}r_{o1}$$

We get the same or larger DC gain as a single $CS/CE$
with $R_{out}$, but with input Miller capacitance reduced
by a factor $\approx |A_{v}|/2$.

In words: The $CG/CB$ transistor *cascoes* - shields -
the input device from the large output swing, holding its
drain/collector at near constant voltage and providing
current gain but $\approx$ unity voltage gain to the first
stage. Without large anti-phase voltage across $C_{gd}/C_{\mu}$ there is no Miller multiplication. This unilateralization greatly extends bandwidth, improves reverse isolation and stability, which is why the cascode is the standard wideband/high gain stage.

It correctly notes Cgd2 connects output to AC ground and does not experience Miller effect. from drain to source. KCL at $o$ : current leaving

If $r_{o1}=r_{o2}=r_{o}$ , $A_{v0}\approx g_{m}r_{o}/2$.
Typ. $20-40{\rm dB}$.

It is a current buffer: short circuit current gain
$\approx 1$.

KCL at $x$ : external current $i_{x}$ injected into $S$.
Current through $R_{sig}$ plus $i_{d2}=0$ with sign
$i_{d2}$ from $D$ to $S$ enters $S$.

For $R_{sig}=0$, $v_{x}=v_{sig}=v_{i}$ and with (1)

From (1)

$$\approx {1\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}\;\;{\rm for}\;r_{o1}\ll r_{o2}$$

answer.text:

neglected the small signal circuit is the two node circuit
in Fig.6.12 of R. The three capacities that go to the
{\rm a.c.} earth at the output

$${{C}_{o}}={{C}_{DB}}+{{C}_{DB2}}+{{C}_{GD2}}\tag{1}$$

are in parallel and the circuit is the conventional

> {\it Fig.1 :} Put ${{R}_{o}}={{r}_{o1}}\parallel {{r}_{o2}}$,
> ${{C}_{o}}$ as in (1) and ${{C}_{i}}={{C}_{GS}}$.  In the
> ${\cal O}\left( {{R}_{o}}^{-1}\right)=0$ approximation

$${{V}_{o}}=-{{g}_{m}}{{V}_{g}}+s{{C}_{GD}}\left( {{V}_{g}}-{{V}_{o}}

\right) \tag{3}$$

so that, e. {\rm g.} with ${{R}_{o}}<\infty $ reinstated,

$${{V}_{o}}\left[1+s{{R}_{o}}\left( {{C}_{o}}+{{C}_{GD}}\right) \right]
+{{V}_{g}}\left[{{g}_{m}}{{R}_{o}}-s{{R}_{o}}{{C}_{GD}}\right]=0\tag{4}$$

$${{V}_{g}}\left[1+s{{R}_{S}}\left( {{C}_{GS}}+{{C}_{GD}}\right) \right]
-s{{R}_{S}}{{C}_{GD}}{{V}_{o}}={{V}_{i}} \tag{5}$$

and

$${{V}_{o}\over {{V}_{i}}}=-{{g}_{m}}{{R}_{o}}
{{1-s{{C}_{GD}}/{{g}_{m}}}\over {D\left( s\right)}}\tag{6}$$

$$\eqalign{
D\left( s\right) =1&+s\left[ {{R}_{S}}\left( {{C}_{GS}}+{{C}_{GD}}
\right)+{{R}_{o}}\left( {{C}_{o}}+{{C}_{GD}}\right)
+{{g}_{m}}{{R}_{o}}{{R}_{S}}{{C}_{GD}}\right]  \cr
&+{{s}^{2}}{{R}_{S}}{{R}_{o}}\left[ {{C}_{GS}}{{C}_{o}}
+{{C}_{GS}}{{C}_{GD}}+{{C}_{o}}{{C}_{GD}}\right] \cr
&=1+s\left[ {{R}_{S}}{{C}_{in}}+{{R}_{o}}{{C}_{o}}^{\prime}\right]
+{{s}^{2}}{{R}_{S}}{{R}_{o}}\left[ {{C}_{in}}{{C}_{o}}^{\prime}
-{{C}_{GD}}^{2}\right] \tag{7}}$$

with

$${{C}_{in}}={{C}_{GS}}+{{C}_{GD}}\qquad 
{{C}_{o}}^{\prime}={{C}_{o}}+{{C}_{GD}}\tag{8}$$

in the conventional form

$$D\left( s\right)=\left( 1+{s\over {{\omega }_{p1}}}\right)
\left( 1+{s\over {{\omega }_{p2}}}\right)\tag{9}$$

and the {\it feed forward} zero

$${{\omega }_{z}}={{g}_{m}\over {{C}_{GD}}}\tag{10}$$

on the positive real axis.  $D\left( s\right)$ is second order.
Lumping (1) there are two ${\rm a.c.}$ nodes in the circuit,
the ${\rm a.c.}$ coupled gate node of ${{M}_{1}}$ and the
common drain node ${{V}_{o}}$, and two finite poles,
normally written in the Miller approximation ${{g}_{m}}{{R}_{o}}\gg 1$,
${{R}_{o}}{{C}_{o}}\gg {{R}_{S}}{{C}_{GS}}$ as the Miller
multiplied input pole and the output pole,

$${{\omega }_{p1}}\approx {1\over {{{R}_{o}}{{C}_{o}}^{\prime}}}
\approx {1\over {{{R}_{o}}\left( {{C}_{DB}}+{{C}_{DB2}}+{{C}_{GD2}}
+{{C}_{GD}}\right)}}\tag{11}$$

$${{\omega }_{p2}}\approx {1\over {{{R}_{S}}{{C}_{in,M}}}}\qquad

\tag{12}$$

With ${{R}_{S}}\to 0$, ${{\omega }_{p2}}\to \infty $ and the
circuit is normally quoted as a {\it one pole} circuit in the
band of interest.  Counting the RHP zero (10) as a
singularity the circuit is normally loosely referred to as a

often quoted as a three pole plus one zero circuit, the two
drain poles coinciding at ${{\omega }_{p1}}$.

In particular with ${{R}_{S}}$ small

$${{V}_{o}\over {{V}_{i}}}\approx -{{g}_{m}}{{R}_{o}}
{{1-s/{{\omega }_{z}}}\over {\left( 1+s/{{\omega }_{p1}}\right)
\left( 1+s/{{\omega }_{p2}}\right)}}\tag{13}$$

so that for $\left| s\right|<{{\omega }_{p2}},{{\omega }_{z}}$

$${{V}_{o}\over {{V}_{i}}}\approx -{{{A}_{0}}\over {1+s/{{\omega }_{p1}}}}
\qquad {{A}_{0}}={{g}_{m}}{{R}_{o}}\tag{14}$$

the conventional dominant pole approximation.  Any of the

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in Figure 19.

answer.text:
This is the {\it self cascode} or {\it composite}
$n$MOS. $W_{1}/L_{1}=W_{2}/L_{2}=W/L$ for
simplicity. Put

$$k_{i}= \mu _{n}C_{ox}W_{i}/L_{i}\qquad 
k_{i}^{\prime}=k_{i}/2\tag{1}$$

$$I_{D1}=k_{1}\left[(V_{GS1}-V_{T1})V_{DS1}-V_{DS1}^{2}/2\right]
\;\;{\rm triode}\tag{2a}$$
$$I_{D1}=k_{1}^{\prime}(V_{GS1}-V_{T1})^{2}(1+\lambda _{1}V_{DS1})
\;\;{\rm sat}\tag{2b}$$
$$I_{D2}=k_{2}\left[(V_{GS2}-V_{T2})V_{DS2}-V_{DS2}^{2}/2\right]
\tag{3a}$$
$$I_{D2}=k_{2}^{\prime}(V_{GS2}-V_{T2})^{2}(1+\lambda _{2}V_{DS2})
\tag{3b}$$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}\;\;V_{DS1}=V_{x}\tag{4}$$
$$V_{GS2}=V_{in}-V_{x}\;\;V_{DS2}=V_{out}-V_{x}\;\;
V_{BS2}=-V_{x}\tag{5}$$
$$V_{T2}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{x}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]=V_{T1}+\Delta V_{T}(V_{x})\tag{6}$$
$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}\tag{7}$$

$V_{T2}\ge V_{T1}$.

{\it Saturation conditions}

$$M_{1}{\rm sat}:V_{x}\ge V_{in}-V_{T1}\tag{8a}$$
$$M_{2}{\rm sat}:V_{out}-V_{x}\ge V_{in}-V_{x}-V_{T2}\iff
V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{T2}\tag{8b}$$

If $M_{1}$ sat $I_{D}=k_{1}^{\prime}(V_{in}-V_{T1})^{2}$,
if $M_{2}$ sat $I_{D}=k_{2}^{\prime}(V_{in}-V_{x}-V_{T2})^{2}$.
$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$ with both sat gives

$$V_{x}=V_{in}-V_{T2}-\sqrt{k_{1}/k_{2}}\,(V_{in}-V_{T1})<V_{in}-V_{T1}$$

for any $k_{1},k_{2}>0$ and $V_{T2}\ge V_{T1}$.
Hence $M_{1}$ sat $+$ $M_{2}$ sat is impossible.
$M_{1}$ sat $+$ $M_{2}$ triode requires

$$V_{x}\ge V_{in}-V_{T1}\;\;{\rm and}\;\;V_{out}<V_{in}-V_{T2}$$

so $V_{out}-V_{x}<V_{T1}-V_{T2}\le 0$, impossible for
$V_{out}>V_{x}$.  Hence for $I_{D}>0$

> $M_{1}$ is {\it always} in the triode, $M_{2}$ is triode
> for $V_{out}<V_{in}-V_{T2}$ and saturated for
> $V_{out}>V_{in}-V_{T2}$.

The composite is off for $V_{in}<V_{T1}$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}$,
triode for small $V_{out}$ and ``saturated'' for

$$V_{out}\ge V_{DS,sat}^{({\rm comp})}\approx V_{in}-V_{T2}\tag{9}$$

just as a single $n$MOS.

In the ``saturation'' region $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ sat,
$\lambda =0$, $V_{T1}=V_{T2}=V_{T}$ for illustration:

$$k_{1}\left[aV_{x}-V_{x}^{2}/2\right]=k_{2}^{\prime}(a-V_{x})^{2}
\tag{10}$$

$a=V_{in}-V_{T}$.  I. e.

$$(k_{1}+k_{2})V_{x}^{2}-2a(k_{1}+k_{2})V_{x}+k_{2}a^{2}=0$$

$$V_{x}=a\left[1-\sqrt{\frac{k_{1}}{k_{1}+k_{2}}}\right]
\tag{11}$$

$$I_{D}=k_{2}^{\prime}(a-V_{x})^{2}
      =\frac12\frac{k_{1}k_{2}}{k_{1}+k_{2}}a^{2}\tag{12}$$

$$I_{D}= \frac12 k_{eff}(V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}\tag{13}$$

with

$$\frac1{k_{eff}}=\frac1{k_{1}}+\frac1{k_{2}}\tag{14}$$

$$\frac1{(W/L)_{eff}}=\frac1{(W/L)_{1}}+\frac1{(W/L)_{2}}\tag{15}$$

In particular for $(W/L)_{1}=(W/L)_{2}=W/L$

$$k_{eff}=k/2\tag{16}$$
$$(W/L)_{eff}=(W/L)/2\tag{17}$$
$$L_{eff}=L_{1}+L_{2}\tag{18}$$

$$V_{x}=a\left(1-1/\sqrt{2}\right)\approx 0.29\,a\tag{19}$$
$$I_{D}= \frac{k}{4}a^{2}= \frac12 I_{D1,{\rm single}}\tag{20}$$

With body effect $V_{T2}(V_{x})>V_{T1}$ Eq.10 becomes

$$k_{1}\left[(V_{in}-V_{T1})V_{x}-V_{x}^{2}/2\right]
 =\frac{k_{2}}2\left[V_{in}-V_{x}-V_{T2}(V_{x})\right]^{2}\tag{21}$$

solved iteratively.  $V_{x}$ is slightly smaller and
$I_{D}$ slightly smaller than (12).  To first order the
composite can still be written as (13) with a slightly
larger effective $V_{T,eff}\approx V_{T1}+ \Delta V_{T}/2$
and $k_{eff}$ given by (14).  If the $n$-well is available
and the body of $M_{2}$ is tied to $V_{x}$, $V_{T2}=V_{T1}$
and (12)-(18) are exact in the square law.

Including $\lambda $,

$$I_{D}\approx \frac12 k_{eff}(V_{in}-V_{T,eff})^{2}
\left[1+\lambda _{eff}V_{out}\right]\tag{22}$$

with, from small signal,

$$g_{ds,eff}= \lambda _{eff}I_{D}= \frac{g_{ds1}g_{ds2}}
{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\approx
g_{ds2}\frac{g_{ds1}}{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}}\tag{23}$$

For $M_{1}$ triode

$$g_{m1}=k_{1}V_{x}\tag{24a}$$
$$g_{ds1}=k_{1}(a-V_{x})\tag{24b}$$
$$g_{m2}=k_{2}(a-V_{x})\tag{24c}$$
$$g_{ds2}= \lambda _{2}I_{D}\tag{24d}$$

so that

$$g_{ds,eff}=g_{ds2}\frac{k_{1}}{k_{1}+k_{2}}
      =\lambda _{2}I_{D}\frac{k_{1}}{k_{1}+k_{2}}\tag{25}$$

$$\lambda _{eff}= \lambda _{2}\frac{k_{1}}{k_{1}+k_{2}}\tag{26}$$

For $k_{1}=k_{2}$, $\lambda _{eff}= \lambda /2$,
$g_{ds,eff}=g_{ds2}/2$.  I. e. the Early voltage is
doubled, the output resistance is doubled for the same
current.

Small signal with $v_{in}$ at the common gate, $v_{x}$ at
the intermediate node:

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{in}+g_{ds1}v_{x}\tag{27}$$
$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}(v_{in}-v_{x})+g_{mb2}(-v_{x})+g_{ds2}(v_{out}-v_{x})\tag{28}$$
$$i_{d1}=i_{d2}\tag{29}$$

$$v_{x}= \frac{(g_{m2}-g_{m1})v_{in}+g_{ds2}v_{out}}
{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\tag{30}$$

$$i_{out}=i_{d2}=G_{m}v_{in}+g_{ds,eff}v_{out}\tag{31}$$

$$G_{m}= \frac{g_{m2}g_{ds1}+g_{m1}(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2})}
{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}
\approx \frac{g_{m2}g_{ds1}+g_{m1}g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}}\tag{32}$$

$$g_{ds,eff}= \frac{g_{ds1}g_{ds2}}
{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\tag{33}$$
$$R_{out}^{({\rm comp})}=1/g_{ds,eff}
 =\frac{g_{ds1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}{g_{ds1}g_{ds2}}
 \approx \frac{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}{g_{ds1}g_{ds2}}\tag{34}$$

With (24),

$$G_{m}= \frac{k_{1}k_{2}}{k_{1}+k_{2}}a =k_{eff}a\tag{35}$$

$$g_{m,eff}=k_{eff}(V_{in}-V_{T})\tag{36}$$

exactly the $g_{m}$ of a single transistor with
$(W/L)_{eff}$.  For $k_{1}=k_{2}=k$,

$$G_{m}=ka/2 = g_{m,{\rm single}}/2\tag{37}$$
$$R_{out}=2/g_{ds2}=2r_{o2}\tag{38}$$

$$r_{o2}=1/\lambda I_{D}\tag{39}$$

so that for the same $V_{in}$

$$R_{out}^{({\rm comp})}=4\,r_{o,{\rm single}}(I_{D,{\rm single}})
      =2\,r_{o2}\tag{40}$$

$$G_{m}R_{out}= \frac{2}{\lambda _{eff}a}
            =\frac{4}{\lambda a}=2\,g_{m}r_{o}|_{\rm single}\tag{41}$$

The intrinsic gain is doubled, as for a transistor of
length $L_{1}+L_{2}$.

With the drain resistor $R_{D}$ the low frequency voltage
gain in saturation is

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}}=-G_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel R_{out}\right)
      \approx -G_{m}R_{D}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{D}\ll R_{out}\tag{42}$$

$$A_{v}\approx -k_{eff}(V_{in}-V_{T})R_{D}
      =-\sqrt{2k_{eff}I_{D}}\,R_{D}\tag{43}$$

For $k_{1}=k_{2}$,

$$A_{v}\approx -\frac{k}{2}(V_{in}-V_{T})R_{D}
          =\frac12 A_{v,{\rm single}}\tag{44}$$

if $R_{D}$ dominates.  If the load is a current source,
$A_{v0}=-G_{m}R_{out}$ is twice that of the short device,
i. e. the long channel intrinsic gain.

In the triode region $V_{out}<V_{in}-V_{T2}$ both devices
are triode and

$$I_{D}=k_{1}\left[aV_{x}-V_{x}^{2}/2\right]
      =k_{2}\left[(a-V_{x})(V_{out}-V_{x})-(V_{out}-V_{x})^{2}/2\right]\tag{45}$$

which for $k_{1}=k_{2}$ gives the usual triode parabola
with $(W/L)_{eff}$.

Remarks:

* The composite emulates a transistor of $L_{eff}=L_{1}+L_{2}$
  for $W_{1}=W_{2}$.  $N$ devices in series give
  $L_{eff}= \sum L_{i}$, $1/(W/L)_{eff}= \sum 1/(W/L)_{i}$.
  It is used to obtain a long channel output resistance,
  reduced $\lambda $, reduced DIBL, velocity saturation and
  better matching $\sigma_{V_{T}}\propto 1/\sqrt{WL}$ without
  drawing a long device, and to increase $r_{o}$ in
  mirrors and OTAs - the ``self-cascode''.

* $M_{1}$ acts as a degeneration resistor in triode for
  $M_{2}$; the circuit is {\it not} a conventional cascode
  because the gate of $M_{2}$ is not ac ground.  Input
  capacitance is $C_{gs1}+C_{gs2}+C_{gb}$.

* An extra pole at the intermediate node
  $\omega_{x}\approx (g_{ds1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2})/C_{x}$,
  $C_{x}=C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}+C_{gd1}+C_{db1}+C_{db2}$ is
  non-dominant because $g_{m2}$ is large, typically
  $\omega_{x}\gg 1/R_{D}C_{out}$.

* Large signal transfer $V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}(V_{in})R_{D}$:
  $V_{out}=V_{DD}$ for $V_{in}<V_{T}$, then
  $V_{out}=V_{DD}-\tfrac12k_{eff}(V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}R_{D}$
  in saturation, bending over to the triode region when
  $V_{out}$ reaches $V_{in}-V_{T2}$.

With body effect eliminated the square law description is
exact; with body effect the effective $V_{T}$ is slightly
higher and $k_{eff}$ slightly lower, but the $L_{1}+L_{2}$
behaviour is retained to first order.  For short channel
velocity saturated models $I_{D}\propto (V_{GS}-V_{T})$ the
same series combination still gives $I_{D}\propto
(W/L)_{eff}(V_{GS}-V_{T})$ with reduced short channel
effects.

The lower device is described as acting like a triode-region channel extension of the upper device, consistent with the golden solution. The gain, output resistance, and intrinsic gain doubling all support the longer-effective-channel conclusion. The answer avoids misclassifying it as a conventional cascode and explicitly notes this is a 'self-cascode', which is consistent with the golden solution's allowance.

It also correctly analyzes the operating regions, showing M1 is always in triode and M2 can be saturated, and derives the effective transconductance and output resistance.
